title: Sayings and Proverbs - ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଢଗଢମାଳି
subtitle: Sayings, meanings and the sources behind them
scope_note: A growing research repository: 211 explained sayings with traceable contemporary witnesses, historical comparisons and a source survey for expansion. This is not a complete anthology or a certified public-domain corpus. Public access, open licensing and historical attestation are recorded separately.
license: Original Project Odisha commentary and illustrations: CC BY-SA4.0. Wikimedia-derived entries retain their attributed CC BY-SA4.0 terms. Three short SCERT quotations have separate source rights and are not openly licensed or relicensed here. Fonts and other source material retain their own rights.
editorial_note: By Ahimanikya Satapathy · Project Odisha. AI-assisted research and drafting; separate AI review is recorded in the research handoff and is not human or community validation. See README.md for method and limits.

odia: ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଢଗଢମାଳି ଚିହ୍ନା ଚିତ୍ର, ଛନ୍ଦ ଓ ଥଟ୍ଟାରେ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ଜୀବନର କଥାକୁ ମନେ ରହିବା ପରି କହେ। ଲେମ୍ବୁ, ମେଘ ବା ଖାଲି ବଟୁଆର କଥା ଦେଇ କେବେ ପରାମର୍ଶ ଦିଆଯାଏ, କେବେ କାହାକୁ ଚିଡ଼ାଯାଏ, କେବେ ତାଙ୍କ ଆଚରଣ ନେଇ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରାଯାଏ। ଏହି ସଂଗ୍ରହରେ ଛନ୍ଦମୟ କଥନ, ପ୍ରବାଦ ଓ ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥରେ ବ୍ୟବହୃତ ଛୋଟ ଉକ୍ତି ରହିଛି; ସେମାନଙ୍କ ଭିନ୍ନ ରୂପ ଓ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଧ୍ୟାନ ଦିଆଯାଇଛି।
english: Odia dhaga–dhamali give everyday observations a memorable shape through familiar images, rhythm and pointed humour. A lemon, a cloud or an empty pouch can become a way to offer advice, tease someone or question their conduct. This collection brings together rhymed sayings, proverbs and figurative expressions, keeping their different forms and the situations in which they make sense in view.

sections.title_odia: ଦୂରେ ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଭିତରେ ରହିଥିବା ଭାଷା
sections.title_english: The language that stays within us

paragraphs.odia: ମୁଁ ପଞ୍ଚତିରିଶ ବର୍ଷ ହେଲା ଓଡ଼ିଶା ବାହାରେ ରହୁଛି। ତଥାପି ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଭାଷା ଓ ତାହା ସହ ଜଡ଼ିତ ଜୀବନବୋଧ ମୋତେ ଛାଡ଼ି ଯାଇନାହିଁ। ମନେ ରଖିବାକୁ ଅଲଗା ଚେଷ୍ଟା ନ କଲେ ବି ସେହି ଭାଷା ମୋ ଭିତରେ ରହିଛି। ମୋ ପାଇଁ ଢଗଢମାଳି ସେହି ସମ୍ପର୍କର ଏକ ଅଂଶ। ଜାଗା ବଦଳିଛି; କଥାକୁ ବୁଝିବାର କେତେକ ଢଙ୍ଗ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ରହିଯାଇଛି।
paragraphs.english: I have lived outside Odisha for thirty-five years. Yet the language, and the way of life it carries, have never left me. They remain within me even without a deliberate effort to hold on to them. Dhaga–dhamali are part of that connection. The place has changed; some of the ways I understand life have travelled with me.

paragraphs.odia: ଭାଷା କେବଳ ଶବ୍ଦ ଓ ବ୍ୟାକରଣରେ ସୀମିତ ନୁହେଁ। କେଉଁ କଥାରେ ହସ ଲାଗେ, କେବେ ମନ ଦୁଃଖ ହୁଏ, କାହାକୁ କିପରି ବୁଝାଇବା ଓ କେବେ ନିଜକୁ ଅଟକାଇବା—ସେସବୁରେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଭାଷା ରହେ। ଏହି ବହିରେ ମୁଁ ସେହି ଜୀବନ ସହ ଢଗର ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଦେଖିବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁଛି।
paragraphs.english: Language reaches beyond words and grammar. It enters what makes us laugh, what hurts, how we reason with another person and when we check ourselves. This book looks at the connection between a saying and that lived experience.

sections.title_english: Familiar pictures that change how we think

paragraphs.odia: “ଅତି ଲେମ୍ବୁ ଚିପୁଡ଼ିଲେ ପିତା” କହିଲେ ଆଖି ଆଗରେ ଲେମ୍ବୁ ଚିପୁଡ଼ିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଆସେ। ତାହା ସହ ଗୋଟିଏ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆସେ: ଯାହା ଭଲ ଫଳ ଦେଉଛି, ତାକୁ ଆଉ କେତେ ଟାଣିବି? କାହାର ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ପାଇସାରି ପୁଣିପୁଣି ଅଧିକ ମାଗିବା ବେଳେ ଏହି କଥା ଆମକୁ ଅଟକାଇପାରେ। ଲେମ୍ବୁର ଚିତ୍ର ଏଠି ସମ୍ପର୍କରେ କେଉଁଠି ଅଟକିବା ଦରକାର, ତାହା ବୁଝାଏ।
paragraphs.english: “ଅତି ଲେମ୍ବୁ ଚିପୁଡ଼ିଲେ ପିତା” brings the action of squeezing a lemon to mind. It also prompts a question: how far should I press something that is already giving a useful result? After someone has helped us, repeatedly asking for more may call for this reminder. The kitchen image becomes a way to think about proportion in a relationship.

paragraphs.odia: “ଗରଜିଲା ମେଘ ବରଷେ ନାହିଁ” ଶୁଣିଲେ ବଡ଼ କଥା ଓ ପ୍ରକୃତ କାମକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଦେଖିବାକୁ ମନ ଯାଏ। ଏହା ପାଗର ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ। କଥା ଦେଇଥିବା ଲୋକ ଆସଲେ କଣ କଲେ, ସେଥିପ୍ରତି ଧ୍ୟାନ ଦେବାର ଏକ ଢଙ୍ଗ। ଢଗର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଏହି ମୋଡ଼ରେ—ଚିହ୍ନା ଜିନିଷ ଦେଇ ସାମ୍ନାର ପରିସ୍ଥିତିକୁ ଆଉ ଥରେ ଦେଖିବା।
paragraphs.english: “ଗରଜିଲା ମେଘ ବରଷେ ନାହିଁ” turns attention from loud words to what someone actually does. It is not a rule about the weather. The familiar cloud supplies a different angle from which to examine a promise. That turn of thought is one of the pleasures of a Dhaga.

paragraphs.odia: ଏକେ ଢଗ କହିବାର ଢଙ୍ଗ ବଦଳିଲେ ତାହାର ପ୍ରଭାବ ବଦଳେ। ହସି କହିଲେ ହାଲୁକା ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ ହୋଇପାରେ; ରାଗରେ କହିଲେ ତାହା ଆଘାତ ଦେଇପାରେ। କିଏ କାହାକୁ, କେଉଁ ଅବସରରେ କହୁଛି, ସେଥିକୁ ବାଦ ଦେଲେ କେବଳ ଶବ୍ଦର ଅର୍ଥ ରହିଯାଏ। ଓଡ଼ିଆ ଶିଖୁଥିବା ଜଣେ ପାଠକଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଏହି ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗ ବୁଝିବା ମଧ୍ୟ ଭାଷାର ନିକଟତର ହେବା।
paragraphs.english: The same saying can feel different when its tone changes. Said lightly, it may be a teasing reminder; said in anger, it may wound. Who speaks, to whom, and on what occasion belongs to the meaning. For a reader learning Odia, understanding that setting offers a closer encounter with the language people live with.

paragraphs.odia: “କହି ଦେଉଥାଇ ପରକୁ, ବୁଦ୍ଧି ନ ଦିଶଇ ଘରକୁ” ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ଉପଦେଶ ଦେବା ଆଗରୁ ନିଜ ଆଚରଣକୁ ଦେଖିବାର ସୁଯୋଗ ଦିଏ। ଢଗକୁ କେବଳ ଅନ୍ୟର ଭୁଲ ଧରିବା ପାଇଁ ବ୍ୟବହାର କଲେ ଏହି ସୁଯୋଗ ହରାଇଯାଏ। କେବେକେବେ ତାହାର ସବୁଠାରୁ ଭଲ ଶ୍ରୋତା ଆମେ ନିଜେ।
paragraphs.english: “କହି ଦେଉଥାଇ ପରକୁ, ବୁଦ୍ଧି ନ ଦିଶଇ ଘରକୁ” invites us to examine our conduct before advising somebody else. If sayings are used only to catch other people out, that possibility is lost. Sometimes we are their most useful audience.

paragraphs.odia: ଏହି କଥାମାନଙ୍କର ଲିଖିତ ସାକ୍ଷ୍ୟ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅଛି। ୧୮୯୩ ମସିହାର “ଢଗମାଳିକା, ପ୍ରଥମଭାଗ” କଟକର ଭିକ୍ଟୋରିଆ ପ୍ରେସରେ ଛପା ହୋଇଥିଲା; ମୁଖପୃଷ୍ଠାରେ ଗୋବିନ୍ଦ ରଥଙ୍କ ନାମ ପ୍ରକାଶକ ଭାବେ ଅଛି। ସେହି ବହିରେ ଲେମ୍ବୁ ଢଗର ଏକ ରୂପ ମିଳେ। ଏଥିରୁ କଥାଟି ସେତେବେଳେ ଲେଖାରେ ଥିଲା ବୋଲି ଜଣାଯାଏ; ପ୍ରଥମେ କିଏ ବା କେବେ କହିଥିଲେ, ତାହା ଜଣାଯାଏ ନାହିଁ।
paragraphs.english: These expressions also have a printed history. The title page of ଢଗମାଳିକା, ପ୍ରଥମଭାଗ identifies Gobinda Rath as publisher and Victoria Press, Cuttack, 1893. A version of the lemon saying appears in that volume. This establishes a written witness by that date; it does not establish who first said it or when it began.

paragraphs.odia: ପୁରୁଣା ବହିରେ ମିଳିବା ଏକ ପ୍ରକାର ସାକ୍ଷ୍ୟ; ଆଜି କେଉଁ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିରେ ଆମେ ତାକୁ ବୁଝୁଛୁ, ସେ ଆଉ ଏକ କଥା। ଏହି ସଂଗ୍ରହରେ ମୂଳ ଉକ୍ତି, ତାହାର ଭିନ୍ନ ରୂପ ଓ ଆମର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାକୁ ଅଲଗା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ସବୁ ଉକ୍ତି ଏକେ ପ୍ରକାରର ନୁହେଁ—କେତେକ ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ପ୍ରବାଦ, କେତେକ ଛନ୍ଦମୟ କଥା, ଆଉ କେତେକ ରୂଢ଼ି।
paragraphs.english: Finding a saying in an old book is one kind of evidence; understanding its possible use today is another. This collection distinguishes the wording, its variants and our interpretation. The entries also differ in form: some are complete proverbs, some rhymed sayings, and some idiomatic expressions.

paragraphs.odia: ପିଲାଙ୍କୁ ଢଗ ସହ ପରିଚିତ କରାଇବା ପାଇଁ ପ୍ରଥମେ ମୁଖସ୍ଥ କରାଇବା ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ। ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ କୌଣସି ଘଟଣା ସହ ମେଳ ଖାଉଥିବା ଏକ ସହଜ ଢଗ କହି ତାହା ଶୁଣି କେଉଁ ଚିତ୍ର ମନକୁ ଆସୁଛି ବୋଲି ପଚାରିପାରିବା: ଲେମ୍ବୁକୁ ଅଧିକ ଚିପୁଡ଼ିଲେ କଣ ଭାବ ମନକୁ ଆସୁଛି? ଏହି କଥା ଆଉ କେଉଁଠି ଲାଗିପାରେ? କେଉଁ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିରେ ଏହା ଠିକ୍ ହେବ ନାହିଁ? ପିଲାର ନିଜ ଉଦାହରଣ ଓ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ପାଇଁ ଜାଗା ରହୁ।
paragraphs.english: Children need not begin by memorising a list. We can introduce a simple saying when an ordinary event gives it a setting, then ask what picture it brings to mind. Where else might it fit? When might it fail? Leave room for the child’s own example and objection. These are invitations to a conversation, not a test.

paragraphs.odia: ଘରେ କେହି ଏହି କଥାକୁ ଅନ୍ୟ ଭାବେ କହୁଥିଲେ, ସେହି ରୂପଟି ମଧ୍ୟ ଶୁଣିବା। ମନେ ଥିବା ଉଚ୍ଚାରଣ, ଲୟ ଓ କହିବାର ଅବସରକୁ ଲେଖି ରଖିପାରିବା। ଓଡ଼ିଆ ନୂଆ ଶିଖୁଥିବା ବୟସ୍କ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ମଧ୍ୟ ଏଭଳି ଆରମ୍ଭ କରିପାରନ୍ତି। ଅନୁବାଦ ଅର୍ଥର ଦୁଆର ଖୋଲିଦେବ; ମୂଳ କଥାଟି ଶୁଣିବା ଓ ତାହାର ବ୍ୟବହାର ବୁଝିବା ସେହି ଅର୍ଥକୁ ଆହୁରି ଜୀବନ୍ତ କରିବ।
paragraphs.english: If someone at home knows another version, listen to it too. Its pronunciation, rhythm and remembered occasion can be worth recording. Adults beginning Odia can approach it in the same spirit. Translation opens a door to the meaning; hearing the expression and understanding its use gives that meaning a fuller life.

sections.title_odia: ବୁଝି ରଖିବା, ବିଚାର କରି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିବା

paragraphs.odia: ପୁରୁଣା କଥା ହେଲେ ବୋଲି ସବୁ ଉକ୍ତିକୁ ଜୀବନର ନିୟମ କରିହେବ ନାହିଁ। କେତେକ ଢଗରେ ଅପମାନ, ପକ୍ଷପାତ ବା ହିଂସାର ଛାୟା ଅଛି। ସେଗୁଡ଼ିକୁ ବୁଝିବା ସହିତ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ମଧ୍ୟ କରିବା ଦରକାର। କାହାକୁ ହେୟ କରିବାର ଅନୁମତି ଭାବେ ତାହାକୁ ନେବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ। ଯାହା ଆମକୁ ଧୈର୍ଯ୍ୟ, ପରିମାଣ, ସହଯୋଗ ବା ଆତ୍ମବିଚାରର ସୁଯୋଗ ଦିଏ, ତାହାକୁ ଆଜିର ଜୀବନରେ ବିଚାର କରି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିପାରିବା।
paragraphs.english: Age does not make every saying a rule to live by. Some contain insults, prejudice or images of violence. Understanding them includes questioning them; remembering an expression does not give us permission to demean someone. We can draw thoughtfully on those that help us consider patience, proportion, cooperation or our own conduct.

paragraphs.odia: ମୋ ପାଇଁ ଏହି ସମ୍ପର୍କ ଦୂରତାରେ ଶେଷ ହୋଇନାହିଁ। ଢଗକୁ ପୁଣି ପଢ଼ିବା ମାନେ କେବଳ ପୁରୁଣା ଶବ୍ଦ ଉଦ୍ଧାର କରିବା ନୁହେଁ; ନିଜ ଭିତରେ ଚାଲୁଥିବା ଏକ କଥାବାର୍ତ୍ତାକୁ ଶୁଣିବା। ସେହି କଥାବାର୍ତ୍ତାରେ ଆଉ ଜଣେ ସାମିଲ ହେଲେ ଭାଷା ମଧ୍ୟ ନୂଆ ଜୀବନ ପାଏ।
paragraphs.english: For me, distance has not ended this connection. Returning to these sayings means hearing a conversation that is still going on within me. When somebody else joins that conversation, the language finds another place to live.

cover.alt: An illustrated tree grows from an open travelling suitcase, a metaphor for language remaining alive across distance.
cover.subtitle: 211 Odia sayings, meanings and everyday life

entries.title: When too much turns bitter
entries.literal_meaning: If you squeeze a lemon too much, it turns bitter.
entries.explanation: The useful action—extracting juice—becomes counterproductive when carried too far. The warning is about proportion: pressing for one more favour, one more concession or one more advantage may damage what was already achieved. It does not mean that effort itself is bad.
entries.meaning_odia: ଲେମ୍ବୁରୁ ରସ ପାଇବାକୁ ଚିପୁଡ଼ିବା ଦରକାର, କିନ୍ତୁ ଅତି କଲେ ସ୍ୱାଦ ବିଗିଡ଼ିଯାଏ—ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ କଥାଟିର ମର୍ମ ଅଛି। ଯେଉଁ ଚେଷ୍ଟା ପ୍ରଥମେ ଉପକାର କରୁଥିଲା, ମାତ୍ରା ଛାଡ଼ିଲେ ସେହି ଚେଷ୍ଟା ଓଲଟା ଫଳ ଦେଇପାରେ। ତେଣୁ କେବେ ଆଉ ଟିକେ କରିବା ଓ କେବେ ଅଟକିବା, ସେହି ବିଚାର ମୁଖ୍ୟ; ପରିଶ୍ରମ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବା ଏହାର ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: After a neighbour has agreed to help for an afternoon, repeatedly asking for more time may invite this saying. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The image makes a social judgement through an ordinary kitchen action. This reading explains the metaphor; it is not a scientific claim about every citrus fruit or a documented account of how the proverb originated.

entries.title: Inviting trouble
entries.literal_meaning: Come, ox, gore me.
entries.explanation: The speaker imagines someone summoning the very trouble they could have avoided. Used ironically, it criticises an unnecessary provocation or a knowingly risky decision. It should not be used to blame someone for harm they did not choose.
entries.meaning_odia: ଶାନ୍ତ ଥିବା ବଳଦକୁ ନିଜେ ଡାକି ବିପଦକୁ ନିମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ କରିବାର ମଜାଳିଆ ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଦରକାର ନଥାଇ ଖୋଚା ଦେବା, ଝଗଡ଼ା ଆରମ୍ଭ କରିବା ବା ଅସୁବିଧାକୁ ନିଜ ଆଡ଼କୁ ଟାଣିବା ବେଳେ କଥାଟି ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ତେବେ କେହି କ୍ଷତିର ଶିକାର ହେଲେ ସେ ନିଜେ ତାହା ଡାକି ଆଣିଥିଲେ ବୋଲି ଧରିନେବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A person interrupts an argument that has nothing to do with them merely to insult both sides; a friend may use this saying. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: ବଳଦ is rendered here as ox or bullock. The horned animal supplies the force of the image; the wording alone cannot establish a particular village, farming community or date of origin.

entries.title: There will be another winter
entries.literal_meaning: Cold does not finish with a single Magha.
entries.explanation: One difficult season is not the last occasion on which we may need help. The saying can warn against treating a temporary advantage as permanent, or remind someone who refuses help that circumstances may change. Tone matters: it can sound like practical advice or a pointed warning.
entries.meaning_odia: ମାଘର ଶୀତ ଥରକରେ ସରେନାହିଁ; ପୁଣି ସେମିତି ଦିନ ଆସିପାରେ—ଏହି ଭାବରେ କଥାଟି କୁହାଯାଏ। ଆଜି ଯାହାର ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ, କାଲି ତାହାର ଦରକାର ପଡ଼ିପାରେ। ଏଥିରେ ଆଗାମୀ ଦିନ ଓ ପରସ୍ପରର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ମନେ ପକାଇବାର ସ୍ୱର ଅଛି, ପାଗର ପୂର୍ବାନୁମାନ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: After borrowing a tool successfully once, someone dismisses the neighbour who lent it. Another person reminds them that they may need that neighbour again. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Magha supplies the seasonal image. The central point is recurring need and changing fortunes, not a precise forecast or a claim that cold is confined to one calendar month.

entries.title: Learning when responsibility arrives
entries.literal_meaning: When it falls on the shoulder, one learns to play.
entries.explanation: Taking responsibility can force a beginner to learn the necessary skill. The compressed wording leaves the instrument unnamed; imagining a carried percussion instrument helps explain the metaphor, but does not establish which instrument first inspired it. This is encouragement to learn through doing, not a guarantee that preparation is unnecessary.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ କାନ୍ଧରେ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ତାହା ସମ୍ଭାଳିବାର ଉପାୟ ଶିଖିବାକୁ ହୁଏ—ଏହି ଭାବ କଥାଟିରେ ଅଛି। ଦୂରରୁ ଦେଖିବା ଓ ନିଜେ କାମରେ ହାତ ଦେବାର ଅନୁଭବ ଏକ ନୁହେଁ। ଏହା କାମ କରି ଶିଖିବାର କଥା; ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି କିମ୍ବା ଅନ୍ୟର ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ବୋଲି କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A first-time organiser worries about arranging a neighbourhood reading session. A more experienced friend uses the saying while offering help with the practical tasks. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The body carrying a burden and the hands learning a performance meet in one image. No historical link to a named musical tradition has been verified.

entries.title: Not even a straw broken
entries.literal_meaning: Not to break one piece of straw into two.
entries.explanation: This expression makes a very small action stand for any contribution at all. Saying that someone has not done even this means they have done no work in the situation being discussed. It is an idiomatic phrase rather than a complete rhymed maxim.
entries.meaning_odia: କୁଟା ଖଣ୍ଡେ ଭାଙ୍ଗିବା ପରି ସାମାନ୍ୟ କାମ ବି ନକରିବାର ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଅସହଯୋଗକୁ ଧରାଯାଇଛି। ସମସ୍ତେ କାମରେ ଲାଗିଥିବା ବେଳେ ଜଣେ ଆଦୌ ହାତ ନଲଗାଇଲେ ବିରକ୍ତିରେ ଏହି ରୂଢ଼ି କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। କିନ୍ତୁ କାମ କରିବାକୁ ଇଚ୍ଛା ନଥିବା ଓ କରିବାକୁ ସମର୍ଥ ନହେବା ଏକ କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Several people clean up after a gathering while one person only gives instructions. Someone complains that the person has not lifted a finger—the comparable English idiom. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Straw provides a small, light object in the verbal image. The comparison with an English idiom explains the sense; it is not a claim of translation, borrowing or shared origin.

entries.title: Advice that stops at the doorstep
entries.odia: କହି ଦେଉଥାଇ ପରକୁ, ବୁଦ୍ଧି ନ ଦିଶଇ ଘରକୁ
entries.literal_meaning: One keeps advising others, but wisdom is not seen at home.
entries.explanation: The criticism is the gap between giving advice and practising it. The outward-facing adviser appears wise, yet fails to apply that wisdom to their own affairs. The saying invites self-examination; it does not imply that advice is worthless whenever its giver has difficulties.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ଭଲ ପରାମର୍ଶ ଦେବା ସହଜ, ନିଜ ଜୀବନରେ ସେହି କଥା ମାନିବା କଷ୍ଟକର ହୋଇପାରେ। ଉପଦେଶ ଓ ନିଜ ଆଚରଣ ମଧ୍ୟର ଏହି ଫାଙ୍କକୁ କଥାଟି ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରେ। କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ନିଜେ ଭୁଲ୍ କରନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ପରାମର୍ଶଟି ଅବଶ୍ୟ ଭୁଲ୍ ହେବ, ଏମିତି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A person lectures everyone about keeping accounts but repeatedly loses track of their own spending. A relative uses this line to point out the inconsistency. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The rhyme of ପରକୁ and ଘରକୁ reinforces the contrast between others and home. Here the structure is part of the saying’s force, not just decoration.

entries.title: Noise is not the same as action
entries.literal_meaning: The cloud that thunders does not rain.
entries.explanation: The contrast between loud thunder and absent rain is used to question bluster: impressive promises or threats do not necessarily lead to action. Read the sentence figuratively. Thunderstorms can, of course, bring rain; the proverb is not a dependable weather rule.
entries.meaning_odia: ମେଘର ଗର୍ଜନ ବଡ଼, କିନ୍ତୁ ବର୍ଷାର ଦେଖା ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ତଫାତକୁ ମଣିଷର କଥା ଓ କାମ ସହ ମେଳାଯାଇଛି। ବହୁତ ଘୋଷଣା ବା ଧମକ ଥାଇ କାମରେ କିଛି ନଦିଶିଲେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଏ। ଗର୍ଜନର ଚିତ୍ରଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗକୁ ଜୋର୍ ଦିଏ; ସବୁ ମେଘ ବିଷୟରେ ନିୟମ ଦେଉନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Someone loudly promises to repair a shared bench, but nothing happens. Others use the saying to ask for action rather than another announcement. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Weather becomes a way of talking about human speech. Similar imagery elsewhere would not by itself prove where this Odia wording originated.

entries.title: Planting when the meal is due
entries.literal_meaning: Planting eggplant at wedding time.
entries.explanation: The joke is a mismatch between a long preparation and an immediate need. Planting a crop when the occasion has arrived cannot supply that occasion’s meal. The saying criticises starting essential work too late, rather than the act of planting itself.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାହାଘରର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ସାମ୍ନାରେ ଆସିଲାଣି, ଅଥଚ ବାଇଗଣ ଚାରା ଲଗାଇବାର ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ଏବେ ଆରମ୍ଭ। ଫଳ ମିଳିବାକୁ ସମୟ ଲାଗୁଥିବା କାମକୁ ଶେଷ ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ପକାଇରଖିବା ହିଁ ଏଠାରେ ହାସ୍ୟର କାରଣ। କଥାଟି ଠିକ୍ ସମୟରେ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତିର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ବୁଝାଏ, ସବୁ ବାହାଘରର ଖାଦ୍ୟତାଲିକା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: The event starts tomorrow, but the organisers only now begin looking for a venue. Someone compares their timing to planting eggplant at wedding time. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The wedding and vegetable crop create the contrast. This does not prove eggplant is required at every Odia wedding or identify a particular community’s menu. The graphic illustrates lead time, not an agricultural timetable.

entries.title: Anger aimed at the bowl
entries.literal_meaning: Biting the bowl in anger at the medicine.
entries.explanation: The unpleasant thing is the medicine, but the anger is directed at its container. The expression describes displaced frustration: attacking a messenger, object or bystander instead of addressing the actual problem.
entries.meaning_odia: ଔଷଧ ଉପରେ ରାଗ ହେଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ ରାଗର ଆଘାତ ପଡ଼ିଲା ପାତ୍ର ଉପରେ। ଅସୁବିଧାର ମୂଳ ଅନ୍ୟଠାରେ ଥାଇ ରାଗ ଆଉ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଝାଡ଼ିବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ବୁଝାଯାଏ। ରାଗ କାହା ଉପରେ ହେଲା ଓ ତାହାର ଫଳ କିଏ ଭୋଗିଲା, ସେହି ଦୁଇଟିକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଦେଖିଲେ କଥାଟିର ମର୍ମ ବୁଝାପଡ଼େ।
entries.usage_example: A delayed delivery frustrates a customer, who shouts at a neighbour merely passing on the update. Another person uses the saying to identify the misplaced anger. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source writes ଓଷଦ and କାମୁଡିବା; this edition preserves those forms rather than silently replacing them with modern spellings. The image explains behaviour and gives no advice about taking medicine.

entries.title: A little game, an enormous quarrel
entries.literal_meaning: From a game of jhimiti to the Mahabharata.
entries.explanation: A small disagreement grows into an outsized conflict. The Mahabharata provides a culturally recognisable scale of conflict. The expression is not evidence that the epic war literally began with this named game, and the game’s precise historical rules have not been established here.
entries.meaning_odia: ଛୋଟ ଖେଳର କଥା ବଢ଼ିବଢ଼ି ମହାଭାରତ ପରି ବଡ଼ କଳହରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିଗଲା—ଏହି ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତିରେ କଥାଟିର ମଜା। ସାମାନ୍ୟ ମତଭେଦକୁ ନେଇ ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ବଡ଼ ଝଗଡ଼ା ହେଲେ ଏହା ଖାପ ଖାଏ। କଥା କେତେ ଛୋଟ ଥିଲା ଓ ଝଗଡ଼ା କେତେ ବଡ଼ ହେଲା, ସେହି ତଫାତକୁ ଏହା ଆଖି ଆଗକୁ ଆଣେ।
entries.usage_example: Two friends disagree over a turn in a game; soon several families are arguing. A neighbour uses the saying to describe how far the quarrel has grown. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: ଝିମିଟି is retained rather than replaced by an invented modern game. The contrast is between a modest starting point and epic-scale escalation.

entries.title: When dishonest gain takes the roots with it
entries.odia: ଅଧର୍ମ ବିତ୍ତ ବଢେ ବହୁତ, ଗଲା ବେଳେ ଯାଏ ମୂଳ ସହିତ ।
entries.literal_meaning: Wrongfully gained wealth grows greatly, but disappears with its roots.
entries.explanation: The image contrasts rapid growth with loss at the root. Wealth obtained dishonestly may look impressive, yet the conduct behind it can endanger the whole household or enterprise. This is a moral warning about how gain is obtained, not a reliable prediction that every dishonest person will become poor.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ଉପାୟରେ ଆସିଥିବା ଧନ ପ୍ରଥମେ ବଢ଼ୁଥିବା ପରି ଲାଗିଲେ ବି ଶେଷରେ ମୂଳ ସମ୍ବଳକୁ ନଷ୍ଟ କରିପାରେ—ଏହି ଚେତାବନୀ କଥାଟିରେ ଅଛି। ତୁରନ୍ତ ଲାଭ ଦେଖି ତାହାର ପରିଣାମ ଭୁଲିଯିବାକୁ ଏହା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ। ଏହା ନୈତିକ ସତର୍କତା, ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଲୋକର ଭବିଷ୍ୟତ ଧନସମ୍ପତ୍ତିର ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହିସାବ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A trader is tempted to falsify weights for a little extra profit. An older colleague uses the saying to warn that losing customers’ trust could destroy the business. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The rhyme of ବହୁତ and ସହିତ gives the warning a memorable close. The root image suggests losing the foundation, not merely the most recent gain. A version appears as the opening proverb of the1893 collection.

entries.title: Keeping one’s own dignity
entries.odia: ଆଲୋ ସଖି, ଆପଣା ମହତ ଆପେ ରଖି
entries.literal_meaning: Friend, preserve your own dignity yourself.
entries.explanation: The friendly address makes this advice sound like one person speaking directly to another: preserve your dignity through your own conduct. It may counsel restraint when someone is tempted to join a humiliating quarrel or chase approval. It does not make a person responsible for mistreatment inflicted by others.
entries.meaning_odia: ସଖୀକୁ ସମ୍ବୋଧନ କରି ନିଜ ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦା ନିଜେ ଜଗିବାର କଥା କୁହାଯାଇଛି। କଥାବାର୍ତ୍ତା ଓ ବ୍ୟବହାରରେ ସଂଯମ ରଖିବା, ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ଭାବେ ନିଜକୁ ଅସୁବିଧାରେ ନପକାଇବା ଏହାର ଏକ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ। କିନ୍ତୁ ଅନ୍ୟର ଅପମାନ ବା ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ପାଇଁ ଅପମାନିତ ଲୋକକୁ ଦାୟୀ କରିବାର ଯୁକ୍ତି ଏହା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: During an argument, a friend is about to answer an insult with another insult. Someone close to them uses the line to encourage a calm withdrawal. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The contemporary witness begins ଆଲୋ ସଖି. The1893 scan appears to begin ଆରେ ସଖି; that difference is retained as a provisional historical reading. The wording does not establish who first used the saying or confine its advice to one gender.

entries.title: When praise becomes suspicious
entries.literal_meaning: Excessive devotion is a thief’s sign.
entries.explanation: Exaggerated displays of devotion or deference can invite suspicion that the speaker wants something. In everyday use the warning can concern flattery, not only religious devotion. The force comes from the deliberately sharp word “thief”; the saying itself is not evidence that a particular admirer is dishonest.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅସାଧାରଣ ଭାବେ ଭକ୍ତି ବା ବିନୟ ଦେଖାଇବା ପଛରେ ଅନ୍ୟ ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ଥାଇପାରେ ବୋଲି ଏହି କଥା ସନ୍ଦେହ ପ୍ରକାଶ କରେ। ଚାଟୁକାରିତାରେ ଭୋଳି ନଯାଇ କାମ ଓ ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟକୁ ଦେଖିବା ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ। ଭକ୍ତି ବା ଭଦ୍ରତା ନିଜେ ଚୋରିର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A stranger showers a shopkeeper with praise and then asks to take goods away without paying. The shopkeeper recalls this saying and checks the request carefully. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: ଭକ୍ତି supplies the outward appearance of reverence, while ଚୋର supplies the hidden motive in the proverb’s contrast. Interpretation depends on the conversation; sincere devotion is not being classified as theft.

entries.title: Swinging without seeing
entries.literal_meaning: Swinging a stick in darkness.
entries.explanation: A stick swung in darkness may miss its intended target because the person cannot see where to aim. The expression describes guesses or effort without adequate information. Its criticism is not that no effort is being made, but that effort has no dependable direction.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ଧାରରେ ବାଡ଼ି ବୁଲାଇଲେ ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ କେଉଁଠି ଅଛି ଜଣା ନଥାଏ। ଆବଶ୍ୟକ ତଥ୍ୟ ନଜାଣି ଅନୁମାନରେ କାମ କରିବା ବା ଉତ୍ତର ଦେବାକୁ ଏହି ରୂଢ଼ି ବୁଝାଏ। ଚେଷ୍ଟା ହେଉଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଦିଗ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ତଫାତଟି ମନେ ରଖିବା ଦରକାର।
entries.usage_example: Several people keep changing settings on a faulty device without checking what has failed. One suggests identifying the problem first instead of trying changes at random. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: This is an idiomatic action phrase rather than a complete rhyming couplet. Darkness is the image for missing information; no specific origin incident has been established.

entries.title: An appetite larger than the means
entries.odia: ଅରଜି ନପାରେ ମୁଣ୍ଡ, ସୁଆଦ ଲୋଡୁଚି ତୁଣ୍ଡ ।
entries.literal_meaning: The head cannot earn; the mouth wants delicacies.
entries.explanation: The line sets the head’s inability to earn against the mouth’s demand for tasty food. It can rebuke expectations of luxury that do not match available means or contribution. Its tone is sharp and can be hurtful when applied to someone whose circumstances are outside their control.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆୟର ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟ ଅଳ୍ପ, କିନ୍ତୁ ରୁଚି ଓ ଚାହିଦା ବହୁତ—ଏହି ଅମେଳକୁ କଥାଟି କଟାକ୍ଷ କରେ। ନିଜ ସମ୍ବଳ ନଦେଖି ଅଧିକ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚର ଇଚ୍ଛା ରଖିବା ବେଳେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଏହାର ସ୍ୱର କଟୁ; ଅଭାବ ବା କାମ ନମିଳିବାକୁ ଲୋକର ଦୋଷ ବୋଲି ଧରିବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A group has agreed to a modest outing, but one member insists on an expensive feast while refusing to contribute. Another uses the saying to question that mismatch. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: ମୁଣ୍ଡ and ତୁଣ୍ଡ create a compact rhyme between earning and appetite. A possible related line in the1893 scan remains unverified; its uncertain wording is not presented here as a confirmed historical match.

entries.title: When means are short
entries.literal_meaning: Little money, an anxious mind.
entries.explanation: The line connects limited means with the distress of being unable to meet needs. Its compact rhyme can express sympathy for someone trying to make a small sum cover many demands. It need not be read as an accusation of greed or a judgement about character.
entries.meaning_odia: ଟଙ୍କା ଅଳ୍ପ ଥିଲେ ଆବଶ୍ୟକ କାମ କିପରି ହେବ, ସେହି ଚିନ୍ତା ମନକୁ ଅସ୍ଥିର କରିପାରେ। ଧନର ଅଭାବ ଓ ମନର ବିକଳତାକୁ ଛୋଟ କଥାଟି ଏକାଠି ରଖିଛି। ଏହାକୁ ଲୋଭର ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଅପେକ୍ଷା ଅପୂରଣ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତାର ଦୁଃଖ ଭାବେ ବୁଝିବା ଏଠାରେ ଅଧିକ ସଂଗତ।

entries.cultural_context: The source adds an explanation about being unable to obtain necessities. That explanatory parenthesis is kept outside the saying itself.

entries.title: Spending tomorrow’s means today
entries.odia: ଆଜି କୁରୁ କୁରୁ ହସୁ, କାଲି ଲଙ୍ଗଳ କାହିଁରେ ଚଷୁ ?
entries.literal_meaning: Today you laugh merrily; tomorrow, what will you plough with?
entries.explanation: The teasing question asks what will remain after today’s enjoyment. It warns against consuming the very means needed for tomorrow’s work. The pleasure is immediate, while the cost becomes visible only when work must resume.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆଜିର ଆନନ୍ଦ ପାଇଁ କାଲିର ଚଳଣିର ସମ୍ବଳ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ କରିଦେବାର ବିରୋଧାଭାସ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି। ହଳକୁ ଜାଳିଦେବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଦେଖାଏ ଯେ କେବଳ ଜିନିଷଟି ନୁହେଁ, ଆଗକୁ କାମ କରିବାର ଉପାୟ ବି ନଷ୍ଟ ହେଉଛି। ଏହା ଆଜିର ଖୁସି ଓ ଆଗାମୀ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ବିଚାରର କଥା, କୌଣସି ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ଘଟଣାର ବିବରଣୀ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: Responding to the occasion
entries.literal_meaning: Hey, you—whatever the occasion calls for.
entries.explanation: This compressed expression advises a fitting response to the circumstances. It may interrupt someone who insists on handling every situation in the same way. The point is practical judgement about this occasion, rather than a rule that commitments can always be discarded.
entries.meaning_odia: ସବୁ ସମୟରେ ଏକା ପ୍ରକାର କଥା ବା ବ୍ୟବହାର ଖାପ ଖାଏନାହିଁ। ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ବୁଝି ଉଚିତ ଉତ୍ତର ବା ପଦକ୍ଷେପ ବାଛିବାର ବୁଦ୍ଧିକୁ ଏହି କଥା ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦିଏ। ସମୟ ଦେଖି ଚଳିବା ମାନେ ଦେଇଥିବା କଥା ବା ଦାୟିତ୍ୱକୁ ସୁବିଧାମତେ ଭୁଲିଯିବା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A host changes the outdoor arrangements when rain begins instead of insisting on the original plan. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source itself supplies an English gloss about appropriate action. The elliptical Odia is retained; the English rendering makes the implied advice explicit.

entries.title: A welcome that sends you away
entries.odia: ଆସିଲ ବନ୍ଧୁ ଭଲ କଲ, ବସିବାକୁ ନାହିଁ ଠା, ଯେଉଁ ବାଟେ ବାଟେ ଆସିଲ ବନ୍ଧୁ ସେଇ ବାଟେ ବାଟେ ଯା ।
entries.literal_meaning: Good of you to come, friend; there is nowhere to sit. Go back by the very way you came.
entries.explanation: The opening sounds hospitable, but the ending cancels the welcome. The humour lies in that sudden reversal: someone offers warm words while making it plain that the visitor is unwanted. Used pointedly, it exposes courtesy that provides no actual welcome.
entries.meaning_odia: ମୁହଁରେ ଆଦର କରି ଡାକୁଛନ୍ତି, କିନ୍ତୁ ବସିବାର ଜାଗା ବି ଦେଉନାହାନ୍ତି—ଏହି ଓଲଟାପଣରେ ହାସ୍ୟ ଅଛି। ସ୍ୱାଗତର କଥା ଓ ପ୍ରକୃତ ବ୍ୟବହାର ମେଳ ନଖାଇଲେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଏ। ଆଦରର ମୂଲ୍ୟ କେବଳ ଡାକରେ ନୁହେଁ, ଅତିଥିଙ୍କୁ କିପରି ରଖାଯାଉଛି ସେଥିରେ ଦିଶେ।
entries.usage_example: A club warmly invites suggestions but immediately dismisses every visitor’s proposal; an observer recalls this saying. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The repeated address to a friend sharpens the irony. The example extends that verbal pattern to another setting; no historical hospitality custom is being asserted.

entries.title: Value put to the test
entries.odia: କାଚ, କାଚ, ମଣି, ମଣି, କିଣା ବିକା ବେଳେ ଜଣା ଜଣି
entries.literal_meaning: Glass is glass, a gem is a gem; buying and selling reveal which is which.
entries.explanation: Resemblance and confident claims are not enough to establish value. The saying imagines a transaction as the moment when differences become consequential. It can be used when an attractive promise finally has to face a practical test.
entries.meaning_odia: କାଚ ଓ ମଣି ଦେଖିବାକୁ ଏକା ଭଳି ଲାଗିଲେ ବି ସେମାନଙ୍କର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଏକ ନୁହେଁ। ପ୍ରକୃତ କାମ ବା ବିଚାରର ସମୟରେ ଗୁଣର ତଫାତ ଜଣାପଡ଼େ—ଏହି ଭାବରେ କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟବହୃତ। ବାହାରର ଚମକ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କାମରେ ଦିଶୁଥିବା ଗୁଣକୁ ପରଖିବାର କଥା ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି।
entries.usage_example: Two suppliers make equally impressive promises; a buyer asks to see their finished work before deciding. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The image comes from comparing valuable objects with lookalikes. It is a metaphor about testing claims, not a guarantee that markets always recognise quality.

entries.title: Making a small irritation worse
entries.literal_meaning: Scratch an itch into a wound.
entries.explanation: An action that brings brief relief can deepen the original trouble. In conversation, the expression can describe reopening a minor grievance until it becomes a serious quarrel. The rebuke is directed at aggravating the problem rather than resolving it.
entries.meaning_odia: କୁଣ୍ଡେଇବାରୁ ଛୋଟ ଅସୁବିଧା ବଢ଼ିବା ପରି, କଥାକୁ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଖୋଚିଲେ କଳହ ବଢ଼ିପାରେ। ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଅସନ୍ତୋଷକୁ ନେଇ ଅଧିକ କଥା ଟାଣିବା ବେଳେ ଏହି ତୁଳନା ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ଶରୀରର ଚିତ୍ର ଏଠାରେ କଥାର ଉପମା, ଚିକିତ୍ସାର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A small misunderstanding has been settled, but repeated sarcastic reminders start the argument again. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The bodily image supplies a social metaphor. This entry explains that metaphor and offers no medical advice.

entries.title: Getting ahead of the occasion
entries.literal_meaning: Undressed before even seeing the river.
entries.explanation: The image mocks preparation that runs ahead of any confirmed need. Someone has acted as though the next step were certain before checking whether the situation calls for it. The saying is sharper than a general reminder to plan carefully.
entries.meaning_odia: ନଈ ପାଖରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିବା ଆଗରୁ ପାର ହେବାର ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି କରିବାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ହାସ୍ୟରେ ଦେଖାଯାଇଛି। କାମ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନଥାଇ ତାହାର ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ପଦକ୍ଷେପରେ ଲାଗିଯିବା ଏହାର ଭାବ। ଆଗୁଆ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ଓ ଅକାରଣ ତରବର ମଧ୍ୟରେ ତଫାତ ଅଛି।
entries.usage_example: Before a trip is agreed, a participant announces the departure date and begins making arrangements for everyone. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The river and undressing belong to the saying’s literal scene. They do not establish a particular place, journey or bathing custom as its origin.

entries.title: Plans are still untested
entries.literal_meaning: Planned beforehand, yet all still raw!
entries.explanation: An advance plan may look settled until circumstances put it to the test. The source explains the line as a warning that earlier arrangements can fall apart at the appointed time. It tempers certainty without making preparation itself pointless.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭଲ ଭାବି ରଖିଥିବା ଯୋଜନା ବି ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ବଦଳିଲେ ଅସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ରହିପାରେ। ମନରେ ଥିବା ଆୟୋଜନ ଓ ପ୍ରକୃତରେ ଯାହା ହେଲା, ତାହାର ଅମେଳକୁ କଥାଟି ଧରେ। ଏଥିରେ ନିରାଶାର ସ୍ୱର ଅଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଯୋଜନା କରିବା ନିରର୍ଥକ ବୋଲି ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: Giving beyond one’s means
entries.odia: ମୋତେ ନ ଅଣ୍ଟେ ମୁଁ ନେଇ କରି ସାଇରେ ବାଣ୍ଟେ
entries.literal_meaning: It is not enough for me, yet I take it and distribute it around the neighbourhood.
entries.explanation: The speaker describes a mismatch between available means and a display of generosity. It can question a promise to provide for everyone when the giver has not secured enough to do so. Its irony concerns overextension; it need not belittle sharing during hardship.
entries.meaning_odia: ନିଜ ପାଇଁ ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ନଥାଇ ସାରା ପଡ଼ାକୁ ବାଣ୍ଟିବାର ଦାବି କରିବାରେ ଅମେଳ ଦିଶେ। ନିଜ ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟଠାରୁ ବଡ଼ ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ଦେବାକୁ ଏହି କଥା ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରେ। ଅଳ୍ପରୁ ଭାଗ କରିଦେବାର ଉଦାରତା ଓ ପୂରଣ କରିହେବନଥିବା ଘୋଷଣା ଏକ କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: An organiser promises supplies to several groups before checking whether the stock covers even the first group. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The neighbourhood gives the boast an audience. This is an editorial reading of the recorded wording; the witness supplies no separate explanation for this item.

entries.title: Nodding without understanding
entries.literal_meaning: Nod the head like a lizard.
entries.explanation: A person keeps signalling agreement whether or not they understand what is being said. The source’s gloss makes the gap between the nod and comprehension explicit. The expression can tease empty assent or call attention to it when a real decision requires understanding.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏଣ୍ଡୁଅର ମୁଣ୍ଡ ହଲାଇବାକୁ ମଣିଷର ହଁ ଭରିବା ସହ ମେଳାଯାଇଛି। କଥାଟି ବୁଝିଛି କି ନାହିଁ ନଜାଣି କେବଳ ସମ୍ମତି ଦେଇ ଚାଲିଲେ ଏହି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ମୁଣ୍ଡ ହଲାଇବା ଓ କଥାଟି ବୁଝିବା ଅଲଗା; ହଁ ଶୁଣିଲେ ମାତ୍ର ବୁଝାମଣା ହୋଇଗଲା ବୋଲି ଭାବିହେବ ନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: After a complicated explanation, a listener nods along but cannot say what they have agreed to do. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The animal comparison belongs to the figurative expression. The entry makes no zoological claim about why a lizard moves its head.

entries.title: Making oneself welcome on every side
entries.odia: ଏ ଘର ମାଉସୀ ସେ ଘର ପିଉସୀ
entries.literal_meaning: A maternal aunt in this house, a paternal aunt in that one.
entries.explanation: The expression portrays someone claiming closeness everywhere while carrying damaging talk between people. The source gloss stresses pleasing both sides and creating discord. Its target is manipulative familiarity, not genuine friendship across households.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୁଇ ପକ୍ଷରେ ଆପଣାପଣ ଦେଖାଇ ଏଠାର କଥା ସେଠାରେ ପହଞ୍ଚାଇବାର ଚାଲାକିକୁ କଥାଟି ଧରେ। ବନ୍ଧୁତାର ଆଡ଼ରେ ଗୋଲମାଳ ବଢ଼ାଇଲେ ସେହି ଘନିଷ୍ଠତା ଉପକାର କରିବା ବଦଳରେ କ୍ଷତି କରେ। ଅନେକଙ୍କ ସହ ଭଲ ସମ୍ପର୍କ ରଖିବା ନୁହେଁ, ସେହି ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଅପବ୍ୟବହାର କରିବା ଏଠାରେ ସମାଲୋଚିତ।
entries.usage_example: A neighbour tells each household that they alone have her sympathy, while repeating complaints from the other. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: ମାଉସୀ and ପିଉସୀ are distinct kinship terms, preserved in the literal rendering. The figurative criticism does not describe a trait of actual aunts or of women generally.

entries.title: A difficulty too awkward to disclose
entries.odia: ଅଜାଗା ଘା ଦେଖି ହୁଏ ନାହିଁ କି ଦେଖାଇ ହୁଏ ନାହିଁ ।
entries.literal_meaning: A sore in an awkward place can neither be seen nor shown.
entries.explanation: The image conveys a predicament that is hard to inspect privately and embarrassing to disclose. In conversation, it can express the burden of a trouble someone feels unable to explain openly. Its force lies in that double bind, rather than in a recommendation to keep suffering secret.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏମିତି ଅସୁବିଧା ହୋଇଛି ଯାହା ସହିବା କଷ୍ଟ, ଆଉ ଅନ୍ୟକୁ କହିବାକୁ ବି ସଙ୍କୋଚ। ଲୁଚା ଘାଆର ଚିତ୍ର ସେହି ଦ୍ୱିଧାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ। କଥାଟି ମନର ଅସହଜତା ପ୍ରକାଶ କରେ; କଷ୍ଟ ଲୁଚାଇ ରଖିବାକୁ ବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନମାଗିବାକୁ କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A person asked to mediate a dispute between close relatives feels unable to describe either side’s private complaints. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The bodily image is retained in the literal rendering. The figurative explanation is an editorial reading; no medical claim or origin incident is established.

entries.title: A quarrel staged for others
entries.odia:
ଅଙ୍ଗୁଳି ସନ୍ଧିରେ ମଳି
ଭିତରେ ଭିତରେ ସଲା ସୁତୁରାଲୋ
ଉପରେ ଉପରେ କଳି ।
entries.literal_meaning: Dirt between the fingers; agreement behind the scenes, quarrelling on the surface.
entries.explanation: Two sides appear to fight while privately cooperating. The repeated contrast between inside and outside exposes a performance meant to mislead an audience. The saying accuses the quarrel of being staged; it does not merely describe people who disagree but remain friendly.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାହାରେ ଝଗଡ଼ାର ଦୃଶ୍ୟ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଭିତରେ ଦୁଇ ପକ୍ଷର ବୁଝାମଣା ରହିଛି। ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଭୁଲ୍ ବୁଝାଇବା ପାଇଁ ବିରୋଧର ଅଭିନୟ କରାଗଲେ ଏହି କଥା ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ସତରେ ମତଭେଦ ହେଉଥିବା ସାଙ୍ଗମାନଙ୍କୁ ମାତ୍ର ଦେଖି ଏପରି ଗୋପନ ବୁଝାମଣା ଧରିନେବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Two organisers loudly blame each other in public, although they have already agreed privately to divide the benefit. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The three source lines are retained. The address particle ଲୋ adds a conversational voice; the English rendering conveys the contrast without inventing a named listener.

entries.title: Saving a reply for later
entries.odia: ଏ କଥା ରହିଲା ମନେ, ବେଳ କାଳ ଦେଖି କହିବି ଦିନେ
entries.literal_meaning: I will keep this in mind; one day I will speak when the time is right.
entries.explanation: The speaker declines an immediate reply while making clear that the matter is not forgotten. Depending on the situation, the line can sound restrained, pointed or quietly threatening. It preserves a future opportunity to answer rather than offering reconciliation now.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏବେ କିଛି ନକହିଲେ ବି କଥାଟି ମନେ ରହିଲା, ପରେ ଉତ୍ତର ଦିଆଯିବ—ଏମିତି ସ୍ୱର ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି। ତୁରନ୍ତ ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା ନଦେଇ ଅସନ୍ତୋଷ ରଖିବାକୁ ଏହା ପ୍ରକାଶ କରିପାରେ। ତେଣୁ ଚୁପ୍ ରହିବାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ମନମାଳିନ୍ୟ ମିଟିଗଲା ବୋଲି ବୁଝିହେବ ନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Someone is dismissed during a meeting and replies that they will return to the matter when the facts can be discussed. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The time and occasion remain unspecified in the wording. This entry explains its possible conversational tone without assigning it a historical dispute.

entries.title: Who is there to tell?
entries.odia: କାହାକୁ କହିବା, କପାଳରେ ସିନା କର ମାରିବା
entries.literal_meaning: Whom can one tell? One can only strike a hand against one’s forehead.
entries.explanation: This is a gesture of exasperation put into words. The speaker feels that complaining will find no useful listener, so frustration turns into a weary reaction. It may be rueful or comic; it expresses a feeling of helplessness without proving that help is unavailable.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥା ଶୁଣିବାକୁ କେହି ନାହାନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ବକ୍ତାଙ୍କୁ ଲାଗୁଛି; ବିରକ୍ତିରେ ନିଜ ମୁଣ୍ଡକୁ ହାତ ଯାଉଛି। ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିବାର ଠିକଣା ନମିଳିବାର ଅସହାୟତାକୁ ଏହି ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତି ଧରେ। ଏହା ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତର କ୍ଷୋଭ, ସତରେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ସବୁ ବାଟ ବନ୍ଦ ବୋଲି ନିଷ୍କର୍ଷ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: After correcting the same simple mistake several times, a person says this with a tired laugh. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: କର means hand here. The literal gesture helps convey the expression; no physical action is prescribed by the explanation.

entries.title: Refusing to be polished into something else
entries.odia: ମୋତେ ଯେତେ ମାଠିବୁ ମାଠ ମୁହିଁ ସେଇ ଦରପଡ଼ା କାଠ
entries.literal_meaning: Polish me as much as you like; I remain that half-burnt wood.
entries.explanation: The speaker declares that repeated efforts to change or improve them will not work. The blunt material image can make the refusal comic, defiant or self-deprecating. It voices a stance in a conversation, not a truth that people cannot learn or change.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘଷିଲେ ବି ଅବସ୍ଥା ବଦଳିବ ନାହିଁ—ଏମିତି ଏକ ଜିଦ୍ ବା ନିଜକୁ ନେଇ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀର ସ୍ୱର ଏଠାରେ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଅଧାପୋଡ଼ା କାଠର ଉପମା ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ିଲେ ଅନ୍ୟର ବଦଳାଇବା ଚେଷ୍ଟାକୁ ଅଗ୍ରାହ୍ୟ କରିବାର ଭାବ ଆସେ। ତେବେ ଉତ୍ସର ‘ଦରପଡ଼ା’ ବନାନର ଏହି ପାଠ ଏକ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା, ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ଶବ୍ଦାର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ; ମଣିଷ ବଦଳିପାରେନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ବି ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: After repeated advice to adopt a more fashionable manner, someone jokingly insists that they will remain as they are. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The wood image and the first-person voice are preserved. This is distinct from enduring pressure: here the emphasis falls on resisting another person’s attempts to remake the speaker. The source spells the word ଦରପଡ଼ା. “Half-burnt” is an editorial interpretation of that spelling, not a verified correction to the original; lexical and human review remain pending.

entries.title: You can shake; I need not move
entries.odia:
ତୁ କେତେ ହଲଉଚୁ ହଲା...
ମୁଁ କିଛି ନହଲିଲେ ଗଲା...!!!
entries.literal_meaning: Shake as much as you like; it is enough if I do not budge.
entries.explanation: The speaker answers pressure with a challenge. Another person may keep trying to unsettle them, but the speaker claims control over their own response. The tone can convey resolve or stubbornness; its value depends on what they are refusing to yield about.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚାରିପଟେ ଯେତେ ହଲଚଲ ହେଉ, ନିଜ ଜାଗାରୁ ନହଟିବାର ଘୋଷଣା ଏହା। ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହା ଦୃଢ଼ ସଂକଳ୍ପ ଭଳି ଶୁଣାଯାଇପାରେ, ପୁଣି ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ଜିଦ୍ ଭଳି ମଧ୍ୟ। କେଉଁ କଥାରେ ଅଟଳ ରହାଯାଉଛି, ସେଥିରୁ ଏହାର ସ୍ୱର ବୁଝିବାକୁ ହୁଏ।

entries.title: No one even asked me to sit
entries.odia:
ମାଲୋ ମଲି,
ଗାଁ ଚାରିଆଡ଼େ ବୁଲି ଆଇଲି...
କେହି ନକହିଲେ ବସ ବୋଲି...!!!
entries.literal_meaning: Oh mother, I am undone! I went all around the village; no one said, “Sit down.”
entries.explanation: The complaint turns a small invitation into the measure of being welcomed. After going everywhere, the speaker has not received even that acknowledgement. The exaggerated opening can make the hurt comic, while the last line reveals the modest courtesy that was missing.
entries.meaning_odia: ସବୁଠି ଯାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ କେଉଁଠି ବସିବାର ଆଦର ମିଳୁନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଅଭିମାନକୁ କଥାଟି ହାସ୍ୟରେ କହେ। ବହୁତ ଚିହ୍ନାପରିଚୟ ଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆପଣା ସ୍ଥାନ ନପାଇବାର ଅନୁଭବ ଏଥିରେ ଧରାପଡ଼େ। ଚିହ୍ନା ଲୋକ ବହୁତ ଥାଇ ବି ଆଦର ନପାଇବାର ଦୁଃଖ ଏଠାରେ ହାସ୍ୟ ସହ ମିଶିଛି।

entries.cultural_context: The source places it under a gloss about not receiving due respect. The dramatic ମଲି is rendered as an exclamation, not a report of death. No universal village hospitality rule is inferred.

entries.title: Pride that boils over
entries.odia:
କ୍ଷୀର ଉତୁରିଲେ ଚୁଲିକୁ,
ମଣିଷ ଉତୁରିଲେ ଗାତକୁ...!!!
entries.literal_meaning: When milk boils over, it spills onto the hearth; when a person goes too far, into the pit.
entries.explanation: The first line supplies an everyday overflow; the second turns it into a warning about arrogance. The source explicitly frames the saying as a response to excessive pride. Its sharp downward ending suggests that losing restraint can bring a fall.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୁଧ ଉତୁରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ସହ ଅତି ଗର୍ବର ପରିଣାମକୁ ମେଳାଯାଇଛି। ନିଜକୁ ବହୁତ ବଡ଼ ଭାବି ସଂଯମ ହରାଇଲେ ଅସୁବିଧା ହୋଇପାରେ—ଏହା ହିଁ ସତର୍କତା। ଆତ୍ମବିଶ୍ୱାସ ଓ ଅହଂକାର ମଧ୍ୟରେ ତଫାତ ଅଛି; ସଫଳତାରେ ଖୁସି ହେବାକୁ କଥାଟି ମନା କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A successful team member begins dismissing everyone else’s advice, and a colleague warns against letting success become arrogance. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The comparison is between two kinds of overstepping. It is a figurative warning, not a prediction that every proud person will suffer a particular fate. The source’s digital punctuation is preserved.

entries.explanation: The small plant provides an image for qualities becoming noticeable early. Someone may use the saying when a beginner already shows promise. Early signs can be encouraging without fixing what a child or learner must become.
entries.meaning_odia: ତୁଳସୀର ଛୋଟ ପତ୍ରରୁ ବାସନା ଜଣାପଡ଼ିବାର ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଆରମ୍ଭରୁ ଗୁଣର ଆଭାସ ମିଳିବା କଥା କୁହାଯାଏ। କାହାର ପ୍ରଥମ ଚେଷ୍ଟାରେ ଦକ୍ଷତା ଦେଖିଲେ ପ୍ରଶଂସାରେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଆରମ୍ଭର ଆଭାସ ଉତ୍ସାହ ଦେଇପାରେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ସେଥିରୁ ଜଣଙ୍କ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଭବିଷ୍ୟତ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।

entries.title: Some help rather than none
entries.odia: ନାହିଁ ମାମୁଁ ଠଉଁ କଣା ମାମୁ ଭଲ

entries.explanation: The comparison expresses a preference for an imperfect resource over having none. Its family image assumes that an uncle can offer care or assistance. The point can be explained without treating disability as a measure of a person’s worth.
entries.meaning_odia: ସବୁ ସୁବିଧା ନଥିଲେ ବି କିଛି ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ମିଳିବା, କିଛି ନମିଳିବାଠାରୁ ଭଲ—ଏହା ଏଠାରେ ମୂଳ ଭାବ। ସୀମିତ ସମ୍ବଳରେ ଉପଯୋଗୀ ବାଟ ବାଛିବା ବେଳେ ଏହି ଅର୍ଥ ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ପୁରୁଣା ଉପମାରେ ଥିବା ଶାରୀରିକ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ କମାଇବାର ମାପକ ଭାବେ ନେବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: A hiding place that gives you away
entries.literal_meaning: Are you hiding? Your two feet are showing!
entries.explanation: Someone’s attempt to conceal a matter leaves an obvious clue. The question punctures the pretence of secrecy: what is meant to be hidden is still visible. It can tease a transparent excuse without proving any particular accusation.
entries.meaning_odia: ଲୁଚିବାର ଚେଷ୍ଟା ଚାଲିଛି, ହେଲେ ପାଦ ଦିଶୁଥିବାରୁ ଲୁଚା କଥାର ଆଭାସ ମିଳୁଛି। ନିଜେ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେଇଥିବା ଚିହ୍ନରୁ ଗୋପନ କଥା ପଦାରେ ପଡ଼ିବାକୁ ଏହା ବୁଝାଏ। ଲୁଚାଇବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁଥିବା ଲୋକର ନିଜ ଅସାବଧାନତା ହିଁ ଏଠାରେ ହାସ୍ୟର କାରଣ।

entries.title: Learning from a lost support
entries.literal_meaning: A blind person loses the walking stick once.
entries.explanation: Losing something relied upon can make a person more careful afterwards. The saying compresses that lesson into the loss of a walking stick. It is a figurative warning about repeating mistakes, not a factual assertion about blind people or a guarantee that a loss happens only once.
entries.meaning_odia: ଥରେ ଅତ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଦରକାରୀ ସମ୍ବଳ ହରାଇଲେ ପରଥର ତାହାକୁ ଅଧିକ ଜଗିବାର ଶିକ୍ଷା ମିଳେ। ଏଠାରେ ବାଡ଼ି ହରାଇବାର ଚିତ୍ର ସେହି ଅନୁଭବକୁ ତୀବ୍ର କରେ। କଥାଟି କ୍ଷତିରୁ ସତର୍କ ହେବା ବିଷୟରେ; ଦୃଷ୍ଟିହୀନ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଆଚରଣର ନିୟମ ବା ଆଉ କେବେ ଭୁଲ୍ ହେବନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଦାବି ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: A difficulty caused by one’s own act
entries.odia: ଆପଣା ହସ୍ତେ ଜିହ୍ଵା ଛେଦି, କେ ଅଛି ତାର ପ୍ରତିବାଦୀ
entries.literal_meaning: Having cut your tongue with your own hand, who is there to speak against it?
entries.explanation: The sharp image points to trouble brought about by one’s own action. It challenges an attempt to shift responsibility elsewhere. It should not be used to assume that every hardship is self-caused or that someone who made a mistake no longer deserves help.
entries.meaning_odia: ନିଜ କାମରୁ ନିଜର ଅସୁବିଧା ହେଲେ ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ଦୋଷ ଦେବା ସହଜ ନୁହେଁ—ଏହି ଭାବ କଥାଟିରେ ଅଛି। ତୀବ୍ର ଶାରୀରିକ ଚିତ୍ରଟି ନିଜ କାମର ଦାୟିତ୍ୱକୁ ଜୋର୍ ଦିଏ। କିନ୍ତୁ ସବୁ କଷ୍ଟ ନିଜ ଭୁଲ୍ରୁ ଆସେନାହିଁ, ଆଉ ଭୁଲ୍ କରିଥିଲେ ବି ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ଶେଷ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A team ignores its own backup plan, then finds that a preventable delay has stopped the work. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

entries.title: Back to the same courtyard
entries.odia: ଆରେ ଢମଣା , ବୁଲି ବୁଲିକରି ସେଇ ଅଗଣା ।
entries.literal_meaning: Hey, dhamana, after all that wandering, you are back in the same courtyard.
entries.explanation: A wandering journey ends where it began. In conversation, the image can describe repeated detours that bring no change, or someone returning to a familiar place after trying alternatives. The tone may be teasing or critical, depending on the situation.
entries.meaning_odia: ବହୁତ ଘୂରିବୁଲି ଶେଷରେ ପୁଣି ସେହି ଅଗଣାକୁ ଫେରିଆସିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଅନେକ ଚେଷ୍ଟା ବା ବୁଲାଣି ପରେ ଫଳରେ ବିଶେଷ ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନ ନହେଲେ କଥାଟି ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗ ଅନୁସାରେ ଏଥିରେ ବିଫଳ ଚେଷ୍ଟାର ହାସ୍ୟ ଥାଇପାରେ, କିମ୍ବା ପରିଚିତ ଜାଗାକୁ ଫେରିବାର ଭାବ।
entries.usage_example: After considering several meeting places, the group chooses its usual courtyard again. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The creature-name dhamana is retained without assigning a precise species. The courtyard supplies the image of return; no belief about animal behaviour or local origin is established.

entries.title: Work that does not move forward
entries.literal_meaning: The swollen-legged person digs; as much as they dig, so much they tread over.
entries.explanation: The image suggests effort whose result is undone as the work proceeds. It can be used for a task that stays unfinished because each advance is cancelled by another action. Its bodily caricature should be recognized rather than turned into a judgment about disabled people.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏକ ପଟେ କାମ ଆଗଉଛି, ଅନ୍ୟ ପଟେ ସେହି କାମ ପୁଣି ନଷ୍ଟ ହେଉଛି—ଏହି ଅସଂଗତିକୁ କଥାଟି ଧରେ। କରିଥିବା ପରିଶ୍ରମର ଫଳ ନିଜ ବା ଅନ୍ୟର କାମରେ ମାଟି ହୋଇଗଲେ ଏହି ଭାବ ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ପୁରୁଣା ଉପମାରେ ଶାରୀରିକ ଅବସ୍ଥାର ଉଲ୍ଲେଖ ଥିଲେ ବି ମଣିଷର ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟ ବିଷୟରେ ସେଥିରୁ ସାଧାରଣ ନିଷ୍କର୍ଷ ଟାଣିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A document is repeatedly reformatted, and each revision removes changes that the team had already agreed on. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Godara is rendered as the saying’s description of swollen legs, without diagnosing a medical condition. The interpretation concerns self-defeating work, not physical capacity or personal worth. The figurative explanation is an editorial interpretation, not a separately verified traditional gloss.

entries.meaning_odia: ମୂଳ ଆୟୋଜନ ହୋଇନାହିଁ, ଅଥଚ ବହୁତ ପରର କଥାର ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ସରିଲାଣି। ପୁଅର ନାଁ ଠିକ୍ କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଏହି ଅକାଳ ନିଶ୍ଚିତତାକୁ ହସି କୁହାଯାଇଛି। କାମର ପ୍ରଥମ ଶର୍ତ୍ତଟି ପୂରଣ ହେବା ଆଗରୁ ଶେଷ ଫଳକୁ ନିଜର ବୋଲି ଧରିନେବା ହିଁ ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ।

entries.title: An answer that reveals too much
entries.odia: ଠାକୁର ଘରେ କିଏ ରେ? ନାଁ ମୁଁ କଦଳୀ ଖାଇନାହିଁ
entries.literal_meaning: Who is in the shrine room? Well, I have not eaten the bananas.
entries.explanation: The question asks who is there, but the answer denies an act nobody mentioned. That unsolicited detail directs attention to the speaker’s possible concern. The humour comes from the mismatch between question and reply; a defensive answer alone does not establish guilt.
entries.meaning_odia: କେବଳ କିଏ ଅଛି ବୋଲି ପଚାରାଗଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ ଉତ୍ତରରେ କଦଳୀ ଖାଇବାର ଅସ୍ୱୀକାର ଆସିଲା। ଯେଉଁ କଥା ପଚରାଯାଇନଥିଲା, ତାହା ନିଜେ ଉଠାଇବାରୁ ମନର ଚିନ୍ତା ପଦାରେ ପଡ଼ିଲା। ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ସଫେଇର ମଜାକୁ ଏହା ଧରେ; ଏପରି ଉତ୍ତର ଏକାକୀ ଦୋଷର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: Resentment that harms oneself
entries.odia: ଘଇତା ପଛେ ମରୁ କିନ୍ତୁ ସଉତୁଣି ରାଣ୍ଡ ହେଉ!.
entries.literal_meaning: Let my husband die, so long as the co-wife becomes a widow.
entries.explanation: Spite becomes so strong that the speaker accepts a shared loss merely to hurt a rival. The deliberately harsh domestic scene exposes the cost of that desire. It is a criticism of destructive resentment, not a claim that women or co-wives naturally behave this way.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣଙ୍କ କ୍ଷତି ହେଉ ବୋଲି ଚାହିଁ ନିଜର ସେହି କ୍ଷତିକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଭୁଲିଯିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ରାଗ ବା ଈର୍ଷା ବିଚାରକୁ ଏତେ ଢାଙ୍କିଦିଏ ଯେ ନିଜ ହାନି ବି ଛୋଟ ଲାଗେ। ଘରୋଇ ସମ୍ପର୍କର ଏହି କଟୁ ଉପମାକୁ ସମସ୍ତ ନାରୀ ବା କୌଣସି ସମ୍ପର୍କର ସ୍ୱଭାବ ବୋଲି ନେବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Two groups refuse a shared resource because each would rather lose access than let the other benefit. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

Those gendered insults are part of the documented wording, not language the explanation endorses or a history of any particular household. entries.title: Familiarity that hides someone’s worth
entries.literal_meaning: The village bride is called runny-nosed.
entries.explanation: People who have known someone from everyday village life may dismiss that person instead of recognizing their qualities. The belittling description makes that dismissiveness audible. The saying can challenge a narrow local judgment without endorsing the insult directed at the bride.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅତି ପରିଚିତ ଲୋକର ଗୁଣ ଦେଖିବା ବଦଳରେ ତାଙ୍କ ପୁରୁଣା ବା ଛୋଟ ଦୋଷକୁ ମନେ ରଖାଯାଉଛି। ନିଜ ପାଖର ଲୋକକୁ ସହଜରେ ତୁଚ୍ଛ କରିବାର ଅଭ୍ୟାସକୁ ଏହି କଥା ଧରେ। ବୋହୂଙ୍କ ପ୍ରତି ଥିବା ଅପମାନଜନକ ଉପମାକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ ନକରି, ପରିଚୟ କିପରି ବିଚାରକୁ ପ୍ରଭାବିତ କରେ ସେଥିରେ ମନ ଦିଆଯାଇପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: A skilled local storyteller receives appreciation elsewhere while neighbours still speak only of childhood mistakes. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The literal image is gendered and dismissive. The editorial reading concerns undervaluing the familiar; neither a universal village custom nor the saying’s first historical use is known.

entries.title: Both share the fault
entries.odia: ଆଲୋ ମୁତୁରି ଶୋଇବା, ତୁ ମୁତୁରୀ କି ମୁଁ ମୁତୁରା ହେଂସ କାହିଁପାଇଁ ଧୋଇବା...!!!
entries.literal_meaning: Come, bed-wetter, let us sleep. Are you the bed-wetter, or am I? Why wash the mat?
entries.explanation: The licensed page places this crude joke in the situation of two people sharing the same fault. One possible reading is that their shared embarrassment lets both excuse leaving things as they are. The specific suggestion of mutual indulgence is an editorial interpretation; the witness does not supply a detailed explanation. This bodily image should not be used to shame someone with an actual condition.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୁଇ ଜଣଙ୍କର ଏକା ପ୍ରକାର ଅସୁବିଧା ଥିବାରୁ ସଜାଡ଼ିବାର କାମକୁ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବାର ଭାବ ଏଥିରୁ ନିଆଯାଇପାରେ। ଏହି ପାଠରେ ଜଣଙ୍କ ତ୍ରୁଟି ଆଉ ଜଣଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଅଜୁହାତ ହୋଇଯାଉଛି। ଏହା ଏକ ସୀମିତ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା; ଶାରୀରିକ ସମସ୍ୟା ଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଲଜ୍ଜିତ କରିବା ପାଇଁ ଉପମାଟି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: The same work, even in heaven
entries.odia: ଢିଙ୍କି ସ୍ୱର୍ଗକୁ ଗଲେ ବି ଧାନ କୁଟିବ
entries.literal_meaning: Even if the dhinki goes to heaven, it will still pound paddy.
entries.explanation: The joke gives a rice-pounding implement a grand change of address but leaves its work exactly as before. In conversation, it can tease someone who brings an old habit into a new setting, or express frustration that a change of place has changed nothing. The pointed contrast is between heaven and the same everyday task.
entries.meaning_odia: ଢିଙ୍କିର ଜାଗା ବଦଳିଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ ତାହାର ଧାନ କୁଟିବା କାମ ବଦଳିଲା ନାହିଁ। ପରିବେଶ ବଦଳିଲେ ବି ପୁରୁଣା ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ରହିଯିବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ କୁହାଯାଏ। ମଣିଷର କାମ ବା ଭବିଷ୍ୟତ ଜନ୍ମରୁ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ବୋଲି ନୁହେଁ, ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନ ସହ ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ବଦଳୁଛି କି ନାହିଁ ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଏଠାରେ ଉପଯୋଗୀ।
entries.usage_example: On a holiday, a friend immediately starts organising everyone’s timetable just as at work. Another friend uses the saying with a laugh. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Dhinki is retained as the name of the traditional rice-pounding implement; paddy is rice still in its husk. Heaven supplies the exaggerated destination. This reading does not turn an implement’s fixed function into a claim that people cannot change, or that anyone must remain in an inherited occupation.

entries.title: Making a small thing enormous
entries.literal_meaning: To make a palmyra fruit out of a sesame seed.
entries.explanation: A tiny seed is imagined as something much larger. The expression calls out exaggeration: a small mistake, slight or difficulty has been enlarged beyond proportion. Its force is a brisk objection to the scale of the telling, rather than a claim that the original problem did not exist.
entries.meaning_odia: ତିଳ ପରି ଛୋଟ କଥାକୁ ତାଳ ପରି ବଡ଼ କରି ଦେଖାଇବା ହିଁ ଏହି ରୂଢ଼ିର ଚିତ୍ର। ଘଟଣାର ଆକାରଠାରୁ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ବହୁତ ବଡ଼ ହୋଇଗଲେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଏ। ତଥାପି କାହାର ଚିନ୍ତାକୁ ନଶୁଣି କେବଳ ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଉଡ଼ାଇଦେବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A message arrives a few minutes late, but its recipient retells the delay as though the entire gathering nearly failed. A friend asks them not to make so much of it. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The compact sound-pair ତିଳ and ତାଳ carries the jump in scale. The English rendering takes ତାଳ as the palmyra fruit; the short witness does not spell out that referent, so this lexical choice remains for fluent-reader review. The explanation should not be used to dismiss another person’s distress without understanding it.

entries.title: More oil for an already oiled head
entries.literal_meaning: Oil on an already oiled head.
entries.explanation: The extra oil goes where there is already oil. Used socially, the image questions giving still more attention, help or advantage to someone already well provided for, while others go without. It can sound wry or resentful, depending on who is speaking and how the benefit is being distributed.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆଗରୁ ତେଲ ଥିବା ମୁଣ୍ଡରେ ପୁଣି ତେଲ ପଡ଼ୁଛି, ଆଉ ଯେଉଁଠି ଅଭାବ ସେଠି ନୁହେଁ। ସୁବିଧା ଓ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଆଗରୁ ସୁବିଧା ପାଇଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପାଖକୁ ଯିବାକୁ ଏହା ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରେ। କିଏ ଆଉ ପାଉଛି ମାତ୍ର ନୁହେଁ, କିଏ ବଞ୍ଚିତ ରହିଯାଉଛି ସେହି କଥା ବି ଭାବିବାକୁ ହୁଏ।

entries.cultural_context: The head and oil remain the material image; no named oiling ritual, caste practice or historical incident is implied. The emphasis here is advantage being added to advantage. Other conversational uses, including praise directed at powerful people, need their own context rather than being treated as the only meaning.

entries.meaning_odia: ମୁହଁରେ ଅସନ୍ତୋଷ ଚାଲିଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ମିଳୁଥିବା ଲାଭକୁ ଛାଡ଼ିବାର ଇଚ୍ଛା ନାହିଁ। ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଓ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରିବାର ଏହି ଯୁଗଳ ଆଚରଣକୁ କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ। କହୁଥିବା କଥା ସହ କରୁଥିବା କାମକୁ ମେଳାଇ ଦେଖିଲେ ଏହାର ମଜା ବୁଝାପଡ଼େ।
entries.usage_example: A guest calls every gift inadequate but carefully packs them all to take home. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

entries.literal_meaning: Call me Ganga and I will stay; call me Gangi and I will leave.
entries.explanation: A change in address changes the reception. The contrast can tease someone who insists on a particular form of respect.

entries.literal_meaning: You married that same husband, after letting the years pass!
entries.explanation: After prolonged delay, the eventual choice is the one available before. The jibe targets the wasted interval.

entries.odia: ତୁଛାକୁ ଏତେ ନା ମୁଦି ନାହିଁ ଗୋଡ଼ କଛାଡୁ କେତେ ।
entries.literal_meaning: Such a fuss over nothing: no ring, yet so much stamping of the feet.
entries.explanation: An exaggerated display outruns what there is to display. The source gloss connects it with being agitated over nothing.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦେଖାଇବାକୁ ଜିନିଷ ନଥାଇ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହାର ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର ବହୁତ। ମୁଦିର ଉଲ୍ଲେଖ ସେହି ଖାଲି ଦେଖାଣିକୁ ଧରିବାର ଏକ ଛବି। କଥା ଓ ହାବଭାବ ପଛରେ ପ୍ରକୃତରେ କଣ ଅଛି, ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବା ବେଳେ ଏହି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ଖାପ ଖାଏ।
entries.usage_example: A group celebrates a project so loudly that nobody notices it has not yet begun. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

entries.meaning_odia: ମିଳିମିଶି ବିଚାର କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ମତକୁ ଏଠାରେ ବଡ଼ ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦିଆଯାଇଛି। ଏକାକୀ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନେବା ବଦଳରେ ଅନ୍ୟଙ୍କ କଥା ଶୁଣିବାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଏଥିରୁ ବୁଝାଯାଇପାରେ। ତେବେ ଅନେକ ଜଣ କହିଲେ ମାତ୍ର ସେହି କଥା ସବୁବେଳେ ସତ୍ୟ ବା ନ୍ୟାୟସଂଗତ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।

entries.title: Tears that conceal support
entries.odia: ଚୋର ମା ଯଦି କାନ୍ଦେ ଆଖି ମଳିମଳି କାନ୍ଦେ ।
entries.literal_meaning: If the thief’s mother cries, she cries rubbing her eyes.
entries.explanation: The source reads the display of distress as concealed support for a wrongdoer. The charge is complicity behind appearances, not proof that a crying relative is guilty.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୁଃଖ ପ୍ରକାଶ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ନିଜର ସମ୍ପୃକ୍ତି ଗୋପନ ରହିଛି—ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହି ବିରୋଧାଭାସକୁ ଧରେ। ବାହାରର କାନ୍ଦଣା ଓ ଭିତରର ଜାଣିବା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଫାଙ୍କ ଥିଲେ କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ହୋଇଉଠେ। କିନ୍ତୁ କାନ୍ଦୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ବା ଅଭିଯୁକ୍ତଙ୍କ ଆତ୍ମୀୟ ହେବା ନିଜେ ଦୋଷର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Someone publicly deplores a friend’s deception while privately helping conceal it. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The maternal figure belongs to the saying; responsibility cannot be inferred from kinship or tears alone.

entries.literal_meaning: A shameless show-off: no betel leaf, no areca nut, only an empty pouch!
entries.explanation: The accessory promises substance that is absent. The source gloss identifies shameless outward boasting.
entries.meaning_odia: ଥଳିର ସଜସଜ୍ଜା ଦିଶୁଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଦେବା ପାଇଁ ଭିତରେ ପାନଗୁଆ ନାହିଁ। ବାହାରର ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର ସହ ଭିତରର ଅଭାବକୁ ଏକାଠି ରଖି କଥାଟି ମଜା କରେ। ଦେଖାଣି ଅପେକ୍ଷା ପ୍ରକୃତ ସମ୍ବଳ ମୁଖ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଯାଇପାରେ; ଆରମ୍ଭର ସବୁ ଶବ୍ଦର ସୂକ୍ଷ୍ମ ଅର୍ଥ ଏଠାରେ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A lavish brochure advertises a service that nobody can actually provide. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The betel pouch supplies the contrast. “Show-off” renders the source’s overall sense; the colloquial opening is not independently glossed word by word.

entries.title: The wrong process cannot make gold
entries.odia: କୁହାଯାଉଥାଇ ସିନା, ତୁହାଇ ତୁହାଇ ପୁଟ ଦେଲେ କାହିଁ, ଲୁହା କି ହୋଇବ ସୁନା
entries.literal_meaning: People may keep saying it, but will repeated firing turn iron into gold?
entries.explanation: Repeating a process does not ensure the transformation wanted. This editorial reading questions an unsuitable method, not anyone’s capacity to learn.
entries.meaning_odia: ଲୁହାକୁ ବାରମ୍ବାର ତତାଇଲେ ବି ସେ ସୁନା ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଏକା ଉପାୟକୁ ଦୋହରାଇବା ମାତ୍ରେ ଇଚ୍ଛାମତେ ଫଳ ମିଳିବ ବୋଲି ଭାବିବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ। କାମର ଉପାୟ ବଦଳାଇବା ଦରକାର କି ନାହିଁ, ସେଥିରେ ମନ ଦେବା ଉପଯୋଗୀ; ମଣିଷ ଶିଖିପାରେନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଏହାକୁ ଟାଣିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Reformatting an inaccurate report cannot make its facts reliable. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: A metalworking image, not a claim of innate human rank or an instruction for processing metals.

entries.title: Remembering a rescue
entries.odia: ଭାସି ଯାଉଥିଲୁ ମଝିନଇରେ ଧରି ଆଣିଥିଲି ତତେ, ଠାକୁଆ ଗାଲରେ ମାଉଁଶ ଲାଗିଲା ଜବାବ ଦେଉଛୁ ମତେ
entries.literal_meaning: I pulled you from the river; now your hollow cheeks have filled out and you answer me back.
entries.explanation: The speaker resents defiance from someone previously helped. The rescue creates the contrast between former dependence and present confidence.
entries.meaning_odia: ବିପଦରୁ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରିବା ପରେ ଓଲଟା କଠୋର କଥା ଶୁଣିବାରୁ ଉପକାରୀଙ୍କ କ୍ଷୋଭ ଜାଗିଛି। ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଓ ମିଳିଥିବା ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟାର ଅମେଳକୁ କଥାଟି ଧରେ। ଅପମାନର ଅଭିଯୋଗ ବୁଝିହେବ, କିନ୍ତୁ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ପାଇଥିବା ଲୋକ ସବୁବେଳେ ଆଜ୍ଞା ମାନିବାକୁ ବାଧ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A mentor complains when a former trainee openly challenges a decision. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Editorial interpretation of an unglossed witness. Receiving help does not remove a person’s right to disagree.

entries.odia: ରାଧା କହିଲେ ଦୂତୀ କି, ଯାହା ହେଇଚି ସେତିକି...!!!
entries.literal_meaning: Radha told the messenger: what has happened is that much.
entries.explanation: A resigned response when events have become difficult to contain: further words cannot undo what has occurred.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାହା ହୋଇଯାଇଛି, ତାହାକୁ କେବଳ କଥାରେ ଫେରାଇହେବ ନାହିଁ—ଏମିତି ଏକ ନିରୁପାୟ ସ୍ୱର ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି। ଅନୁତାପ ବା ପଛରୁ କଥା କହିବା ଫଳକୁ ବଦଳାଉନଥିବା ବେଳେ ଏହା ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ପଛର କଥା କହିଲେ ବି ଘଟିଯାଇଥିବା କାମ ଆଗରେ ମଣିଷ କେତେ ଅସହାୟ ଲାଗିପାରେ, ସେହି ସ୍ୱର ଏଠାରେ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: After an announcement has already gone out, arguing over the unsent draft no longer changes it. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source invokes Radha and a female messenger but names no underlying poem or episode; none is supplied here.

entries.literal_meaning: The liquor seller’s witness is the drunk!
entries.explanation: The supposed witness has a connection to the person being defended. The pointed question is whether that testimony is independent.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାହାଙ୍କୁ ସାକ୍ଷୀ କରାଯାଉଛି, ସେ ନିଜେ ସେହି କାମରେ ଜଡ଼ିତ—ଏହି ଅସୁବିଧାକୁ କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ। ଏକା ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥ ଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ କଥାକୁ ସ୍ୱାଧୀନ ପ୍ରମାଣ ଭାବେ ନେବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ବିଚାର ଦରକାର। ଏହା ସାକ୍ଷ୍ୟର ସମ୍ପର୍କ ବିଷୟରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ, କୌଣସି ପେଶାର ସବୁ ଲୋକ ଅସତ୍ୟ କହନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଦାବି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A seller cites only their business partner as proof of a product’s quality. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The occupational caricature is not evidence about any community’s honesty. Shared interests invite scrutiny, not automatic disbelief.

entries.literal_meaning: The lizard’s dash is to the siju bush!
entries.explanation: The source uses the short dash to mock a narrow range of thought. Much motion may still lead only to a familiar answer.
entries.meaning_odia: ବହୁତ ହଲଚଲ ଥିଲେ ବି ଶେଷରେ ଚିନ୍ତା ସେହି ଛୋଟ ପରିସରରେ ଅଟକି ରହୁଛି। ଏଣ୍ଡୁଅ ଓ ସିଜୁବୁଦାର ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଏହି ସୀମିତ ଘୂରଣକୁ ଦେଖାଯାଇଛି। ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ ରହିବା ଓ ଦୃଷ୍ଟିକୋଣ ବଢ଼ିବା ଏକ ନୁହେଁ; ଏହାକୁ କାହାର ଜନ୍ମଗତ ବୁଦ୍ଧିର ମାପ ବୋଲି ନେବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.cultural_context: Siju is retained as the plant name. This is a figurative reading, not a zoological claim or a judgment of fixed intelligence.

entries.odia: କାଣୀ ବିରାଡ଼ି କୁଜି ଅସରପା ଉପରେ ରଜା
entries.literal_meaning: The one-eyed cat is king over the bent-backed cockroach.
entries.explanation: Even a limited power can dominate a weaker opponent. The contrast makes that small kingdom look less impressive.
entries.meaning_odia: ନିଜେ ଦୁର୍ବଳ ସ୍ଥିତିରେ ଥାଇ ବି ଆହୁରି ଦୁର୍ବଳଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ପ୍ରଭୁତ୍ୱ ଦେଖାଇବାକୁ କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ। ନିଜ ସୀମା ଭୁଲି ଅନ୍ୟକୁ ଛୋଟ କରିବାର ଆଚରଣ ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ। ଉପମାରେ ଥିବା ଦୃଷ୍ଟି ବା ଶରୀରର ତଫାତକୁ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: Living with the jolts
entries.odia: ଅଖ ବୁଲୁଥିଲେ ଚକ ବୁଲୁଥାଏ, ବୁଲି ପଡୁଥାଏ ମହି, ସଂସାର ଭିତରେ ଘର କରିଥିଲେ ପଥର ପଡ଼ିଲେ ସହି ।
entries.literal_meaning: The axle turns, the wheel turns, the earth turns; having made a home in the world, endure even falling stones.
entries.explanation: The movement of ordinary life leads into counsel to withstand hardship. Endurance is the proposed response to unavoidable jolts.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଖ ଓ ଚକର ଚଳଣି ସହ ଜୀବନର ଟାଣ ଓ କଷ୍ଟକୁ ମେଳାଯାଇଛି। ଚଳିବାକୁ ହେଲେ କିଛି ଅସୁବିଧା ସମ୍ଭାଳିବାକୁ ପଡ଼େ—ଏହି ସହନଶୀଳତାର ଭାବ କଥାଟିରେ ଅଛି। ତେବେ ଏଡ଼ାଇହେବା ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ବା ନିର୍ଯାତନାକୁ ଜୀବନର ନିୟମ କହି ସହିବା ପାଇଁ ଏହାକୁ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: After a storm delays a harvest, a family steadies itself and plans the remaining work. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Editorial interpretation of an unglossed verse. Endurance does not require accepting abuse or preventable harm.

entries.odia: ଗଂଗାଦି ନାନା ତୀର୍ଥ ନିକଟେ ଥାଇଣ ଚାତକ, ଜଳଦ ଜଳ ଟୋପେକୁ ଆଶ୍ରାକରି ଅବିରତେ ତୃଷୀକ
entries.literal_meaning: Near the Ganga and other sacred waters, the chataka remains thirsty, depending on a drop from a cloud.
entries.explanation: The verse pictures longing fixed on one source despite alternatives nearby. It may evoke steadfast desire; context determines whether that seems admirable or impractical.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚାରିପଟେ ପାଣି ଥିଲେ ବି ଚାତକର ଆଶା ମେଘ ପାଖରେ—ଏହା ଏକମୁଖୀ ଆକାଂକ୍ଷାର ଚିତ୍ର। ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗ ଅନୁସାରେ ସେହି ଅପେକ୍ଷା ନିଷ୍ଠା ଭଳି ଲାଗିପାରେ, ପୁଣି ହାତରେ ଥିବା ସୁଯୋଗକୁ ଅଣଦେଖା କରିବା ଭଳି ବି। କାହା ପାଇଁ କିମ୍ବା କେଉଁ ଆଶାରେ ଅପେକ୍ଷା, ତାହା ବୁଝିଲେ ଏହି ସାହିତ୍ୟିକ ଚିତ୍ରର ଅର୍ଥ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ହୁଏ।
entries.usage_example: A musician declines several engagements while waiting for the invitation that matters most to them. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Read as a literary bird-image, not a claim about a species’ drinking habits. The page names no author or originating work.

entries.title: The catch and the meal differ
entries.literal_meaning: The Keuta catches fish but eats crab.
entries.explanation: The contrast suggests that producing something does not ensure enjoying it oneself. The line can point to a gap between someone’s work and their own circumstances.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯିଏ ମାଛ ଯୋଗାଉଛନ୍ତି, ତାଙ୍କ ନିଜ ଭାଗରେ ସେହି ଭଲ ଜିନିଷ ନପଡ଼ିବାର ବିରୋଧାଭାସ ଏଠାରେ ଅଛି। ଉତ୍ପାଦନ ବା ପରିଶ୍ରମ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ନିଜ ଶ୍ରମର ସୁଫଳ ଉପଭୋଗ କରୁଛନ୍ତି କି ନାହିଁ, ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଏଥିରୁ ଉଠେ। ଏହାକୁ କେଉଟ ସମୁଦାୟର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଖାଦ୍ୟାଭ୍ୟାସର ବିବରଣୀ ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଇନାହିଁ।

entries.title: Refusing what is freely offered
entries.odia: ମାଗି ଖାଉଥାଏ ବାସି ତୋଡ଼ାଣି, ଯାଚିଲେ ନ ଖାଏ ସର ଲବଣୀ
entries.literal_meaning: They ask for stale rice-water to eat, yet refuse cream and butter when offered.
entries.explanation: The contrast mocks a refusal that appears at odds with what someone usually seeks. An unsolicited offer is rejected despite being presented as more desirable.
entries.meaning_odia: ନିଜେ ମାଗି ବାସି ତୋଡ଼ାଣି ବି ଖାଉଛନ୍ତି, ହେଲେ ଆଦରରେ ଦିଆଯାଇଥିବା ସର ଲବଣୀକୁ ମନା କରୁଛନ୍ତି। ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ଓ ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟାର ଏହି ଅମେଳରେ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ଅଛି। କଥାଟି ଅସଂଗତ ମନା କରିବାକୁ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରେ; କାହାର ଖାଦ୍ୟ ନେବାକୁ ମନା କରିବାର ଅଧିକାରକୁ ନାକଚ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Someone repeatedly asks to borrow basic tools but declines a better set freely offered by a neighbour. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary explicitly labels this a dhaga under offering something. Rice-water interprets the witness spelling ତୋଡ଼ାଣି without changing it. The saying does not explain why the offer is refused; consent and personal preference remain valid.

entries.title: A dramatic farewell
entries.odia:
ଛାଡ଼ ଅଞ୍ଚଳ ମହାବାହୁ...
ଏ ଜନ୍ମେ ଭେଟ ନାହିଁ ଆଉ...!!!
entries.literal_meaning: Let go of my garment’s end, mighty-armed one; in this life we shall meet no more.
entries.explanation: The source places this farewell under distress that feels unbearable. Its absolute language gives the parting a dramatic finality.
entries.meaning_odia: ବିଦାୟ ବା ବିଚ୍ଛେଦର ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତକୁ ବଡ଼ ଆବେଗରେ କହିବାର ଢଙ୍ଗ ଏହା। ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବାର ଅନୁରୋଧରେ ମନର ଟାଣ ଓ ଦୁଃଖ ଏକାଠି ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ସାଧାରଣ ବିଦାୟର କଥାଠାରୁ ଏହାର ଆବେଗ ବଡ଼, ତେଣୁ ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଓ କହିବାର ଭଙ୍ଗୀ ସହ ତାହାକୁ ଶୁଣିବାକୁ ହୁଏ।
entries.usage_example: A performer uses the line to portray a wounded character’s farewell; the scene is newly imagined. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The witness names no underlying song or episode. Mahabahu is rendered literally; no particular speaker or deity is assigned.

entries.title: The fire nobody sees
entries.odia: ବଣ ପୋଡ଼ିଲେ ଦୁନିଆ ଜାଣେ, ମନ ପୋଡ଼ିଲେ କେହୀ ନ ଜାଣେ
entries.literal_meaning: When a forest burns, the world knows; when the heart burns, no one knows.
entries.explanation: Visible calamity draws attention; private grief can remain unnoticed. The contrast asks the listener to recognise pain that has no outward blaze.
entries.meaning_odia: ବଣରେ ନିଆଁ ଲାଗିଲେ ବାହାରୁ ଦିଶେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ମନର ଜ୍ୱାଳା ସେମିତି ଦିଶେନାହିଁ। ବାହାରେ ସାଧାରଣ ଦିଶୁଥିବା ଜଣଙ୍କ ଭିତରେ ବି ଗଭୀର କଷ୍ଟ ଥାଇପାରେ। ଏହି ତୁଳନା ଆମକୁ ଦେଖାଯାଉଥିବା ଚେହେରାରୁ ସବୁ କଥା ଧରିନନେବାକୁ ମନେ ପକାଏ।
entries.usage_example: A neighbour appears composed at work while privately grieving a loss. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary places this under mental distress. “No one” is the saying’s emphatic contrast, not a claim that support is impossible.

entries.title: A year lost and a life affected
entries.odia: ଚଷା ହୁଡ଼ିଲେ ବରଷେ, ମଣିଷ ହୁଡିଲେ ପୁରୁଷେ
entries.literal_meaning: If the cultivator goes wrong, a year is lost; if a person goes wrong, a lifetime.
entries.explanation: A seasonal mistake is contrasted with a decision that can shape a life. The warning concerns the scale of consequences, not the impossibility of recovery.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚାଷର ଭୁଲ୍ର ଫଳ ବର୍ଷକ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଲାଗିପାରେ, ମଣିଷର କେତେକ ଭୁଲ୍ ଆହୁରି ଦୀର୍ଘ ସମୟ ପ୍ରଭାବ ପକାଇପାରେ—ଏହି ତଫାତ କଥାଟିରେ ଅଛି। ଉତ୍ସର ଏହି ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ‘ପୁରୁଷେ’ ଜୀବନକାଳର ଅର୍ଥ ବହନ କରେ। ଦୂର ପରିଣାମ ଭାବିବା ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ; ଭୁଲ୍ ହେଲେ ଆଉ ସୁଧାରିବାର ବାଟ ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Before making a lasting commitment, someone pauses to consider consequences beyond the present season. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The cited sense defines ପୁରୁଷ as lifetime, not generation. ଚଷା is read in the farming image; no caste-wide trait is asserted.

entries.explanation: Something impressive to one person may be ordinary to someone with easy access. The rhetorical question puts the proposed treat in perspective.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜଣଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଖଜା ବହୁତ ଲୋଭନୀୟ ହୋଇପାରେ, ହେଲେ ସହଜରେ ତାହା ପାଉଥିବା ଜଣଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ସେତେ ବିଶେଷ ନୁହେଁ। ସମାନ ଜିନିଷକୁ ନେଇ ଆଗ୍ରହ କାହିଁକି ଅଲଗା ହୁଏ, ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ସେହି ତଫାତକୁ ଧରେ। ନିଜକୁ ଯାହା ସାଧାରଣ ଲାଗେ, ଆଉ ଜଣଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ତାହା ବଡ଼ ଆକର୍ଷଣ ହୋଇପାରେ।

entries.odia: ରଜାର ପ୍ରଜା ନୁହେଁ କି ସାହୁର ଖାତକ ନୁହେଁ
entries.literal_meaning: Neither the king’s subject nor the moneylender’s debtor.
entries.explanation: The speaker presents themself as independent and free of debt. It is a forceful refusal to be treated as someone under another’s control.
entries.meaning_odia: ମୁଁ ତୁମର ଅଧୀନ ନୁହେଁ, ତୁମ ପାଖରେ ଋଣୀ ବି ନୁହେଁ—ଏହି ଢଙ୍ଗରେ ନିଜ ସ୍ୱାଧୀନତା ଘୋଷଣା କରାଯାଇଛି। ଅକାରଣ ଆଦେଶ ବା ଚାପକୁ ମାନିବାକୁ ମନା କରିବା ବେଳେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ରାଜା ଓ ସାହୁକାରର ତୁଳନା ସେହି ମନା କରିବାକୁ ଜୋର୍ ଦିଏ; ବକ୍ତା କାହିଁକି ନିଜକୁ ବାଧ୍ୟ ମନେ କରୁନାହାନ୍ତି, ତାହା କହୁଛନ୍ତି।
entries.usage_example: A self-supporting craftsperson rejects a patron’s attempt to dictate a personal decision. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary gloss supports independence and absence of debt. This is figurative self-assertion, not a legal exemption from obligations.

entries.literal_meaning: An obtuse king.
entries.explanation: A curt, rhyming criticism of a ruler’s awkward understanding. Authority has not brought good judgment.
entries.meaning_odia: କ୍ଷମତା ଅଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ତାହାକୁ ଚଳାଇବାର ବିଚାର ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଅମେଳକୁ ଛୋଟ କଟାକ୍ଷଟି ଧରେ। ଦାୟିତ୍ୱର ସ୍ଥାନରେ ଥାଇ ବି ନିର୍ବୋଧ ଭଳି କାମ କଲେ ଏହି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ହୋଇପାରେ। ପଦବୀର ଓଜନ ଅଛି ବୋଲି ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତିରେ ବିଚାର ଅଛି, ଏମିତି ଧରିନେବାକୁ କଥାଟି ଦିଏନାହିଁ।

entries.explanation: Poor leadership is compounded by equally foolish advice. The pairing, rather than the ruler alone, is the target.
entries.meaning_odia: ନେତୃତ୍ୱରେ ବିଚାରର ଅଭାବ, ପରାମର୍ଶରେ ବି ସାର ନାହିଁ—ଦୁଇଟି ଦୁର୍ବଳତା ଏକାଠି ହୋଇଛି। ସୁବିଚାରପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ପରାମର୍ଶର ଅଭାବରୁ ଭୁଲ୍ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ଆହୁରି ବିଗିଡ଼ୁଥିବା ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ। ପଦବୀ ଥିବା ଓ ସେହି ପଦର କାମ ଠିକ୍ ଭାବେ କରିବା ଅଲଗା କଥା।
entries.usage_example: An ill-planned proposal survives because the person asked to assess it understands it no better. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Straw-bundle is a belittling image. The source gloss explicitly describes a foolish adviser to an unjust ruler.

entries.title: Trading alongside a prince
entries.literal_meaning: The folly of dried-fish trading with a prince.
entries.explanation: A person with fewer resources can suffer by joining someone whose means are much greater. The warning concerns an unequal undertaking.
entries.meaning_odia: ବଡ଼ ସମ୍ବଳ ଥିବା ଜଣଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଯେଉଁ କାମର ବିପଦ ଅଳ୍ପ, ଅଳ୍ପ ସମ୍ବଳର ଜଣଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ସେହି ବିପଦ ବଡ଼ ହୋଇପାରେ। ରାଜପୁତ୍ର ଓ ବ୍ୟବସାୟର ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଏହି ଅସମାନ ସ୍ଥିତିକୁ ଭାବିହେବ। ମୁଖ୍ୟ କଥା ସମ୍ବଳ ଓ କ୍ଷତି ସମ୍ଭାଳିବାର ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟ, ଜନ୍ମରୁ କିଏ ବଡ଼ ବା ଛୋଟ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.literal_meaning: Is the marriage arranged by looking at the household, or at the groom?
entries.explanation: The question contrasts a family’s standing with the individual being considered for marriage. It exposes two different ways of judging a match.
entries.meaning_odia: ବିବାହରେ ପରିବାରର ସ୍ଥିତିକୁ ଦେଖିବା ଓ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିକୁ ଦେଖିବା—ଏହି ଦୁଇ ଦୃଷ୍ଟିକୋଣକୁ କଥାଟି ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖେ। କେଉଁ ଗୁଣକୁ ଆଗରେ ରଖାଯାଉଛି, ସେଥିରୁ ପସନ୍ଦର ତଫାତ ହୋଇପାରେ। ଏହା ଏକ ଲିପିବଦ୍ଧ ବିଚାରଧାରାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ; ଆଜି କାହାର ସଙ୍ଗୀ ବାଛିବାର ନିୟମ ଭାବେ ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A discussion of a prospective marriage dwells on the family name while saying little about the person. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary places ଘର under high family. That records a status-conscious setting, not an endorsement of inherited rank; the saying does not establish either person’s consent.

entries.meaning_odia: ମାଘର ଶୀତକୁ ବାଘ ସହ ତୁଳନା କରି ତାହାର ପ୍ରଚଣ୍ଡତା ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି। ‘ମାଘ’ ଓ ‘ବାଘ’ର ମିଳ ଥଣ୍ଡାର ଅନୁଭବକୁ ସହଜରେ ମନେ ରଖାଏ। ଏହା ଶୀତର ଜୋର୍ କହିବାର ଢଙ୍ଗ, ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ବର୍ଷ ବା ସବୁ ଜାଗାର ପାଗର ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.literal_meaning: Cold in Magha, cold under clouds; wherever wind, there cold.
entries.explanation: A rhythmic reply names occasions when cold is felt.
entries.meaning_odia: କେବେ ଶୀତ ଲାଗେ ବୋଲି ପଚାରିଲେ ମାସ, ମେଘ ଓ ପବନକୁ ନେଇ ଏହି ଛନ୍ଦମୟ ଉତ୍ତର ଆସେ। ଅନୁଭବକୁ ଏକ ଲୟରେ ସଜାଇ କହିବାରୁ କଥାଟି ଶୁଣିବା ଓ ମନେ ରଖିବା ସହଜ। ଏହା ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ଅନୁଭବର କଥନ, ପାଣିପାଗ ବିଜ୍ଞାନର ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: The art of saying it well
entries.odia: କହି ଜାଣିଲେ କଥା ସୁନ୍ଦର ବାନ୍ଧି ଜାଣିଲେ ମଥା ସୁନ୍ଦର
entries.literal_meaning: Know how to speak, and words are beautiful; know how to arrange hair, and the head is beautiful.
entries.explanation: How something is done matters. Well-chosen words are compared with hair arranged by a practised hand.
entries.meaning_odia: କେଶକୁ ଭଲରେ ସଜାଇଲେ ମଥା ସୁନ୍ଦର ଦିଶେ, ସେମିତି ଶବ୍ଦ ବାଛି କହିଲେ କଥା ଭଲ ଲାଗେ। ବିଷୟ ସହ ତାହା କହିବାର ଢଙ୍ଗ ବି ଶ୍ରୋତାଙ୍କ ଅନୁଭବକୁ ପ୍ରଭାବିତ କରେ। ମିଠା କଥା କହିବା ମାତ୍ର ନୁହେଁ, ଉଚିତ ଶବ୍ଦ ଓ ଉଚିତ ଭଙ୍ଗୀର କୌଶଳ ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ।

entries.title: Little rest, many troubles
entries.odia: ଅଳପ ନିଦକୁ ବହୁତ କଥା, ଝୁରିମରିବାକୁ କଲା ବିଧାତା
entries.literal_meaning: Little sleep, so much happening; fate has made me pine away.
entries.explanation: A weary complaint that troubles leave little rest. The exaggerated lament carries the feeling of being overwhelmed.
entries.meaning_odia: ବିଶ୍ରାମ ପାଇଁ ସମୟ ଅଳ୍ପ, ଅଥଚ ଚିନ୍ତା ଓ ଘଟଣାର ଶେଷ ନାହିଁ। ଏହି କ୍ଲାନ୍ତିକୁ ବକ୍ତା ଭାଗ୍ୟର ଦୋଷ ଦେଇ ବଡ଼ ଅଭିଯୋଗରେ କହୁଛନ୍ତି। ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତିଟି ମନର ଭାରକୁ ବୁଝାଏ, ଜୀବନ ସବୁବେଳେ ଏପରି ରହିବ ବୋଲି ଭବିଷ୍ୟବାଣୀ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: After several demanding days, someone sighs that even bedtime brings another worry. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

entries.explanation: A brief occasion can leave a lasting impression, good or bad. Its memory outlasts the meal.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭୋଜନର ଅବସରଟି ଦିନକର, କିନ୍ତୁ ସେଠାରେ ହୋଇଥିବା ଭଲମନ୍ଦ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ସ୍ମୃତି ବହୁଦିନ ରହିପାରେ। ଆୟୋଜନର ଅବଧି ଓ ତାହାର ପ୍ରଭାବର ଅବଧି ଏକ ନୁହେଁ। ତେଣୁ ସେହି ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତରେ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ସହ କିପରି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରାଗଲା, ସେ କଥା ଖାଦ୍ୟ ସରିବା ପରେ ବି ମନେ ରହେ।

entries.title: The crow eats; someone else is blamed
entries.odia: କଥାର ମଞ୍ଜି, କୁଆ ଧାନ ଖାଏ ବୋହୁକୁ ଗଞ୍ଜି
entries.literal_meaning: The kernel of the matter: the crow eats the paddy, but the daughter-in-law is scolded.
entries.explanation: Blame falls on someone other than the one responsible. The contrast exposes how unfair that is.
entries.meaning_odia: ଧାନ ଖାଉଛି କାଉ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଗାଳି ଶୁଣୁଛନ୍ତି ବୋହୂ। ପ୍ରକୃତ କାରଣକୁ ନଦେଖି ସହଜରେ ଦୋଷ ଦେଇହେବା ଲୋକ ଉପରେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଲଦିବାର ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ। ଦୋଷ କାହା ଉପରେ ପଡ଼ୁଛି ଓ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟଟି କିଏ କରିଛି, ସେ ଦୁଇଟିକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଦେଖିବାକୁ ହୁଏ।
entries.usage_example: A shared file disappears because of a system fault, but a new colleague is blamed before anyone checks. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The household scene names a daughter-in-law as the target of blame. It is not a claim about every family or an endorsement of blaming women.

entries.title: That sounds like mockery to me
entries.odia: କଥା କହୁଥାଏ କେଉଁ ରସରେ, ମୋତେ ଲାଗୁଥାଏ ପରିହାସରେ
entries.literal_meaning: Whatever the manner of the speech, it feels like mockery to me.
entries.explanation: A listener hears ridicule, whatever the speaker intended. The contrast draws attention to how words are received.
entries.meaning_odia: କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ଭାବ ଯାହା ହେଉ, ଶୁଣୁଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ କଥାଟି ଥଟ୍ଟା ପରି ଲାଗୁଛି। କହିବାର ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ଓ ଶୁଣିବାର ଅନୁଭବ ଏକ ନହେବାରୁ ମନମାଳିନ୍ୟ ହୋଇପାରେ। ନିଜେ କଣ କହିବାକୁ ଚାହିଁଲୁ ମାତ୍ର ନୁହେଁ, ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣେ କିପରି ଶୁଣିଲେ ସେଥିରେ ବି ମନ ଦେବାର ଅବସର ଏହି କଥା ଦିଏ।

entries.title: Time slips away
entries.odia: ମାରି ମାରି ଗଲା କାଳକ ଆଉ ରହିଗଲା ଫାଳକ
entries.literal_meaning: Whiling it away, time has gone; a half remains.
entries.explanation: Time has passed while one was merely getting through it. The remaining half is a rhyming image, not a measured lifespan.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏମିତି ଦିନ କାଟୁକାଟୁ ବହୁତ ସମୟ ଚାଲିଗଲାଣି, ଆଉ ଯାହା ବାକି ତାହାର କଥା ମନେ ପଡ଼ୁଛି। ଗଡ଼ିଯାଇଥିବା ସମୟକୁ ପଛକୁ ଚାହିଁ ଦେଖିବାର ଭାବ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି। ‘ଫାଳକ’ ଛନ୍ଦର ଏକ ଚିତ୍ର; ଜୀବନର ଠିକ୍ ଅଧା ରହିଛି ବୋଲି ମାପ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: After postponing a task repeatedly, someone notices how much of the available time has passed. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
