entries.meaning_odia: ଝିଣ୍ଟିକାର କ୍ଷତିରୁ ବଣିର ପୋଷଣ ହେଉଛି—ଏହି ଦୁଇ ବିପରୀତ ଫଳକୁ କଥାଟି ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖେ। ଜଣଙ୍କ ଲାଭ ପାଇଁ ଆଉ ଜଣଙ୍କୁ କ୍ଷତି ସହିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ଏହି ଉପମା ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ଲାଭର କଥା ଶୁଣିବା ବେଳେ ତାହାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ କିଏ ଦେଉଛି, ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ବି ରହେ।

entries.title: Even river sand runs out
entries.literal_meaning: If one sits and consumes, even the river’s sand runs out.
entries.explanation: Even a large store can be exhausted if it is continually used without replenishment. The exaggerated sand image makes the scale of the reserve irrelevant.
entries.meaning_odia: ନଈର ବାଲି ପରି ପ୍ରଚୁର ଭଣ୍ଡାର ବି କେବଳ ବ୍ୟବହାର ହୋଇଚାଲିଲେ ସରିଯିବ ବୋଲି କୁହାଯାଇଛି। ବଡ଼ ସମ୍ବଳ ଅଛି ବୋଲି ତାହାର ଭରଣା ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ, ଏମିତି ନୁହେଁ। ଏଠାରେ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ଓ ଭରଣାର ସମ୍ପର୍କ ମୁଖ୍ୟ; କାମ କରିପାରୁନଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷ ଦେବା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A club repeatedly pays expenses from its reserve but collects no new contributions. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source places this under consuming savings without earning. It should not be used to blame people unable to work or to deny their need for support.

entries.title: Words travel farther than drums
entries.odia: ଚମବାଇଦ କୋଶେ, ତୁଣ୍ଡ ବାଇଦ ଶହସ୍ର କୋଶ
entries.literal_meaning: A hide-drum carries one kos; the mouth’s drum a thousand kos.
entries.explanation: News passed from person to person can spread much farther than a sound heard at its source. The contrast is deliberate exaggeration, not a measured claim about distance.
entries.meaning_odia: ଢୋଲର ଶବ୍ଦ ଏକ ଦୂରତା ପରେ ଶୁଣାଯାଏନାହିଁ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଲୋକମୁଖର କଥା ଜଣକଠାରୁ ଆଉ ଜଣକୁ ଯାଇଚାଲେ। ସେହିପାଇଁ ତୁଣ୍ଡର ବାଇଦକୁ ଅଧିକ ଦୂର ପହଞ୍ଚୁଥିବା କୁହାଯାଇଛି। ହଜାର କୋଶ ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତି; କଥା ଛାଡ଼ିବା ପରେ ତାହା କେତେ ଦୂର ଯାଇପାରେ ସେହି ଭାବଟି ମୁଖ୍ୟ।
entries.usage_example: A small announcement at a village gathering is being discussed in distant households the next day. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary’s sense1 is a report or rumour carried by word of mouth. The longer witness is retained; the discovery list gives only its latter idea.

entries.title: Measure farther than you step
entries.literal_meaning: Measure a cubit, then move a span.
entries.explanation: Examine more of the situation than the immediate step requires. The proverb recommends deliberation before acting; careful preparation can reduce risk without guaranteeing safety.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯେତିକି ଆଗକୁ ପାଦ ପକାଇବା, ତାଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ଦୂରର କଥା ଆଗେ ବିଚାର କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। ଛୋଟ ପଦକ୍ଷେପ ପଛରେ ସୁଚିନ୍ତିତ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ଥିଲେ ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ବିପଦ କମିପାରେ। ଏହା ସତର୍କ ବିଚାରର ପରାମର୍ଶ, ସବୁ ବିପଦ ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିହେବ ବୋଲି ନିଶ୍ଚିତତା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Before moving a workshop, its owners check access, costs and likely demand, then try a small temporary space. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary itself explains the longer measure and shorter step. These are traditional body-based measures; no fixed modern conversion is needed here.

entries.title: Harm from what was kept close
entries.literal_meaning: The knife tucked at the waist cuts the throat.
entries.explanation: Something or someone trusted and kept close becomes the source of harm. The dictionary puts the saying beside its figurative sense of cheating.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାହାକୁ ଭରସା କରି ନିଜ ପାଖରେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି, ସେହିଠାରୁ କ୍ଷତି ଆସୁଛି। ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ଛୁରିର ତୀବ୍ର ଚିତ୍ର ବିଶ୍ୱାସଭଙ୍ଗର ଆଘାତକୁ ବୁଝାଏ। ଏହା ଭରସା ଭାଙ୍ଗିବାର ଅନୁଭବ, ସମସ୍ତ ନିକଟ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ସନ୍ଦେହ କରିବାର ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A trusted business partner secretly diverts the shop’s receipts. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Violent imagery describes betrayal; it is not an instruction to harm anyone. The source does not establish a particular origin story.

entries.title: Do not delay a good beginning
entries.literal_meaning: For what is auspicious, promptly.
entries.explanation: Once a worthwhile action is decided, avoid needless delay. This is encouragement to begin, not a reason to abandon judgment or preparation.
entries.meaning_odia: କାମଟି ଭଲ ଓ କରିବାଯୋଗ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ହୋଇଗଲେ ଅକାରଣ ପକାଇ ନରଖିବାର ଉତ୍ସାହ ଏହା। କେବଳ ଭାବି ରହିବା ଓ ଆରମ୍ଭ କରିବା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଯେଉଁ ବିଳମ୍ବ, କଥାଟି ତାହାକୁ କମାଇବାକୁ କହେ। ଶୀଘ୍ର କାମ କରିବା ମାନେ ବିଚାର ବା ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ଛାଡ଼ିଦେବା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: After agreeing to repair the library’s leaking roof, the volunteers arrange the work promptly. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

entries.title: A pious appearance that deceives
entries.literal_meaning: A cat as a Vaishnava devotee.
entries.explanation: A show of devotion conceals conduct that contradicts it. The target is the mismatch between appearance and action, not believers as a group.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାହାରେ ଧାର୍ମିକ ବେଶ ଓ ଭକ୍ତିର ଦେଖାଣି, ଭିତରେ ତାହାର ବିପରୀତ ଆଚରଣ। ରୂପ ଓ କାମର ଏହି ଅମେଳକୁ ବିରାଡ଼ିର ଉପମାରେ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରାଯାଇଛି। କପଟକୁ ଚିହ୍ନିବା ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ, କୌଣସି ଧର୍ମର ସବୁ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଏକା ଭାବେ ଦେଖିବା ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: Each place has its own ways
entries.literal_meaning: Each place has its particular ways; each river has its bends.
entries.explanation: A way of doing things that feels ordinary in one place may differ elsewhere. The river image makes local variation easy to picture. The saying invites attention to the place you are in, without declaring every local practice beyond question.
entries.meaning_odia: ନଈର ବାଙ୍କ ଏକା ପରି ନୁହେଁ, ସେମିତି ସବୁ ଅଞ୍ଚଳର ରୀତି ବି ଏକା ପରି ନୁହେଁ। ନିଜ ଜାଗାରେ ସ୍ୱାଭାବିକ ଲାଗୁଥିବା କଥା ଅନ୍ୟଠାରେ ଅଲଗା ହୋଇପାରେ। ନୂଆ ଜାଗାରେ ନିଜ ଅଭ୍ୟାସକୁ ଏକମାତ୍ର ମାପକ ନକରି ସେଠାର ଚଳଣି ବୁଝିବାର ମନ ଦରକାର। ତଥାପି ସ୍ଥାନୀୟ ରୀତି ହେଲେ ତାହାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିହେବ ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A visitor notices that a neighbouring village arranges its shared meal differently and asks how the local arrangement works. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The example appears under locality in the dictionary. A separate lexical entry gives particular and differing customs among the senses of ଫାଙ୍କ; that supports the reading used here.

entries.odia_summary: ସବୁ ଅଞ୍ଚଳର ରୀତି ଏକା ପରି ନୁହେଁ; ନଈର ବାଙ୍କ ପରି ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ସ୍ଥାନର ନିଜସ୍ୱ ଢଙ୍ଗ ଅଛି। ଏହା ସ୍ଥାନୀୟ ଚଳଣି ବୁଝିବାକୁ କହେ, ସବୁ ରୀତିକୁ ନିର୍ବିଚାରରେ ମାନିନେବାକୁ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Each place has its own ways, like each river its bends; understanding local practice need not mean accepting it without question.
entries.narrative_credit: Explanation by Project Odisha, informed by the sources below.

entries.title: One hand cannot clap
entries.literal_meaning: A clap cannot sound with one hand alone.
entries.explanation: Some things require a response or a shared effort. The image of two palms meeting makes that dependence immediate. It can invite cooperation; it should not be used to assume that both sides bear equal blame for harm.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୁଇ ହାତ ମିଶିଲେ ତାଳିର ଶବ୍ଦ ହୁଏ—ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ପରସ୍ପରର ସହଯୋଗର କଥା କୁହାଯାଏ। କିଛି କାମରେ ଜଣଙ୍କ ଚେଷ୍ଟା ସହ ଆଉ ଜଣଙ୍କ ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା ବା ସହଭାଗ ଦରକାର। କିନ୍ତୁ କୌଣସି ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ଘଟିଲେ ଉଭୟ ପକ୍ଷ ସମାନ ଦୋଷୀ ବୋଲି ଏହି ଉପମାରୁ ଧରିନେବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: One person proposes a shared reading group; the others must also make time for it. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

entries.title: What is past cannot be undone
entries.literal_meaning: No lamentation for what has gone.
entries.explanation: The maxim urges someone to stop dwelling on an irreversible event and attend to what can still be done. It need not mean forgetting lessons or dismissing grief.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାହା ଘଟିସାରିଛି ଓ ଫେରାଇହେବ ନାହିଁ, ତାହାକୁ ନେଇ କେବଳ ଅନୁତାପରେ ଅଟକି ନରହିବାର କଥା ଏହା। ଆଗକୁ କଣ କରିହେବ, ସେଥିରେ ମନ ଦେବା ପାଇଁ ଏହା ଉତ୍ସାହ ଦେଇପାରେ। ଏହା ଘଟଣାରୁ ଶିଖିବାକୁ ବା ଦୁଃଖକୁ ସ୍ୱୀକାର କରିବାକୁ ମନା କରେନାହିଁ।

entries.title: A flower growing in the sky
entries.literal_meaning: A sky-flower.
entries.explanation: An attractive idea has no basis in reality, like a flower imagined as growing in empty sky. The expression questions feasibility rather than imagination itself.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆକାଶରେ ଫୁଲ ଫୁଟିବା ପରି ସୁନ୍ଦର କଳ୍ପନା, କିନ୍ତୁ ତାହାର ବାସ୍ତବ ଭିତ୍ତି ନାହିଁ। ଶୁଣିବାକୁ ଆକର୍ଷଣୀୟ ଯୋଜନାଟି କିପରି ସମ୍ଭବ ହେବ, ତାହା ଦେଖାଯାଉନଥିଲେ ଏହି ରୂଢ଼ି ଖାପ ଖାଏ। କଳ୍ପନା କରିବାକୁ ଅଟକାଇବା ନୁହେଁ, କଳ୍ପନା ଓ କରିହେବା କାମ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ବାଟଟି ଖୋଜିବା ମୁଖ୍ୟ।

entries.title: A small search uncovers something larger
entries.literal_meaning: While digging for tubers, Mahadeva appeared.
entries.explanation: An ordinary investigation unexpectedly brings a much larger matter to light. This explanation follows the contrast in scale; the dictionary does not provide an origin tale.
entries.meaning_odia: ସାଧାରଣ କିଛି ଖୋଜୁଥିଲେ, ହଠାତ୍ ତାଠାରୁ ବହୁତ ବଡ଼ କଥା ବାହାରିପଡ଼ିଲା। ଛୋଟ ଖୋଜା ଓ ବଡ଼ ଆବିଷ୍କାରର ତଫାତରେ କଥାଟିର ଆଶ୍ଚର୍ଯ୍ୟ ଓ ମଜା ଅଛି। ଏହା ଏକ ତୁଳନା; ପ୍ରକୃତରେ ଆଳୁ ଖୋଳି ମୂର୍ତ୍ତି ମିଳିଥିବା କୌଣସି ଘଟଣାକୁ ଏହାର ଉତ୍ପତ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଦାବି କରାଯାଇନାହିଁ।

entries.title: When silence is read as agreement
entries.literal_meaning: Silence is a sign of agreement.
entries.explanation: This maxim describes an inference people make from another person’s silence. Silence can also mean hesitation, fear or uncertainty, so it does not establish that someone has agreed.
entries.meaning_odia: କେହି ପ୍ରତିବାଦ ନକଲେ ସେ ରାଜି ବୋଲି ଧରିନେବାର ଧାରଣାକୁ ଏହି କଥା ପ୍ରକାଶ କରେ। ହେଲେ ଚୁପ୍ ରହିବା ପଛରେ ଦ୍ୱିଧା, ଭୟ ବା କଣ କହିବେ ନଜାଣିବା ମଧ୍ୟ ଥାଇପାରେ। ତେଣୁ ନିରବତାକୁ ଅର୍ଥ ଦେବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ଭାବେ ପଚାରି ବୁଝିବା ଦରକାର।

entries.title: Distance makes things look better
entries.odia: ଦୂର ପର୍ବତ ସୁନ୍ଦର; ଦୂର ବନ୍ଧୁ ସୁନ୍ଦର
entries.literal_meaning: A distant mountain is beautiful; a distant friend is beautiful.
entries.explanation: Distance can hide the rough edges of a place or a relationship. What looks inviting from afar may feel different when we know its everyday difficulties. The saying gently questions an ideal picture; it does not claim that friendship needs distance.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୂରରୁ ପାହାଡ଼ର ଖାଲଢିପ ଦିଶେନାହିଁ; ଦୂରର ବନ୍ଧୁଙ୍କ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ଅସୁବିଧା ବି ଆଖିରେ ପଡ଼େନାହିଁ। ନିକଟରୁ ଜାଣିଲେ ଯେଉଁ ତଫାତ ଦିଶେ, କଥାଟି ତାହାକୁ ମନେ ପକାଏ। ଦୂରର ସୁନ୍ଦର ଛବିକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବା ଏହାର ଭାବ, ବନ୍ଧୁତା ଭଲ ରହିବା ପାଇଁ ଦୂରେଇ ରହିବା ଦରକାର ବୋଲି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Someone envies a friend’s life from holiday photographs; a longer visit reveals ordinary chores and worries too. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary gives two parallel images: a mountain seen from afar and a friend kept at a distance. This explanation is an editorial reading of that contrast, not an origin story.

entries.title: Giving someone a rough reception
entries.literal_meaning: To give someone “good and middling”.
entries.explanation: The ordinary words suggest grades of quality, but together they can describe harsh treatment. In the dictionary’s example, the speaker sends someone away after giving them blows and abuse. The expression conveys that rough reception; reading the words as praise would miss the point. The source records the usage, not a recommendation to treat anyone this way.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଲଗା ଭାବେ ‘ଉତ୍ତମ’ ଓ ‘ମଧ୍ୟମ’ ଗୁଣର ମାନ ବୁଝାଏ, ହେଲେ ଏହି ରୂଢ଼ିରେ ସେଗୁଡ଼ିକ ପ୍ରଶଂସା ନୁହେଁ। ଅଭିଧାନର ଉଦାହରଣରେ ମାଡ଼ ଓ ଗାଳି ଦେଇ ବିଦା କରିବାର ଅର୍ଥରେ କଥାଟି ଆସିଛି। ଶବ୍ଦର ଅଲଗା ଅର୍ଥ ଯୋଡ଼ିଲେ ଏଠାରେ ପ୍ରକୃତ ଭାବ ମିଳେନାହିଁ। ଏହା କଠୋର ବ୍ୟବହାରର ଅର୍ଥ ବୁଝାଏ, ସେଭଳି ବ୍ୟବହାରକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: In a fictional account of a quarrel, a neighbour says that a visitor was given “uttama madhyama” before being sent away. The phrase signals a rough encounter, not a warm welcome. This is an original illustrative situation, not a collected account.
entries.cultural_context: This is an idiomatic expression documented within a dictionary example, rather than a complete proverbial sentence. The entry heading uses an editorial infinitive for easy lookup. The witness retains the sentence’s actual inflected wording and the dictionary’s explanation. No claim is made about when or where the expression began.

entries.title: Pride before a fall

entries.explanation: The source invokes Ravana’s downfall as an image of destructive pride. It warns against arrogance through a literary-religious allusion, not a verified historical event.
entries.meaning_odia: ରାବଣଙ୍କ ପତନର ସାହିତ୍ୟିକ ଓ ଧାର୍ମିକ କାହାଣୀକୁ ଅତି ଗର୍ବର ଉଦାହରଣ କରାଯାଇଛି। ନିଜ ଶକ୍ତି ଉପରେ ଅତ୍ୟଧିକ ଭରସା କରି ସୀମା ଭୁଲିଗଲେ ବିପଦ ଆସିପାରେ। ବଡ଼ ନାଁର ଏହି ଉଲ୍ଲେଖ ଚେତାବନୀକୁ ଜୋର୍ ଦିଏ, ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ଐତିହାସିକ ଘଟଣାର ବିବରଣୀ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: Hope for the unprotected
entries.literal_meaning: Providence supports the unprotected.
entries.explanation: The saying expresses faith that someone without protection may still find help. It offers reassurance, not a reason to withhold practical assistance.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାହାଙ୍କ ପାଖରେ ରକ୍ଷା ବା ସହାୟତାର ବଳ ନାହିଁ, ତାଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ବି ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ଆଶା ଅଛି—ଏହି ଆସ୍ଥା କଥାଟି ପ୍ରକାଶ କରେ। ଅସହାୟ ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତରେ ଏହା ମନକୁ ଭରସା ଦେଇପାରେ। ଦଇବ ସାହା ହେବେ ବୋଲି କହି ଆମେ ଦେଇପାରୁଥିବା ପ୍ରକୃତ ସାହାଯ୍ୟରୁ ପଛେଇଯିବା ଏହାର ଉଚିତ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: The danger of knowing only a little

entries.explanation: A partial understanding can cause trouble when someone acts as if it were enough. The warning is against misplaced certainty, not against beginning to learn.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଳ୍ପ ଜାଣିବା ନିଜେ ଭୟଙ୍କର ନୁହେଁ; ସେତିକିକୁ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଜ୍ଞାନ ଭାବି କାମ କଲେ ଅସୁବିଧା ହୁଏ। ନିଜ ଜ୍ଞାନର ସୀମା ନଜାଣି ଅତି ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ହୋଇଯିବାକୁ ଏହା ସତର୍କ କରେ। ଶିଖିବା ଆରମ୍ଭ କରିଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ଅଟକାଇବା ନୁହେଁ, ଆଉ କଣ ଜାଣିବା ବାକି ଅଛି ତାହା ଦେଖିବା ମୁଖ୍ୟ।

entries.title: A distraction and a stolen meal
entries.odia:
ଅଇଲା ମାଳି, ମାଇଲା ତାଳି
ଧରି ପଳେଇଲା, ଖେଚୁଡ଼ି ଥାଳି।
entries.literal_meaning: Mali arrived, clapped, and ran away carrying the plate of khichdi.
entries.explanation: A show of activity diverts attention while someone takes the thing that matters. The rhyme exposes the trick rather than admiring the theft.
entries.meaning_odia: ତାଳି ଓ ହୋହଲ୍ଲା ଆଡ଼କୁ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ଧ୍ୟାନ ଯାଉଛି, ସେହି ଫାଙ୍କରେ ଖେଚୁଡ଼ି ଥାଳି ନେଇଯିବାର କାମ ସରିଯାଉଛି। ଦେଖାଣିଆ ତତ୍ପରତା ପଛରେ ଲୁଚିଥିବା ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥକୁ ଛନ୍ଦଟି ଧରେ। କିଏ ସବୁଠୁ ଅଧିକ ହଲଚଲ କରୁଛି ମାତ୍ର ନୁହେଁ, ସେଥିରେ କାହାର ଲାଭ ହେଉଛି ସେହି କଥା ବି ଦେଖିବାକୁ ହୁଏ।
entries.usage_example: During a noisy discussion about small expenses, someone quietly takes the shared funds. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source supplies a deception gloss. ମାଳି is retained as the rhyme’s label; it is not evidence about a community’s conduct.

entries.title: Good intentions, a spoiled result

entries.title: A benefit out of reach
entries.literal_meaning: What does the crow gain when the bael fruit ripens?
entries.explanation: A desirable thing can become available without helping someone who cannot make use of it. The saying asks who actually benefits, not merely whether something is good.
entries.meaning_odia: ବେଲ ପାଚିଗଲା ବୋଲି କାଉର ଲାଭ ହେଲା, ଏମିତି ନୁହେଁ—ଏହି ତଫାତ କଥାଟିର କେନ୍ଦ୍ର। ଭଲ ଜିନିଷ ମିଳିଲେ ବି ତାହାକୁ ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିପାରୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ପାଇଁ ହିଁ ସେହି ଉପକାର ଫଳେ। ଜିନିଷଟି ଭଲ କି ନୁହେଁ ସହ କାହା ପାଇଁ ଓ କିପରି ଉପଯୋଗୀ, ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ବି ରହେ।
entries.usage_example: A village receives digital equipment but has no reliable electricity to use it. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source gloss concerns a useful thing failing to reach the appropriate person. The fruit-and-crow image is proverbial, not a biological claim about every crow.

entries.title: Do not laugh at another’s turn
entries.odia:
ଉପର ବରଡ଼ା ଖସୁଛି,
ମଝି ବରଡ଼ା ହସୁଛି 
ତଳ ବରଡ଼ା କହୁଛି,
ମୋ ଦିନ କାଳ ଯାଉଛିରେ ଭାଇ ତୋ ଦିନକାଳ ଆସୁଛି ॥
entries.literal_meaning: The upper leaf falls; the middle leaf laughs; the lower leaf says, “My time is passing, brother; your time is coming.”
entries.explanation: The speaking leaves place laughter beside the passing of time. Read cautiously, the verse warns against treating another’s decline as something that can never reach oneself.
entries.meaning_odia: ଗୋଟିଏ ପତ୍ର ଖସୁଛି, ଆଉ ଗୋଟିଏ ହସୁଛି, ତୃତୀୟଟି ନିଜ ପାଳିର କଥା ମନେ ପକାଉଛି। ଅନ୍ୟର ଅବନତିକୁ ନିଜଠାରୁ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଦୂରର କଥା ଭାବିବାକୁ ଏହି କଥା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ। ସମୟ ସହ ଅବସ୍ଥା ବଦଳେ ବୋଲି ମନେ ରଖିଲେ ଅନ୍ୟର ଦୁଃଖକୁ ନେଇ ହସିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଟିକେ ଅଟକିହେବ।
entries.usage_example: Younger colleagues mock a retiring worker until they consider their own eventual retirement. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

entries.odia: ଉପକାର କଲି କୁକୁରକୁ କୁକୁର ମୁତିଲା ଉପରକୁ।
entries.literal_meaning: I helped the dog; the dog urinated upwards at me.
entries.explanation: The crude image expresses resentment when help is answered with harm or disrespect. It describes a feeling of betrayal, not a reason to assume everyone who needs help will be ungrateful.
entries.meaning_odia: ଉପକାର କରିବା ପରେ ସମ୍ମାନ ଅପେକ୍ଷା ଅପମାନ ବା କ୍ଷତି ମିଳିଲେ ଯେଉଁ କ୍ଷୋଭ ହୁଏ, ଏହି କଟୁ ଚିତ୍ର ତାହାକୁ କହେ। ବକ୍ତା ନିଜ ଭରସା ଓ ମିଳିଥିବା ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟାର ଅମେଳରେ ଆଘାତ ପାଇଛନ୍ତି। ଏହା ସେହି ଅନୁଭବର ପ୍ରକାଶ, ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଦରକାର କରୁଥିବା ସବୁ ଲୋକ ଅକୃତଜ୍ଞ ବୋଲି ଧରିନେବାର କାରଣ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.odia:

entries.literal_meaning: “Thaka thaka Mali, bhajana tana”; when hunger comes, bring the rice near. (The opening phrase is retained in transliteration because its precise literal force remains uncertain.)
entries.explanation: The verse sets a loud display of devotion beside an ordinary appetite. It can be read as a jab at performance that conceals self-interest, though the source gives no separate explanation.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜୋର୍ ଭଜନର ଦେଖାଣି ସହ ଭୋକ ଲାଗିଲେ ଭାତ ଖୋଜିବାର ସାଧାରଣ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତାକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଏଥିରେ ଭକ୍ତିର ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନ ପଛରେ ନିଜ ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥ ଲୁଚିଥିବାକୁ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରାଯାଉଥିବା ପରି ପଢ଼ିହେବ। ଉତ୍ସରେ ଅଲଗା ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ନଥିବାରୁ ଏହି ପାଠ ସୀମିତ; ଭୋକ ଲାଗିବା ନିଜେ କପଟ ଭକ୍ତିର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A fictional character makes a grand show of sacrifice but promptly insists on a special meal. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: ମାଳି remains a source label, not a judgment about a caste or occupation. Neither hunger nor devotional singing is itself treated as proof of hypocrisy. The opening ଠକ ଠକ and ଭଜନ ଟାଣ are not given a definite literal gloss; the interpretation remains provisional.

entries.title: Promises made in a crisis
entries.odia: ଆତଙ୍କ ବେଳେ ଯାଚନ୍ତି କୁକୁଡ଼ା, ଆତଙ୍କ ଗଲେ ଦିଅନ୍ତି ନେଫେଡ଼ା
entries.literal_meaning: In a crisis they promise a chicken; when the crisis passes they give “ନେଫେଡ଼ା” (the final noun is left untranslated because its meaning is unresolved here).
entries.explanation: The source explains this as a vow made to God during danger and neglected once the danger passes. More broadly, it can remind someone not to forget a promise after receiving help. The precise meaning of the final noun is unresolved; the interpretation follows the supplied gloss.
entries.meaning_odia: ବିପଦରେ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ମାନସିକ କରାଗଲା, ବିପଦ ଟଳିଲା ପରେ ସେହି କଥା ଭୁଲିଗଲେ—ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହି ଆଚରଣକୁ ଧରେ। ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଦରକାର ବେଳର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ଓ ସ୍ୱସ୍ତି ମିଳିବା ପରର ବ୍ୟବହାର ମେଳ ଖାଉଛି କି ନାହିଁ, ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଏଥିରୁ ଉଠେ। ଶେଷ ଶବ୍ଦ ‘ନେଫେଡ଼ା’ର ସଠିକ୍ ଅର୍ଥ ଏଠାରେ ଅନିଶ୍ଚିତ; ଏହି ବୁଝାମଣା ଉତ୍ସର ଦିଆଯାଇଥିବା ଅର୍ଥ ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କରେ।
entries.usage_example: After asking for urgent help and promising to return it, someone stops answering once their own problem is solved. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The religious vow is the source’s explanatory setting, not a recommendation or a claim that everyone follows this practice. A previously deferred dictionary saying has different wording; no equivalence or repaired final word is certified.

entries.title: Only you know what is in your heart
entries.odia: ମାଲୁଣି ହାତରେ ଲଙ୍କା ମରିଚଲୋ, ମାଳି ହାତେ ଫୁଲ ହାର, ଯାହା ମନ କଥା, ସିଏ ଜାଣେ ସିନା, ତାହା କି ଜାଣିବ ପର ॥
entries.literal_meaning: Chillies in the woman gardener’s hand, a flower garland in the gardener’s hand: each person knows their own thoughts; how would another know them?
entries.explanation: The closing lines remind us that another person’s private thoughts are not directly visible. The everyday objects lead into that contrast; this reading does not assign a hidden moral meaning to the chillies or garland. Ask rather than assume what someone feels.
entries.meaning_odia: ହାତରେ ଥିବା ଲଙ୍କା ବା ଫୁଲହାର ଦିଶୁଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ମନର କଥା ସେମିତି ଦିଶେନାହିଁ। ଜଣେ କଣ ଭାବୁଛନ୍ତି ବା ଅନୁଭବ କରୁଛନ୍ତି, ତାହା ସେ ନିଜେ ଭଲ ଜାଣନ୍ତି। ତେଣୁ ବାହାରର ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ଦେଖି ମନ କଥା ଧରିନେବା ଅପେକ୍ଷା ପଚାରି ଶୁଣିବା ଭଲ। ଏହି ପାଠରେ ଲଙ୍କା ଓ ଫୁଲକୁ ଅଲଗା ନୈତିକ ଅର୍ଥ ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A friend seems quiet after receiving good news. Rather than decide that they are ungrateful, you ask what is on their mind. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Listed as a saying in this community anthology; author, earliest use and possible song or literary relationships remain unverified. Gardener words are translated as occupational imagery, not evidence about any community’s traits.

entries.title: Contentment with what comes
entries.literal_meaning: In food there is no good or bad: whatever is available in a place.
entries.explanation: The verse sets aside distinctions between preferred and less preferred food: one accepts what is available. A related passage in Jagannath Das’s Odia Bhagabata places this thought in the Avadhuta’s account to King Yadu of equanimity and the python as a teacher. Read in everyday conversation, it can counsel contentment instead of constant complaint. That everyday application is an interpretation, not an account of the saying’s first use.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯେଉଁଠି ଯାହା ମିଳେ, ତାହାକୁ ସନ୍ତୋଷରେ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରିବାର କଥା ଏହି ପଦରେ ଅଛି। ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ ଦାସଙ୍କ ଭାଗବତର ଏକ ସମ୍ପର୍କିତ ପାଠରେ ଅବଧୂତ ଯଦୁ ରାଜାଙ୍କୁ ନିଜର ସମଭାବ ଓ ଅଜଗରଠାରୁ ଶିଖିଥିବା ଧର୍ମ ବିଷୟରେ କହନ୍ତି। ସେଠାରେ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଅଳ୍ପ ବା ବହୁତ ହେଲେ ବି ସନ୍ତୋଷ ରହେ। ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ କଥାରେ ପଦଟି ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ଖୁଣ ନ ଧରି, ମିଳିଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ନେଇ ଚଳିବାର ପରାମର୍ଶ ହୋଇପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: On a visit, a guest welcomes a simple meal instead of complaining that a favourite dish is missing. (Original imagined occasion.)
entries.cultural_context: The related Bhagabata text is an ascetic teaching about contentment. entries.title: Learning as wealth
entries.literal_meaning: Learning is a great treasure; children, acquire it.
entries.explanation: The verse calls learning wealth and directly addresses children. Unlike a possession handed over once, learning must be acquired through effort. The comparison gives everyday study a value beyond an immediate reward; it does not promise that education alone removes every hardship.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏଠାରେ ବିଦ୍ୟାକୁ ବଡ଼ ଧନ ବୋଲି କହି ପିଲାମାନଙ୍କୁ ତାହା ଅର୍ଜନ କରିବାକୁ ଡକାଯାଇଛି। ପଢ଼ିବା, ପଚାରିବା ଓ ଶିଖିବାରେ ଲାଗୁଥିବା ପରିଶ୍ରମକୁ ଏହି ତୁଳନା ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଦିଏ। ଏହା ଶିକ୍ଷାର ମହତ୍ତ୍ୱ ବୁଝାଏ; ପଢ଼ିଲେ ଜୀବନର ସବୁ ଅସୁବିଧା ଦୂର ହେବ ବୋଲି ନିଶ୍ଚୟତା ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A grandparent encourages a child to spend a little time learning something new each day, even when there is no examination ahead. (Original imagined occasion.)
entries.cultural_context: The direct address to children and paired lines make this a didactic verse. The captured compilation places it under instructive Dhaga but supplies no author or literary work; attribution must remain unresolved.

entries.title: A home held together by affection
entries.literal_meaning: Ah, that home is like Vaikuntha, where mutual affection remains unbroken.
entries.explanation: The verse imagines an ideal home through the affection people show one another. The important word is mutual: care is not demanded from just one person. Its heavenly comparison celebrates a quality of relationships rather than the size or expense of a house.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯେଉଁ ଘରେ ପରସ୍ପର ସ୍ନେହ ରହେ, ସେହି ଘରକୁ ପଦଟି ବୈକୁଣ୍ଠ ସହ ତୁଳନା କରେ। ଘରର ଆକାର ବା ଧନସମ୍ପତ୍ତି ନୁହେଁ, ଲୋକେ ପରସ୍ପରକୁ କିପରି ଆଦର କରନ୍ତି ତାହା ଏଠାରେ ମୁଖ୍ୟ। ସ୍ନେହ ଉଭୟ ପଟୁ ଆସିବା ଦରକାର; ଜଣଙ୍କୁ ସବୁବେଳେ ସହିବାକୁ କହିବା ଏହାର ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Family members share chores and make time to listen during a difficult week; someone says this mutual care is what makes the house a home. (Original imagined occasion.)
entries.cultural_context: Vaikuntha supplies the religious comparison. This is an ideal expressed in verse, not evidence about every household or a reason to remain in a harmful relationship. No original author or work is identified by the captured entry.

entries.english_summary: Mutual affection, rather than a grand building, makes the verse’s ideal home.

entries.title: No embodied life is beyond death
entries.literal_meaning: Bearing a body in the mortal world, even a god dies.
entries.explanation: The verse uses the strongest possible contrast: even divinity does not escape death after taking bodily form in the mortal world. Read as counsel, it asks the listener to recognise the limits of embodied life. Its force is reflective and religious, not a factual account of a particular death.
entries.meaning_odia: ମର୍ତ୍ୟରେ ଦେହ ଧରିଥିଲେ ଦେବତାଙ୍କର ବି ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ପଦଟି କହେ। ବଡ଼ତ୍ୱ ବା ଶକ୍ତି ଥିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେହର ସୀମା ଏଡ଼ାଇହୁଏ ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଚିନ୍ତାକୁ ଏଥିରେ ତୀବ୍ର କରାଯାଇଛି। ଏହା ଜୀବନର ଅନିତ୍ୟତା ନେଇ ଏକ ଧାର୍ମିକ ପଦ, କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଘଟଣାର ବିବରଣୀ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: While remembering an admired elder, a family reflects quietly on how no position or achievement makes a life endless. (Original imagined occasion.)
entries.cultural_context: The wording resembles a literary or devotional maxim; the saved compilation alone does not establish its original work or oral circulation. Do not present it as medical advice or use it to dismiss someone’s grief.

entries.title: Ill will turned back on its maker
entries.literal_meaning: Whoever plans harm for another, Govinda plans harm for that person.
entries.explanation: The verse warns against deliberately wishing or planning another person’s misfortune. It imagines that ill will being answered by Govinda. This is a religious moral warning, not a guarantee that every wrongdoer will suffer or that a person’s suffering proves wrongdoing.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅନ୍ୟର ମନ୍ଦ ଚାହିଁବା ବା ମନ୍ଦ ଯୋଜନା କରିବାରୁ ପଦଟି ବାରଣ କରେ। ସେପରି ଲୋକର ମନ୍ଦ ଗୋବିନ୍ଦ ପାଞ୍ଚନ୍ତି ବୋଲି କହି ଏଥିରେ ଧାର୍ମିକ ଚେତାବନୀ ଦିଆଯାଇଛି। କାହାର ଦୁଃଖ ଦେଖି ସେ ନିଶ୍ଚୟ କିଛି ଖରାପ କରିଥିଲା ବୋଲି ରାୟ ଦେବାର ଆଧାର ଏହା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Someone proposes spreading a rumour to damage a rival’s chances, and a friend urges them to abandon the plan. (Original imagined occasion.)
entries.cultural_context: Govinda is retained as the named divine figure in the source. The compilation supplies no separate explanation or attribution. The moral should not be converted into victim-blaming or a prediction of supernatural punishment.

entries.title: Persistence meets resistance
entries.literal_meaning: Tough iron meets a persistent smith.
entries.explanation: The same word changes force across the line: the iron resists, while the smith refuses to give up. The dictionary explicitly marks these two senses. The image suggests meeting a difficult task with sustained effort rather than expecting it to yield immediately. It need not turn persistence into an obligation to continue every losing effort.
entries.meaning_odia: ଲୁହା ସହଜରେ ବଙ୍କେ ନାହିଁ, କମାର ମଧ୍ୟ ସହଜରେ ହାର ମାନେ ନାହିଁ। ଏକା କୋଚଟ ଶବ୍ଦ ଲୁହାର ଦୃଢ଼ତା ଓ କାରିଗରର ନଛୋଡ଼ ଚେଷ୍ଟାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ୁଛି। କାମ କଠିନ ହେଲେ ଧୈର୍ଯ୍ୟ ଓ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଚେଷ୍ଟା ଦରକାର ବୋଲି ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରୁ ବୁଝିହୁଏ।
entries.english_summary: The same word changes force across the line: the iron resists, while the smith refuses to give up.
entries.odia_summary: ଲୁହା ସହଜରେ ବଙ୍କେ ନାହିଁ, କମାର ମଧ୍ୟ ସହଜରେ ହାର ମାନେ ନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A learner patiently retries a difficult passage of music instead of abandoning it after the first mistake. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The craft image concerns resistance and effort; it does not describe an inherited trait of a community. Parenthetical dictionary sense numbers are omitted from the displayed wording and recorded as an editorial change.

entries.title: Say what you want in time
entries.odia: ଚଇତା ! ତବତ ଖାଇବୁ କି ପଖାଳ ଖାଇବୁ ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ ଥାଉଁ କହିଥା
entries.literal_meaning: Chaita! Will you eat hot food or pakhala? Say so while there is still time.
entries.explanation: The pointed address and choice between hot food and pakhala turn a practical request into a memorable line: say what you want while another person still has time to arrange it. The dictionary marks Chaita as a non-respectful form of Chaitanya, so the tone can carry impatience or a dismissive edge. Applying it to other decisions is an editorial reading of the complete quoted example; its first occasion is unknown.
entries.meaning_odia: ତବତ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ନା ପଖାଳ—କଣ ଖାଇବ, ତାହା ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ କହିବାକୁ ଚଇତାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି। ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣେ ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା କରିବାକୁ ହେଲେ ଆମ ଇଚ୍ଛାଟି ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିବା ଦରକାର। ସବୁ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ସରିଗଲା ପରେ ମତ ବଦଳାଇବାଠାରୁ ସମୟରେ କହିଦେବା ଭଲ—ଏହି ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ବିଚାରଟି ଏଠି ଖାଇବା କଥାରେ ଆସିଛି।
entries.english_summary: A meal cannot be arranged around an answer that arrives too late.
entries.odia_summary: ତବତ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ନା ପଖାଳ—କଣ ଖାଇବ, ତାହା ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ କହିବାକୁ ଚଇତାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି।
entries.usage_example: A friend arranging a shared journey asks everyone to confirm their plans before tickets are booked. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source identifies Chaita as a non-respectful or dismissive form of Chaitanya. No particular historical person or household is established. Pakhala remains a named food; the wording should not be softened into a uniformly polite request.

entries.title: Care for the person doing the work
entries.literal_meaning: Take care of your body while carrying out your religious duty.
entries.explanation: The dictionary places this saying under caring for the body and health. Duty does not erase the needs of the person who performs it. In a wider everyday application, commitment and care for oneself can belong together; exhaustion is not the only measure of sincerity.
entries.meaning_odia: ଧର୍ମକାର୍ଯ୍ୟ କରିବା ସହ ନିଜ ଦିହକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଜଗିବାକୁ କଥାଟି କହୁଛି। ନିଷ୍ଠା ଥିଲେ ବି ନିଜ ଶକ୍ତି ଓ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତାକୁ ଭୁଲିଯିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ। ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ କାମରେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନେବା ଓ ନିଜକୁ ସମ୍ଭାଳିବା ପରସ୍ପରର ବିରୋଧୀ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: Embarrassed on someone else’s behalf
entries.odia: ନାଚିଲା ଲୋକକୁ ଲାଜ ନାହିଁ ଦେଖିଲା ଲୋକକୁ ଲାଜ
entries.literal_meaning: The person dancing feels no embarrassment; the person watching does.
entries.explanation: The dictionary explains a mismatch: someone behaves without embarrassment while witnesses feel ashamed on that person’s behalf. The saying can name that uncomfortable distance between an action and how it appears to others. Its image need not be used to condemn dancing or to police someone’s harmless enjoyment.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯେଉଁ ଲୋକ କାମଟି କରୁଛି, ତାକୁ ଲାଜ ଲାଗୁନାହିଁ; ଦେଖୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ତା ପାଇଁ ଅସହଜ ହେଉଛି। ନିଜ ଆଚରଣ ଅନ୍ୟଙ୍କୁ କିପରି ଲାଗୁଛି, ସେଥିପ୍ରତି ଅସଚେତନ ରହିଲେ ଏଭଳି ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ହୋଇପାରେ। ଏଠି ନାଚର ଚିତ୍ର ଅଛି ବୋଲି ନାଚିବାକୁ ଲଜ୍ଜାର କାମ ଭାବିବା ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: The dictionary explains a mismatch: someone behaves without embarrassment while witnesses feel ashamed on that person’s behalf.

entries.usage_example: Someone loudly claims credit for a group effort while their companions exchange embarrassed looks. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

entries.title: A seed bigger than its fruit
entries.odia: ବାର ହାତ କାକୁଡ଼ିର ତେର ହାତ ମଞ୍ଜି
entries.literal_meaning: A cucumber twelve cubits long contains a seed thirteen cubits long.
entries.explanation: The part has become larger than the whole that supposedly contains it. The dictionary explicitly calls this an impossible claim. The absurd measurements make a quick test for an exaggerated story: do its own details fit together? The point is inconsistency, not an accurate description of cucumber growth.
entries.meaning_odia: କାକୁଡ଼ି ବାର ହାତ, ହେଲେ ତା ଭିତର ମଞ୍ଜି ତେର ହାତ—ହିସାବଟି ନିଜେ ନିଜକୁ ଖଣ୍ଡନ କରୁଛି। ଅସମ୍ଭବ କଥାକୁ ବଡ଼ କରି କହିବାର ମଜା ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଅଛି। କାହାର କଥାରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଅଂଶ ଆଉ ଗୋଟିଏ ସହ ମେଳ ନଖାଇଲେ, ତାହାକୁ ଏହିପରି ହସି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରାଯାଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: The part has become larger than the whole that supposedly contains it.

entries.title: A boat needs a river
entries.literal_meaning: What can a boat do when the river dries up?
entries.explanation: A useful boat cannot replace the water it needs. The image invites a distinction between ability and the conditions that make ability useful. When an essential resource disappears, blaming the tool or the person alone may miss the real obstacle. This wider application is an editorial interpretation of the quoted saying.
entries.meaning_odia: ନାଆ ଭଲ ଥିଲେ ବି ଶୁଖିଲା ନଈରେ ଚାଲିପାରିବ ନାହିଁ। କାମ କରିବାର କ୍ଷମତା ସହ ସେଥିପାଇଁ ଦରକାରୀ ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ମଧ୍ୟ ରହିବା ଦରକାର। ମୂଳ ସାଧନଟି ନଥିଲେ କେବଳ ଲୋକ ବା ଯନ୍ତ୍ରକୁ ଦୋଷ ଦେଇ ସମସ୍ୟା ବୁଝିହେବ ନାହିଁ—ନଈ ଓ ନାଆର ଚିତ୍ରରୁ ଏହି ବିଚାରଟି ଆସେ।

entries.title: When spending outgrows income
entries.literal_meaning: Like the temple’s front hall exceeding the temple itself.
entries.explanation: The dictionary explicitly applies this architectural comparison to expenditure exceeding income. What should be a supporting part has grown beyond the thing that supports it. The image asks us to notice proportion in a plan, especially when its surrounding costs threaten to consume more than the available means.

entries.title: A whole village stirred by one household
entries.odia:
ଅପାଇ ପାଇଚି ପିଲା,
ନା ଗାଁ ଯାକ କିଲିବିଲା...!!!
entries.literal_meaning: Apai has got a child; the whole village is in a commotion.
entries.explanation: A private event becomes everybody’s noisy business. The source introduces this saying as something used when someone makes too much of a display. Its joke lies in the size of the response: one household’s news seems to shake an entire village.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜଣଙ୍କ ଘରେ ପିଲା ହେବାର ଖବର, ଅଥଚ ଗାଁ ସାରା କିଲିବିଲି। ନିଜ କଥାକୁ ନେଇ ଅତିରିକ୍ତ ଦେଖେଇ ହେଲେ ଏହି ଉକ୍ତିରେ ପରିହାସ କରାଯାଏ। ଛୋଟ ପରିସରର ଘଟଣାକୁ ବଡ଼ ହୋହଲ୍ଲା କରିଦେବାର ତୁଳନାଟି ଏହାକୁ ମନେ ରଖାଏ।
entries.usage_example: A small household purchase is announced repeatedly to every neighbour, with more ceremony than the occasion seems to need. (Original imagined occasion.)
entries.cultural_context: The source explicitly supplies a display/show-off context. Apai is retained as an unidentified source designation; no historical person, kinship role or gender is inferred. The criticism is of disproportionate display, not of celebrating a child.

entries.title: Boasting beside the kitchen stove
entries.odia:

ପୁଅ ଦେଖଉଚି ନୁଖୁରା ବଡ଼େଇ...!!
entries.literal_meaning: The cat may be doing nahunia exercises beside the stove; the boy displays empty boasting.
entries.explanation: The source introduces this line for unnecessary swagger. A cat’s ordinary-looking movement by the stove is set beside a boy making much of himself. The disproportion makes the boast look small: loud self-display is not itself an achievement.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚୁଲି ପାଖରେ ବିଲେଇ ନହୁଣିଆ ପାରୁଛି, ଆଉ ପୁଅ ବଡ଼େଇ ଦେଖାଉଛି—ଏହି ତୁଳନାରେ ଅଯଥା ଆସ୍ଫାଳନକୁ ଛୋଟ କରିଦିଆଯାଇଛି। ଉତ୍ସରେ ବି ଅଯଥା ଆସ୍ଫାଳନ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକ ପାଇଁ ଉକ୍ତିଟି ଦିଆଯାଇଛି। କଥାର ଜୋର ଦେଖାଇବା ଓ ସତରେ କିଛି କରିବା ଏକ କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Someone claims to be an expert after one easy practice task, and a friend gently punctures the swagger. (Original imagined occasion.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary lists nahunia as a kind of bodily exercise, which supports retaining an exercise image; no precise pose or movement sequence is established. The source’s own usage condition supports the swagger reading. The literal rendering of ନୁଖୁରା as empty remains contextual rather than separately dictionary-certified.

entries.title: A secret concealed inside an ordinary action
entries.odia: ବୁଡ଼ି କରି ପାଣି ପିଇଲେ ମହାଦେବଙ୍କ ବାପା ମଧ୍ୟ ଜାଣି ପରିବେ ନାହିଁ
entries.literal_meaning: If someone drinks water while submerged, even Mahadev’s father will not know.
entries.explanation: The dictionary places this example under doing something secretly. Drinking is hidden within the larger act of being underwater, so an observer cannot easily separate one from the other. The extravagant appeal to Mahadev’s father makes the claim of secrecy comic. It can describe someone’s confidence that a concealed action will escape notice; it does not establish that deception always succeeds.
entries.meaning_odia: ପାଣି ଭିତରେ ବୁଡ଼ିଥିବା ଲୋକ ପାଣି ପିଇଲେ, ବାହାରୁ ଦେଖୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ସେ କାମଟି ଅଲଗା କରି ଜଣାପଡ଼େ ନାହିଁ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହାକୁ ଗୋପନରେ କାମ କରିବାର ଉଦାହରଣ ଭାବେ ଦେଇଛି। ମହାଦେବଙ୍କ ବାପା ବି ଜାଣିପାରିବେ ନାହିଁ କହି କଥାଟି ଲୁଚାଇବାର ଦାବିକୁ ହସରେ ବଢ଼ାଇଦିଏ। ଏଥିରୁ ସବୁ ଲୁଚା କାମ ଚିରକାଳ ଅଜଣା ରହିବ ବୋଲି ନିଶ୍ଚୟ କରିହୁଏ ନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: The dictionary places this example under doing something secretly.
entries.odia_summary: ପାଣି ଭିତରେ ବୁଡ଼ିଥିବା ଲୋକ ପାଣି ପିଇଲେ, ବାହାରୁ ଦେଖୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ସେ କାମଟି ଅଲଗା କରି ଜଣାପଡ଼େ ନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: While supposedly tidying a shared desk, someone quietly removes a note and assumes nobody noticed. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: The expression is comic hyperbole, not theological genealogy or an instruction to drink underwater. Source spelling ପରିବେ is retained, not silently changed to ପାରିବେ.

entries.title: Talking oneself out of a welcome meal
entries.odia: ପୁତୁରା ସାଙ୍ଗରେ କଳି କଲି, ମହୁର ତିଅଣରୁ ମେଞ୍ଚାଏ ପାଆନ୍ତି, ତୁଣ୍ଡ ପରସାଦୁଁ ନାଶ ଗଲି
entries.literal_meaning: I quarrelled with my nephew; I might have received a generous portion of mahura curry, but my own mouth spoiled it.
entries.explanation: The speaker looks back on a quarrel and the food they might otherwise have enjoyed. The dictionary defines ମେଞ୍ଚାଏ as a large portion of food. Here the humorous self-accusation turns an abstract consequence of quarrelling into a lost meal: the mouth that wanted food also said the words that cost it. This is a close reading of the example, not a reconstructed family incident.
entries.meaning_odia: ପୁତୁରା ସହ କଳି କରିବା ପରେ କଥକ ମନେ ପକାଉଛନ୍ତି, ନକରିଥିଲେ ମହୁର ତିଅଣରୁ ଭଲ ଭାଗଟିଏ ମିଳିଥାନ୍ତା। ଯେଉଁ ତୁଣ୍ଡ ଖାଇବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁଥିଲା, ସେହି ତୁଣ୍ଡର କଥା ହିଁ ଖାଇବାର ସୁଯୋଗ ନଷ୍ଟ କଲା—ଏହି ବିରୋଧରେ ହସ ଅଛି। ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ କଳି କରି ନିଜ ସୁବିଧା ବା ସମ୍ପର୍କ ବିଗାଡ଼ିଦେବା ପରେ ଏପରି ନିଜକୁ ନେଇ କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ତାହା ବୋଲି ଖାଇବା ବା ସୁବିଧା ପାଇଁ ସବୁ ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ସହିବାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: The speaker looks back on a quarrel and the food they might otherwise have enjoyed.
entries.odia_summary: ପୁତୁରା ସହ କଳି କରିବା ପରେ କଥକ ମନେ ପକାଉଛନ୍ତି, ନକରିଥିଲେ ମହୁର ତିଅଣରୁ ଭଲ ଭାଗଟିଏ ମିଳିଥାନ୍ତା।
entries.usage_example: After needlessly snapping at a friend, someone regrets spoiling the relaxed lunch they had planned together. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: Mahura is retained as a named curry; no ingredients, temple recipe or historical household are inferred. The reading concerns needless quarrelling, not an obligation to remain silent about mistreatment.

entries.title: Respect that lasts only while help is needed
entries.odia: କାମ ପଡ଼ିଲେ କାଜି, କାମ ଛାଡ଼ିଲେ ପାଜି
entries.literal_meaning: When there is work to be done, a qazi; when the need is over, a scoundrel.
entries.explanation: The paired words move abruptly from a title of authority to an insult. Read together, they expose respect that depends entirely on another person’s usefulness: someone is important while needed and dismissed afterward. The target of this reading is the speaker’s opportunism, not the integrity of qazis or any religious community.
entries.meaning_odia: କାମ ପଡ଼ିଥିବା ବେଳେ ଯାହାକୁ କାଜି କହି ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦିଆଯାଉଥିଲା, କାମ ସରିଲେ ତାଙ୍କୁ ପାଜି କୁହାଯାଉଛି। ଦୁଇଟି ମିଳୁଥିବା ଶବ୍ଦରେ ଆଦରରୁ ଅପମାନକୁ ହଠାତ୍ ବଦଳିଯିବା ଧରାପଡ଼େ। ଦରକାର ବେଳେ ଆଦର କରି, ଦରକାର ସରିଲେ ମଣିଷଟିକୁ ଭୁଲିଯିବାର ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥପରତାକୁ ଏହି ପାଠରେ ଦେଖିହୁଏ। ଏହା କୌଣସି ଧର୍ମର ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଚରିତ୍ର ବିଷୟରେ ନିଷ୍କର୍ଷ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: The paired words move abruptly from a title of authority to an insult.
entries.odia_summary: କାମ ପଡ଼ିଥିବା ବେଳେ ଯାହାକୁ କାଜି କହି ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦିଆଯାଉଥିଲା, କାମ ସରିଲେ ତାଙ୍କୁ ପାଜି କୁହାଯାଉଛି।
entries.usage_example: An organiser repeatedly praises a volunteer while asking for help, then refuses even to acknowledge that help once the event ends. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: The source defines qazi as a Muslim judge and explicitly labels the paired line ଢଗ; a separate lexical entry confirms ପାଜି is an insult. Institutional history in the old dictionary is not adopted as present-day law or status.

entries.title: A lesson that stays with you
entries.literal_meaning: You will keep washing the sack and singing praises.
entries.explanation: The praise has an ironic edge. The source explains the expression as remembering someone after receiving a hard lesson from them. The repeated work of washing the sack makes that memory linger: the consequences remain after the encounter is over. It can be a rueful comment on having been taken in, rather than sincere gratitude.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଖା ଧୋଇବା ସହିତ ଗୁଣ ଗାଇବାର କଥା ଶୁଣିଲେ ପ୍ରଶଂସା ପରି ଲାଗେ। କିନ୍ତୁ ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ଏହା ଅନ୍ୟଠାରୁ ପାନେ ପାଇ ତାକୁ ମନେ ପକାଇବା। ଘଟଣାଟି ସରିଗଲେ ବି ତାହାର ଫଳ ଭୋଗିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ୁଛି। ସେହି ଅନୁଭବକୁ ନେଇ ଏଠାରେ ଟିକେ କଟାକ୍ଷ ଅଛି; ଏହା ସରଳ ଧନ୍ୟବାଦ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: A buyer keeps repairing a supposedly excellent second-hand bicycle and ruefully remembers the seller’s promises. (Original imagined occasion, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The source supplies the hard-lesson gloss but no story explaining why a sack is washed. The sack image and ironic praise are retained without inventing that missing story.

entries.english_summary: The trouble continues, and so does the rueful memory of who brought it about.

entries.title: Nothing left at the root
entries.literal_meaning: To wipe out at the root.
entries.explanation: This is an expression for complete destruction, not merely a setback or a surface change. The source pairs it with another expression and explicitly glosses both as destroying something entirely. The root image makes the degree of loss clear: what might have allowed it to continue has also been removed.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏଠାରେ କେବଳ ଉପରୁ କିଛି ନଷ୍ଟ ହେବାର କଥା ନୁହେଁ। ମୂଳ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ସବୁ ପୋଛିଦେବାର ଛବିରେ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଧ୍ୱଂସର ଅର୍ଥ ଅଛି। ଉତ୍ସ ମଧ୍ୟ ଏହି ଅର୍ଥ ଦେଇଛି। ଆଉ କିଛି ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ ନ ରହିବାର ତୀବ୍ରତାକୁ ଏହା ପ୍ରକାଶ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: A flood has destroyed a family’s stored seed, tools and the shed itself; a neighbour uses the expression to describe the extent of the loss. (Original imagined occasion, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: Selected as the second expression in the source’s slash-separated pair ଖୋଳ କରିବା/ମୂଳପୋଛ କରିବା. The source’s first term is retained as a related expression, not silently translated through a guessed literal sense or counted as a second entry.
entries.odia_summary: ସାମାନ୍ୟ କ୍ଷତି ନୁହେଁ, ସମୂଳେ ଧ୍ୱଂସ ହେବାର ତୀବ୍ର ଅର୍ଥ।
entries.english_summary: An emphatic expression for destruction that leaves nothing at the root.

witnesses.locator: Revision 3584061; wikitext lines 9–11, item beginning ଖୋଳ କରିବା

entries.title: The tether and the horse
entries.literal_meaning: According to the stake, the horse leaps.
entries.explanation: The source applies this image to disorder under weak supervision. The horse’s movement is viewed in relation to what holds it, so the remark turns attention from the actor alone to the arrangement around them. In a wider everyday application, repeated disorder may reveal that responsibilities or boundaries have not been made clear. That wider application is editorial; the source does not supply a history of the image.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘୋଡ଼ାର ଡେଇଁବାକୁ ଏଠାରେ ଖୁଣ୍ଟ ସହିତ ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଉତ୍ସ ଏହାକୁ ଦୁର୍ବଳ ଶାସନରେ ବିଶୃଙ୍ଖଳା ଘଟିବାର ଅର୍ଥରେ ବୁଝାଇଛି। କେବଳ କାମ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ଦୋଷ ନ ଦେଇ, ତାଙ୍କ ଚାରିପାଖର ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେଖିବାର ଏକ ପାଠ ଏଥିରୁ ନିଆଯାଇପାରେ। ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ କାହାର, କଣ କରିବାକୁ ହେବ—ଏସବୁ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନଥିଲେ ଅବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା ବଢ଼ିପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: At a shared event, supplies repeatedly go missing because nobody has been assigned to track them. Someone points to the loose arrangement rather than blaming one volunteer. (Original imagined occasion, not a collected quotation.)
entries.cultural_context: The weak-supervision reading comes from this source’s gloss. Other readings of strength or support are not established here. The comparison is not a recommendation for harsh discipline or a claim that people are animals.
entries.odia_summary: କାମର ଅବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା ପଛରେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଓ ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥାର ଦୁର୍ବଳତା ମଧ୍ୟ ଥାଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: The source’s image directs attention to weak supervision behind disorder.

entries.title: The words will outlast the moment
entries.literal_meaning: The words will remain for all time.
entries.explanation: A conversation ends, but what was said can remain in memory. The dictionary labels this short line a Dhaga under “for ever”. It can give a promise weight or warn that a remark will not be easily forgotten. Which feeling it carries depends on the speaker and the occasion; the source does not specify a single original scene.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥା କହିବାର ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତଟି ସରିଯାଏ, ହେଲେ କହିଥିବା କଥା ମନରେ ରହିଯାଇପାରେ। ଛୋଟ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଗୋଟିଏ ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତିକୁ ଓଜନ ଦେଇପାରେ, ପୁଣି ଭୁଲି ନ ହେବା ଭଳି କଥା ପ୍ରତି ସତର୍କ କରିପାରେ। କିଏ କାହାକୁ କେଉଁ ସ୍ୱରରେ କହୁଛି, ସେଥିରୁ ଏହାର ଭାବ ବଦଳେ।
entries.english_summary: A conversation ends, but what was said can remain in memory.

entries.title: When both of us agree
entries.odia: ତୋର ମୋର ରାଜି, କିସ କରିବ କାଜି
entries.literal_meaning: You and I agree—what can the qazi do?
entries.explanation: The rhyme between raji and qazi turns agreement into a cheeky challenge to an outside authority. The dictionary places it under the qazi’s marriage-registration role. Its force is rhetorical: if the people concerned agree, why should someone else obstruct them? That is the speaker’s claim, not a statement that consent removes legal duties.
entries.meaning_odia: ତୁ ରାଜି, ମୁଁ ରାଜି—ତେବେ ମଝିରେ ଆଉ କାହାର ବାଧା କାହିଁକି? ରାଜି ଓ କାଜିର ମିଳ ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନକୁ ଟିକେ ମଜା ଓ ଟିକେ ଆହ୍ୱାନର ସ୍ୱର ଦିଏ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ କାଜିଙ୍କ ବିବାହ ପଞ୍ଜୀକରଣ ଭୂମିକା ପାଖରେ ଏହି ଉଦାହରଣ ଅଛି। ଏହା କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ଯୁକ୍ତି; ଆଇନର ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: The rhyme between raji and qazi turns agreement into a cheeky challenge to an outside authority.
entries.odia_summary: ତୁ ରାଜି, ମୁଁ ରାଜି—ତେବେ ମଝିରେ ଆଉ କାହାର ବାଧା କାହିଁକି? ରାଜି ଓ କାଜିର ମିଳ ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନକୁ ଟିକେ ମଜା ଓ ଟିକେ ଆହ୍ୱାନର ସ୍ୱର ଦିଏ।

entries.title: Land to cultivate, yet no meal
entries.literal_meaning: A bati of cultivation, yet fasting every day.
entries.explanation: The joke places a substantial-looking agricultural resource beside an empty stomach. The source explains it as plenty of rice but too little cooked food. Possession and actual provision have come apart: what looks sufficient has not become something usable. The saying does not identify one universal cause for that mismatch.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚାଷ ଅଛି, ଚାଉଳର ଅଭାବ ବି ନାହିଁ, ଅଥଚ ଖାଇବାକୁ ଭାତ ନିଅଣ୍ଟ। ଢଗଟିର ପରିହାସ ଏହି ବିରୋଧରେ। କାଗଜରେ ବା ଦେଖିବାକୁ ଯାହା ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ, ତାହା ଦରକାର ବେଳେ କାମରେ ଆସୁନାହିଁ। ଅଭାବର କାରଣଟି କଣ, ଏହି ଛୋଟ ଧାଡ଼ି ନିଜେ କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A community room has cupboards full of donated supplies, but nobody can find the materials needed for today’s class. Someone recalls this mismatch between plenty and use. (Original imagined example.)
entries.cultural_context: Bati is retained as the source’s land-measure term; no regional conversion is supplied. The witness spells the daily expression ନୀତି, which is preserved. The accompanying gloss, not an invented household story, supports the reading.

entries.title: Quiet persistence against a rush
entries.odia:
ଧୀର ସ୍ଥିର ନୋହି ଉତ୍ତେଜିତ ହେଲେ
କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ କେବେ ସିଦ୍ଧ ନୁହେଁ ।
ଧୀରପାଣି ସିନା ପଥର କାଟଇ
ସ୍ରୋତ ତହିଁ ବ୍ୟର୍ଥ ହୁଏ  ॥
entries.literal_meaning: If one becomes agitated instead of steady, work never succeeds. Slow water cuts stone; the rushing current fails there.
entries.explanation: The verse gives patient work the quieter but stronger image. Water that keeps returning to the stone stands against a rush of agitation. Its supplied gloss recommends thinking and acting steadily instead of becoming angry. The absolute contrast belongs to the verse’s exhortation; it is not a scientific claim that fast water cannot erode stone.
entries.meaning_odia: ପଥର କାଟୁଥିବା ଧୀର ପାଣିର ଛବି ଦେଇ ପଦଟି ସ୍ଥିର ମନରେ କାମ କରିବାକୁ କହେ। ହଠାତ୍ ଉତ୍ତେଜନାର ଜୋର ଦେଖାଯାଏ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଧୈର୍ଯ୍ୟର କାମ ଚାଲିଥାଏ। ଏଠାରେ ପାଣି ଓ ସ୍ରୋତର ତୁଳନା ମନର ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ; ପ୍ରକୃତିର ସବୁ ଘଟଣା ପାଇଁ ନିୟମ ବାନ୍ଧେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Two people keep restarting a repair in irritation. A companion suggests checking one connection at a time and recalls the quiet water working on stone. (Original imagined example.)
entries.cultural_context: This four-line exhortation appears in the collection of traditional sayings, with a supplied gloss. No named poet, composition date, tune or independent evidence of proverbial circulation is established in this pass. Its four-line form is retained, not silently shortened to a slogan.
entries.odia_summary: ଉତ୍ତେଜନାର ଜୋର ଅପେକ୍ଷା ସ୍ଥିର ଚିନ୍ତା ଓ ଲାଗିରହିବାକୁ ପଦଟି ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦିଏ।
entries.english_summary: The verse makes quiet persistence stronger than agitation.
entries.category: Instructive verse in a collection of sayings

entries.title: Staying alive to carry something forward
entries.literal_meaning: If you yourself survive, your father’s name lives on.
entries.explanation: The short line makes survival the condition for carrying a family name forward. The collection’s gloss extends the thought towards being able to help the world by first getting oneself ahead. This is a reminder that continuing to live and act matters; it does not establish that another person’s welfare is unimportant.
entries.meaning_odia: ନିଜେ ବଞ୍ଚି ରହିଲେ ହିଁ ବାପର ନାଁ ଆଗକୁ ନେଇହେବ—ଛୋଟ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଏହି କଥା କହେ। ସବୁକିଛି କରିବାର ଆଗରୁ ନିଜର ରହିବା ଓ କାମ କରିପାରିବା ଦରକାର। ଏହି ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହାକୁ ନିଜେ ଆଗେଇ ପରର ମଙ୍ଗଳ କରିବା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ। କଥାର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଅନୁସାରେ କେହି ନିଜ ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥକୁ ଆଗରେ ରଖିବା ପାଇଁ ବି ଧାଡ଼ିଟି କହିପାରେ; ଉତ୍ସର ଏହି ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ସବୁ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ସୀମା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Someone carrying out a long family task is exhausted but unwilling to stop. A relative uses the line to urge a pause so the work can continue tomorrow. (Original imagined example.)
entries.cultural_context: The father’s name is the source’s family image, not a claim that only sons sustain families. English “lives on” supplies the implied continuation rather than an additional historical assertion. No origin story is supplied.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଜେ ବଞ୍ଚି ଓ ସମର୍ଥ ରହିଲେ ହିଁ ଆଗକୁ କିଛି କରିହେବ।
entries.english_summary: Survival makes continuing the family’s work possible.

entries.title: Imagine a horse with horns
entries.odia: ଜାଣି ଘୋଡ଼ାର ଶିଙ୍ଗ ନାହିଁ, ଶିଙ୍ଗ ଥିଲେ ଘୋଡ଼ା ରଖନ୍ତା ନାହିଁ ।
entries.literal_meaning: The horse has no horns; with horns it would spare no one.
entries.explanation: The image starts with an already powerful animal and imagines giving it another weapon. The collection explains the line as a limit on the strength granted to the strong: with still more power, they might heed nobody. The humour is in the impossible extra equipment, not in a claim that real horses are naturally malicious.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘୋଡ଼ାର ଜୋର ତ ଅଛି; ସେଥିରେ ଯଦି ଶିଙ୍ଗ ବି ଥାଆନ୍ତା! ଏହି ଅସମ୍ଭବ ଛବିରେ ଢଗଟି ଶକ୍ତିର ସୀମାକୁ ଦେଖାଏ। ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଅନୁସାରେ ବଳୁଆକୁ ଆହୁରି ବଳ ମିଳିଲେ ସେ କାହାକୁ ଖାତିର ନକରିପାରେ। ଘୋଡ଼ାର ସ୍ୱଭାବ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କରିବା ଏହାର କଥା ନୁହେଁ; ମଣିଷର ଅସୀମ କ୍ଷମତାକୁ ନେଇ ପରିହାସ।
entries.usage_example: A forceful committee member asks to control both the funds and every decision. Another member jokes about adding horns to the horse. (Original imagined example.)
entries.cultural_context: The supplied gloss invokes divine restraint; this is the collection’s explanation, not evidence for a particular myth or author. The last clause’s omitted object is rendered “no one” in English in line with the gloss’s reference to heeding nobody. The opening ଜାଣି does not securely establish who knows or intends this; the English does not turn it into an imperative. Its agency remains unresolved.

entries.title: Trying to keep both
entries.literal_meaning: The friend will remain; the jewel will remain.
entries.explanation: The words sound reassuring: neither precious thing need be lost. But the dictionary labels the saying ironic and applies it to someone who tries to preserve both sides and succeeds with neither. The sting lies in that gap between a comfortable promise and what actually happens. It can tease an attempt to avoid a difficult choice, rather than praise a successful compromise.
entries.meaning_odia: ମିତ ବି ରହିବ, ମାଣିକ ବି ରହିବ—ଶୁଣିଲେ ଲାଗେ କିଛି ହରାଇବାକୁ ପଡ଼ିବ ନାହିଁ। ହେଲେ ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ଅର୍ଥରେ ଦୁଇ ପଟକୁ ରଖିବାକୁ ଯାଇ ଶେଷରେ କୌଣସି ପଟକୁ ରଖି ହୁଏ ନାହିଁ। ସବୁ ଠିକ୍ ରହିବ ବୋଲି କହିବା ଓ ପ୍ରକୃତରେ ସମ୍ଭାଳିବା ଭିତରର ଫରକଟି ଏଠି ଧରାପଡ଼େ। କଠିନ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତିକୁ ଏଡ଼ାଇବାର ଚେଷ୍ଟା ଦେଖି କେହି ଏହାକୁ ଟିକେ ଟାହି କରି କହିପାରନ୍ତି।
entries.english_summary: An ironic promise to preserve both sides ends with neither secured.
entries.odia_summary: ଦୁଇ ପଟ ରଖିବାର ଆଶ୍ୱାସନ ଶେଷରେ ଦୁଇ ପଟ ହରାଇବାର ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ହୁଏ।
entries.usage_example: A person promises to attend two gatherings at the same time, keeps postponing a decision and misses both; a friend uses the saying. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: The ironic, unsuccessful outcome follows the explicit dictionary gloss, not an inferred win-win moral. Friend/jewel are a literal reading, not identified historical characters or objects. Source-listed parallels are not claimed as independently verified variants.

entries.title: Does long hair make a yogi?
entries.odia: ନଖ ବାଳ ରଖି ଭାଲୁଏ ଏ କେତେ ଯୋଗୀ ହେଲେଣି?
entries.literal_meaning: By keeping their nails and hair, how many bears have become yogis?
entries.explanation: The question makes an outward resemblance look absurd. A bear has hair and claws, but those features do not make it a yogi. The joke challenges the idea that an appearance can stand in for the practice it is supposed to signify. Applied elsewhere, it can puncture showy signs of expertise without the patient work behind them; that wider application is an editorial reading of the image.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭାଲୁର ବାଳ ଓ ନଖ ଅଛି ବୋଲି ସେ କଣ ଯୋଗୀ ହୋଇଗଲା? ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ହସାଏ, ପୁଣି ବାହାର ଚେହେରା ଦେଖି ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି କରିବାକୁ ଅଟକାଏ। ଯେଉଁ ସାଧନାର ପରିଚୟ ବୋଲି କୌଣସି ଚିହ୍ନକୁ ଧରାଯାଏ, କେବଳ ସେହି ଚିହ୍ନ ରଖିଲେ ସାଧନା ହୋଇଯାଏ ନାହିଁ। ଦକ୍ଷତାର ଦେଖାଣି ଅଛି, ହେଲେ ତାହା ପଛରେ ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ନାହିଁ—ଏପରି ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଏହି ଛବି ସହ ତୁଳନା କରାଯାଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: Outward resemblance cannot replace the practice it appears to represent.
entries.odia_summary: ବାହାର ଚିହ୍ନ ରଖିଲେ ତାହା ପଛର ସାଧନା ଆସିଯାଏ ନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Someone buys an impressive set of painting tools but never practises; a friend jokes that owning the outward signs does not yet make an artist. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: The source places the question under letting nails and hair grow and explicitly labels it Dhaga. The broader expertise example is an original analogy, not a documented customary use. Do not treat hair, dress or religious affiliation as evidence of dishonesty, or attribute the saying to a particular yogic tradition.

entries.odia: ରଖେ ହରି ମାରେ କିଏ? ମାରେ ହରି ରଖେ କିଏ?
entries.title: Who can overrule Hari?
entries.literal_meaning: If Hari protects, who can kill? If Hari kills, who can protect?
entries.explanation: The mirrored questions express faith in divine authority over life and death. Repeating the same verbs in reverse makes the speaker’s conviction sound absolute. It may voice surrender when human control feels limited; that use is an editorial reading, not a documented origin.
entries.meaning_odia: ହରି ରଖିଲେ କିଏ ମାରିବ, ହରି ମାରିଲେ କିଏ ରଖିବ? ଦୁଇ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ସେହି ଶବ୍ଦର ସ୍ଥାନ ବଦଳି ଭକ୍ତିର ବିଶ୍ୱାସକୁ ଦୃଢ଼ କରେ। ନିଜ ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରଣର ସୀମା ଅନୁଭବ କରୁଥିବା ବକ୍ତାଙ୍କ ସମର୍ପଣ ଭାବେ ଏହାକୁ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: The mirrored questions express faith in divine authority over life and death.
entries.odia_summary: ହରି ରଖିଲେ କିଏ ମାରିବ, ହରି ମାରିଲେ କିଏ ରଖିବ? ଦୁଇ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ସେହି ଶବ୍ଦର ସ୍ଥାନ ବଦଳି ଭକ୍ତିର ବିଶ୍ୱାସକୁ ଦୃଢ଼ କରେ।

entries.title: A tiger among tulsi plants
entries.literal_meaning: A tiger in a tulsi garden.
entries.explanation: The source imagines a cat claiming a tiger’s stature in a small setting. It mocks someone displaying modest knowledge as great authority where others cannot readily challenge it. The target is inflated self-importance, not the worth of people with less schooling.
entries.meaning_odia: ଛୋଟ ତୁଳସୀ ବଣରେ ବିରାଡ଼ି ନିଜକୁ ବାଘ ଭାବୁଛି—ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାର ଛବି ଏହି। ଅଳ୍ପ ଜାଣି ମଧ୍ୟ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବା ଲୋକ ନଥିବା ଜାଗାରେ ବଡ଼ ପଣ୍ଡିତ ସାଜିବାକୁ ଏହା ଟାହି କରେ। କମ୍ ପାଠ ପଢ଼ିଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ତୁଚ୍ଛ କରିବା ଏହି ପାଠର ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: Such a grand household, such stinginess
entries.literal_meaning: Pumpkin vine! A son of a grand household, so miserly!
entries.explanation: The rhyme of ଡ଼ଙ୍କ and ରଙ୍କ gives the complaint a teasing snap. A grand household suggests resources, yet its son behaves as though even a small contribution is too much. The joke exposes that mismatch between the family’s impressive image and the person’s stinginess. Here the dictionary places ରଙ୍କ under “miserly”, not “poor”; lack of generosity and lack of money must not be confused.
entries.meaning_odia: କଖାରୁଡ଼ଙ୍କ ସହ ରଙ୍କର ମିଳ ଅଭିଯୋଗଟିକୁ ଟାହିର ସ୍ୱର ଦିଏ। ବଡ଼ଘରର ପୁଅ ବୋଲି ନାମ ଅଛି, ଅଥଚ ସାମାନ୍ୟ କିଛି ଦେବାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ହାତ ଖୋଲୁନାହିଁ—ହସଟି ଏହି ଅମେଳରେ। ଘରର ବଡ଼ ନାମ ଓ ମଣିଷର ଛୋଟ ବ୍ୟବହାରକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖି କଥାଟି କହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଏଠି ରଙ୍କର ଅଭିଧାନ ଅର୍ଥ କୃପଣ; ଟଙ୍କାର ଅଭାବକୁ କୃପଣତା ସହ ମିଶାଇବା ଠିକ୍ ହେବ ନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A grand family name makes a small act of stinginess look all the more ridiculous.
entries.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ଘରର ନାମ ଓ ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚରେ କୃପଣତା—ଏହି ଅମେଳକୁ କଥାଟି ଟାହି କରେ।
entries.usage_example: At a shared picnic, someone boasts about the size of his family home but refuses to contribute even a few cups. A friend says, “କଖାରୁଡ଼ଙ୍କ ! ବଡ଼ଘରପୁଅ ଏଡ଼ିକି ରଙ୍କ !” The teasing targets his conduct, not someone unable to afford a contribution. (Original imagined example.)
entries.cultural_context: Source sense1 supports stinginess. The household label is the speaker’s taunt, not a rule about class.

entries.title: Whose choice is the meal?
entries.literal_meaning: Does the needy person’s wish decide the meal?
entries.explanation: Wanting a meal and being able to choose it are different things. The source explains that someone dependent on another’s food receives what the giver wishes to provide. The question can expose how little say the recipient has. Its tone matters: it may describe that constraint sympathetically, or dismiss the person’s wishes. This reading draws attention to limited choice without endorsing that dismissal.
entries.meaning_odia: ଭୋକ ଲାଗିବା ଓ ନିଜ ଇଚ୍ଛାର ଖାଦ୍ୟ ବାଛିପାରିବା ଏକା କଥା ନୁହେଁ। ଅନ୍ୟର ଦାନ ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କଲେ ଦାତା ଯାହା ଦେବେ, ସେତିକି ହିଁ ମିଳିପାରେ—ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହାକୁ କହେ। ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ସେହି ଅସହାୟତାକୁ ବୁଝି କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ, ପୁଣି କାହାର ଇଚ୍ଛାକୁ ତୁଚ୍ଛ କରିବାକୁ ବି ବ୍ୟବହାର ହୋଇପାରେ। ଏଠାରେ ଆମେ ବାଛିବାର ସୁଯୋଗ କମିଯିବାକୁ ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ କରୁଛୁ, ଅଭାବରେ ଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ କଥାକୁ ଅଗ୍ରାହ୍ୟ କରିବାକୁ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Depending on another’s provision can leave little room for one’s own choice.
entries.odia_summary: ଅନ୍ୟର ଦାନ ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କଲେ ନିଜ ଇଚ୍ଛାରେ ବାଛିବାର ସୁଯୋଗ କମିଯାଇପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: At a relief kitchen, a family asks whether a different meal is available, but only one prepared dish can be served. Afterwards a recipient says, “ରଙ୍କ ଇଚ୍ଛାରେ କି ଭୋଜନ?” to express having no choice, not to praise the arrangement. (Original imagined example.)
entries.cultural_context: Historical need/dependence language; do not turn it into a demand for unquestioning gratitude.

entries.title: Kartika brings a chill at night
entries.literal_meaning: Kartiki—the cold comes at night.
entries.explanation: The echo between କାର୍ତ୍ତିକି and ରାତିକି makes a seasonal observation easy to remember. The line draws attention to night rather than declaring that the whole day has turned cold. In conversation it can accompany noticing a change in the air. This is a calendar-linked saying, not a forecast for every place or year.
entries.meaning_odia: କାର୍ତ୍ତିକି ସହ ରାତିକିର ମିଳ ଋତୁର କଥାକୁ ମନରେ ରଖିଦିଏ। ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଦିନସାରା ଶୀତର କଥା ନକହି ରାତିର ଥଣ୍ଡାକୁ ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ କରେ। ସନ୍ଧ୍ୟା ପରେ ପବନ ବଦଳିଥିବା ଅନୁଭବ କଲେ ଏହି କଥା ମନେ ପଡ଼ିପାରେ। ସବୁ ଜାଗାରେ ସବୁ ବର୍ଷ ଏକା ପାଗ ହେବ ବୋଲି ଏହାକୁ ଧରିବା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A rhyme links Kartika with the chill felt at night.

entries.title: Breaking rather than bending
entries.literal_meaning: The kaunria stick will break; it will not bend.
entries.explanation: The image makes refusal to yield stark: breaking becomes possible before bending does. Applied to a person, it can sound like admiration for resolve or criticism of costly stubbornness. The words alone do not settle which tone the speaker intends. The object gives that tension a shape without turning every refusal into a virtue.
entries.meaning_odia: କାଠି ନଇଁବା ବଦଳରେ ଭାଙ୍ଗିଯିବ—ଛବିଟି ନଛାଡ଼ିବା ମନୋଭାବକୁ ତୀବ୍ର କରେ। କାହାର ଦୃଢ଼ତା ଦେଖି ପ୍ରଶଂସାରେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ, ପୁଣି କ୍ଷତି ହେଲେ ବି ଜିଦ୍ ନଛାଡ଼ିବାକୁ ଟାହି କରି ବି। ବକ୍ତାଙ୍କ ସ୍ୱର ଓ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିରୁ ଫରକଟି ବୁଝାଯାଏ। ସବୁବେଳେ ନଇଁବା ଖରାପ କିମ୍ବା ନଇଁନଥିବା ଭଲ ବୋଲି ଏହା କହେ ନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: An unbending stick pictures resolve that may become costly stubbornness.
entries.odia_summary: ନଇଁନଥିବା କାଠିର ଛବିରେ ଦୃଢ଼ତା ଓ କ୍ଷତିକାରକ ଜିଦ୍ ଦୁହିଁ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇପାରେ।

entries.cultural_context: Source gives a fibre-stripped plant-stem sense, not an experimentally verified botanical rule. Keep kaunria name without fixing an independently verified species. Dual social readings are editorial.

entries.title: How would the back know the belly’s pain?
entries.literal_meaning: How would the back know the belly’s pain?
entries.explanation: Even two parts of the same body do not occupy the same place. The question gives private suffering a simple image: being near someone is not the same as feeling what they feel. It can ask a listener to be less certain about another person’s troubles. That reading need not mean that understanding or help is impossible.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏକା ଦେହର ପେଟ ଓ ପିଠି ବି ଏକା ଜାଗାରେ ନାହାନ୍ତି। ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ନିଜର କଷ୍ଟକୁ ଅନ୍ୟେ ସହଜରେ ବୁଝିନପାରିବାର ଭାବ ଅଛି। ପାଖରେ ରହିଲେ ବି ଅନ୍ୟ ମଣିଷର ଅନୁଭବକୁ ନିଜର ବୋଲି ଧରିନେବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ। ତଥାପି ଶୁଣିବା, ବୁଝିବାକୁ ଚେଷ୍ଟା କରିବା ବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରିବା ଅସମ୍ଭବ ବୋଲି କଥାଟିକୁ ପଢ଼ିବା ଦରକାର ନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Closeness does not give automatic knowledge of someone else’s suffering.
entries.odia_summary: ପାଖରେ ଥିଲେ ବି ଅନ୍ୟର କଷ୍ଟ ଆପେ ଆପେ ଜଣାପଡ଼େ ନାହିଁ।

entries.title: Whose salt, whose praise?
entries.literal_meaning: Eat someone’s salt; sing that person’s merits.
entries.explanation: Salt stands for livelihood received through service in the dictionary definition. The line links material dependence with praise of the provider. It may express loyalty, or make a sharp comment about praise shaped by dependence; the occasion decides the force. It does not establish that every employee’s praise is dishonest or that support requires silence.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏଠି ଲୁଣ ଖାଇବା କେବଳ ଖାଦ୍ୟର କଥା ନୁହେଁ; ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା କାହା ଅଧୀନରେ ଚାକିରି କରି ଜୀବିକା ଚଳାଇବା। ଯାହାଠାରୁ ଜୀବିକା ମିଳେ ତାହାର ପ୍ରଶଂସା କରିବା ସହ କଥାଟି ଯୋଡ଼େ। କେବେ ଏହା ଆନୁଗତ୍ୟର କଥା, କେବେ ନିର୍ଭରତା ପାଇଁ ହେଉଥିବା ପ୍ରଶଂସାକୁ ଟାହି। ସବୁ କର୍ମଚାରୀଙ୍କ ପ୍ରଶଂସା ମିଛ କିମ୍ବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନେଲେ ଚୁପ୍ ରହିବାକୁ ହେବ ବୋଲି ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: The salt image connects livelihood with loyalty—or praise shaped by dependence.
entries.odia_summary: ଜୀବିକା ଓ ପ୍ରଶଂସାର ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଲୁଣର ଛବି ଧରେ।

entries.title: The cost of speaking, the cost of silence
entries.literal_meaning: If I speak, the family is ashamed; if I do not, the family is being swept away.
entries.explanation: Both choices carry a cost. Speaking exposes something embarrassing; remaining silent allows the damage to grow. The image of a family being swept away makes silence seem less safe than it first appears. The saying voices a dilemma, not a command to conceal wrongdoing for the sake of reputation.
entries.meaning_odia: କହିଲେ ପରିବାରର ଲାଜ, ନକହିଲେ ପରିବାରର କ୍ଷତି—ଦୁଇ ପଟେ ଚିନ୍ତା। ଚୁପ୍ ରହିଲେ ମାନ ରହିଯିବ ବୋଲି ଲାଗିପାରେ, ହେଲେ ଭିତରର ଅସୁବିଧା ବଢ଼ୁଥାଏ। କୁଳ ଭାସିଯିବାର ଛବି ସେହି ବିପଦକୁ ତୀବ୍ର କରେ। ଏହା ଦ୍ୱିଧାର କଥା; ପରିବାରର ନାମ ପାଇଁ ଭୁଲ ବା ଅନ୍ୟାୟ ଲୁଚାଇବାର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Protecting a family’s reputation by silence may allow its troubles to deepen.

entries.title: A mountain for a mouse
entries.literal_meaning: Dig a mountain; kill a mouse.
entries.explanation: The work is mountain-sized, but the result is only a mouse. That sudden reduction supplies the joke. Praharaj’s dictionary applies the saying to much effort yielding little or a negligible result. The expanded reading here also notices the fuss or grand promises surrounding such an outcome. It is the mismatch of scale that matters, rather than a rule that small results are always worthless.
entries.meaning_odia: ପାହାଡ଼ ଖୋଳିବା ଭଳି ବଡ଼ କାମର ଶେଷରେ ମିଳିଲା ମୂଷାଟିଏ। ବଡ଼ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତିରୁ ଏତେ ଛୋଟ ଫଳ—ଏହି ଅମେଳଟି ହସାଏ। ଅନେକ ହଇଚଇ, ପରିଶ୍ରମ ବା ବଡ଼ କଥା ପରେ ଫଳ ଅତି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ହେଲେ ଏହି ଛବି ମନକୁ ଆସିପାରେ। ଛୋଟ ଫଳର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ନୁହେଁ; ଯେତେ ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର ହେଲା, ତାହା ସହ ଫଳ ମେଳ ଖାଉନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Grand effort ends in a disproportionately small result.
entries.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ଆୟୋଜନର ଫଳ ଅତି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ହେବାର ଛବି।
entries.usage_example: After several elaborate meetings, a group changes only the colour of a notice; someone quietly compares the result to a mouse. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary explicitly labels this a proverb and supplies the effort-versus-result gloss. The joke about scale and the imagined meeting are editorial expansions. No originating incident or borrowing history is established.

entries.title: When unclear words become scripture
entries.literal_meaning: When Brahma speaks incoherently, it is the Veda.
entries.explanation: The saying makes the speaker’s standing outweigh the clarity of the words. Even incoherent speech is received as scripture when it comes from Brahma. The dictionary places this example under the sense “to speak incoherently” and labels it a Dhaga. The further reading offered here is satirical: a statement can acquire authority merely because of who says it. That is an editorial interpretation of the contrast, not a doctrinal account of the Vedas.
entries.meaning_odia: ବ୍ରହ୍ମା ବିଳିବିଳେଇଲେ ବି ତାହା ବେଦ। କଥା କେତେ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ, ତାହାଠାରୁ କିଏ କହୁଛି ସେ କଥା ବଡ଼ ହୋଇଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଅନର୍ଥକ ବାକ୍ୟ କହିବା ଅର୍ଥରେ ଏହି ଢଗଟି ଉଦାହରଣ ହୋଇଛି। ଏଠାରେ ଆମର ପାଠ ହେଉଛି ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦାର ଜୋର ଉପରେ ଏକ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ—ବଡ଼ ଲୋକ କହିଛନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଅସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କଥାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅଭ୍ରାନ୍ତ ଧରିନେବା।
entries.english_summary: A speaker’s prestige can make unclear words seem authoritative.
entries.odia_summary: କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦାରେ ଅସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କଥା ବି ପ୍ରମାଣ ହୋଇଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: A vague remark by a famous speaker is repeated as a firm rule, although nobody can explain what was meant. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: Brahma and the Veda remain the source’s cultural anchors. The dictionary supports the lexical sense and identifies the example as Dhaga; the prestige-over-clarity interpretation is Project Odisha’s reading. No originating scripture passage or religious teaching is asserted, and the saying is not attributed to Brahma as its author.

entries.title: Enough at home, still eager for a bite
entries.literal_meaning: A son from a well-fed household, yet eager for food!
entries.explanation: The teasing surprise lies in the mismatch: food is plentiful at home, yet the child lights up at the sight of something to eat. Here ରଙ୍କ carries eagerness for food, rather than the stinginess it carries in another saying on the same dictionary page. Spoken warmly, the line can notice the temptation of a fresh treat even after a meal; spoken sharply, it can embarrass the child. The joke is about that moment, not proof of a child’s character or whether they are hungry.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘରେ ଖାଇବାର ଅଭାବ ନାହିଁ, ତଥାପି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଦେଖି ପିଲାର ଆଗ୍ରହ ବଢ଼ିଯାଉଛି—ଏହି ଫରକରେ କଥାଟିର ଥଟ୍ଟା। ଏଠି ରଙ୍କ କହିଲେ କଞ୍ଜୁସ ନୁହେଁ, ଖାଇବା ପାଇଁ ଲାଳାୟିତ ହେବାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ। ଖାଇସାରିଥିଲେ ବି ନୂଆ ଜଳଖିଆ ଦେଖି ମନ ବଳିବା ବେଳେ ଆଦରରେ ଏହି କଥା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ; କଟୁ ସ୍ୱରରେ କହିଲେ ସେଇ କଥା ପିଲାକୁ ଲଜ୍ଜିତ କରିପାରେ। ଏକ ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତର ଆଗ୍ରହ ଦେଖି ପିଲାର ସ୍ୱଭାବ କିମ୍ବା ତାକୁ ଭୋକ ଲାଗିଛି କି ନାହିଁ, ତାହାର ରାୟ ଦେବା ଏହି ଥଟ୍ଟାର କାମ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A teasing contrast between having enough food at home and eagerly wanting another treat.
entries.odia_summary: ଘରେ ଖାଇବା ଥାଇ ବି ଆଉ ଏକ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଆଗ୍ରହ ଦେଖାଇବାକୁ ନେଇ ଥଟ୍ଟା।
entries.usage_example: After lunch, a child eagerly asks what is in a newly opened snack box. An aunt smiles and says, “ଖାଇଲାଘରର ପୁଅ ରଙ୍କ!” She then asks whether the child would like a little now or later. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: The source explicitly describes children in households where food is not lacking. The affectionate scene and discussion of tone are editorial, not observed testimony. Preserve the source’s son wording without making hunger or eagerness a gendered or innate trait. Distinct from 190’s stinginess and 191’s restricted choice.

entries.title: The claim of knowing three births
entries.literal_meaning: A poor person knows the story of three births.
entries.explanation: The line sounds like a claim to remarkable knowledge, but the dictionary supplies a harsh explanation. It attributes present poverty to not giving charity in a previous birth, then predicts poverty in the next birth from not giving in the present one. The three births connect alleged past conduct, present hardship and a predicted future; the gloss does not say that the person was poor in the previous birth. This is a recorded belief, not evidence explaining anyone’s poverty. Read critically, the saying shows how a neat turn of speech can make blame sound like settled knowledge.
entries.meaning_odia: ତିନି ଜନ୍ମର କଥା ଜାଣିବା ଶୁଣିଲେ ଅସାଧାରଣ ଜ୍ଞାନର କଥା ମନେ ହୁଏ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ଅଛି ଏକ କଠୋର ବିଶ୍ୱାସ। ସେହି ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ପୂର୍ବ ଜନ୍ମରେ ଦାନ ନକରିବାକୁ ଏ ଜନ୍ମର ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟର କାରଣ କହେ, ଆଉ ଏ ଜନ୍ମରେ ଦାନ ନକରିବାରୁ ପର ଜନ୍ମରେ ବି ଦରିଦ୍ର ହେବ ବୋଲି କଳ୍ପନା କରେ। ପୂର୍ବ ଜନ୍ମରେ ସେ ଦରିଦ୍ର ଥିଲା ବୋଲି ସ୍ରୋତ କହେ ନାହିଁ। ଏହା ଲିପିବଦ୍ଧ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ, କାହାର ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟର ପ୍ରମାଣିତ କାରଣ ନୁହେଁ। କଥାଟିକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରି ପଢ଼ିଲେ ଦେଖାଯାଏ, ଏକ ଚତୁର ଉକ୍ତି କିପରି ଅଭାବରେ ଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଦୋଷ ଲଦି ତାହାକୁ ଜ୍ଞାନ ପରି ଶୁଣାଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: The recorded belief blames present poverty on past-life non-giving and predicts future poverty from non-giving now; this explanation questions that claim.
entries.odia_summary: ପୂର୍ବ ଜନ୍ମର ଦାନ ନକରିବା ସହ ଏବର ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟକୁ, ଏବର ଦାନ ନକରିବା ସହ ପର ଜନ୍ମର ଦାରିଦ୍ର୍ୟକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ୁଥିବା ବିଶ୍ୱାସକୁ ଏଠି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରାଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: In a reading group, someone quotes “ରଙ୍କ ତିନି ଜନମ କଥା ଜାଣେ” and reads the dictionary gloss aloud. Another reader asks, “How could we know someone’s past birth—and why should their present hardship be taken as evidence against them?” (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: Critical historical documentation, not a recommended reproach to use against poor people. The source gives a karma/charity explanation explicitly; no observed past-life fact, empirical cause of poverty, general Odia belief or present community endorsement is established. The critical reading is Project Odisha’s editorial response.

entries.title: Eat the gruel or shoo the flies?
entries.literal_meaning: Eat the gruel, or shoo the flies?
entries.explanation: A meal is ready, but the flies will not leave it alone. The question catches the frustration of two necessary tasks demanding attention at once: attending to one interrupts the other. It gives that predicament a small, comic scene rather than blaming someone for not doing everything at the same time. The dictionary explicitly applies the saying to two unavoidable tasks arising together.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜାଉ ଖାଇବାକୁ ବସିଛି, ହେଲେ ମାଛି ଘଉଡ଼ାଇବାରୁ ଫୁରୁସତ୍ ନାହିଁ। ଖାଇବା ବି ଦରକାର, ମାଛି ହଟାଇବା ବି ଦରକାର; ଗୋଟିକରେ ମନ ଦେଲେ ଅନ୍ୟଟି ବାଧା ଦେଉଛି। ଏକା ସମୟରେ ଦୁଇଟି ଜରୁରୀ କାମ ପଡ଼ିଲେ କାହାକୁ ଆଗ କରିବା, ସେହି ଅଡ଼ୁଆକୁ ଏହି ଛୋଟ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ହସ ସହିତ କହେ। ଅଭିଧାନର ଟୀକାରେ ମଧ୍ୟ ଏକା ସମୟର ଦୁଇଟି ଅନିବାର୍ଯ୍ୟ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଏହାର ବ୍ୟବହାର ଦିଆଯାଇଛି।
entries.english_summary: Two necessary tasks can compete for the same moment of attention.
entries.odia_summary: ଏକା ବେଳେ ଦୁଇଟି ଜରୁରୀ କାମ ପଡ଼ିଲେ କାହାକୁ ଆଗ କରିବା?
entries.usage_example: At a small event, the person serving lunch is also asked to check arriving guests against a list. They use the question with a laugh and ask another volunteer to take one task. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: Jau is a grain gruel. The printed dictionary pictures flies, not fish; the online Wiktionary transcription drops the final vowel sign in that word. The meal scene and application above expand the dictionary’s stated two-task gloss. No particular household, occupational custom or originating incident is established.

entries.odia: ଏଡ଼େ ମଲାଠେଇଁ ଦିଓଳି ବି ତତଲା ଖିଆ!
entries.title: Such poverty, yet hot food twice a day
entries.literal_meaning: In such dire poverty, yet eating hot food at both meals!
entries.explanation: The dictionary places this saying under extreme poverty. The line then sets that condition beside eating hot food at both meals: its surprise lies in the contrast. It can be read as a teasing challenge to a description of hardship, though the dictionary does not supply a separate use gloss. Cooking again costs fuel and work; a literary passage about one cooked-rice meal and one meal of pakhala helps explain the image. That context does not make hot food a reliable measure of anyone’s means.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏଠାରେ ‘ମଲା’ର ଅର୍ଥ ଅତି ଗରିବ ଅବସ୍ଥା। ଢଗଟି ସେହି ଦୁରବସ୍ଥା ସହ ଦିଓଳି ତତଲା ଖାଇବାକୁ ମୁହାଁମୁହିଁ କରେ। ଦୁଇ ଓଳି ତତଲା ଖାଦ୍ୟର କଥା ଶୁଣି ଅଭାବର ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନାକୁ କଥକ ଥଟ୍ଟା କରୁଥିବା ପରି ଲାଗେ। ଏହି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ ପାଠଟି ଶବ୍ଦର ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ରରୁ କରାଯାଇଛି; ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହାର ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ଅଲଗା କରି ବୁଝାଇନାହିଁ। କାହାର ଗରିବୀ ସତ କି ମିଛ, ଖାଦ୍ୟର ଉଷ୍ଣତା ଦେଖି ତାହା ସ୍ଥିର କରିହେବ ନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A contrast between described hardship and hot food at both meals; its teasing application remains an editorial reading.
entries.odia_summary: ଦୁରବସ୍ଥାର କଥା ସହ ଦିଓଳି ତତଲା ଖାଇବାର ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ର।
entries.usage_example: During an imagined discussion of household expenses, one person complains that nothing is affordable. A companion sees the freshly cooked evening meal and quips, “ଏଡ଼େ ମଲାଠେଇଁ ଦିଓଳି ବି ତତଲା ଖିଆ!” The reply comes back: “A hot meal does not tell you what we have had to go without.” (Original imagined use, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: Recorded as ଢଗ under ମଲା, noun2, printed Praharaj page6322. Preserve the social sting rather than recasting it as a universal lesson about extravagance. The source establishes wording and the poverty sense; the teasing application is editorial. The separate Rudrakshya passage clarifies meal/fuel language but neither quotes nor explains this proverb. No first-use, popularity or community-wide endorsement is claimed.

entries.title: An ant guarding the jaggery
entries.literal_meaning: An ant as the guard of the jaggery store.
entries.explanation: The supposed guard has an appetite for exactly what it must protect. The dictionary uses this mismatch for entrusting something to its would-be consumer: the arrangement itself puts the goods at risk. In conversation, the image can make a questionable appointment look absurd before anyone has to explain it at length. It questions a particular conflict between duty and temptation, rather than declaring that a whole kind of person is dishonest.

entries.title: The ant grows wings

entries.explanation: The image sounds like a new freedom, but the dictionary turns it into a sign of approaching ruin or death. That reversal gives the expression its ominous force: what looks like an advance is read as a warning. A speaker may use it when another person becomes recklessly confident, though that particular application is an editorial example rather than a separate source gloss. The image carries an old belief; it is not a biological account of winged ants or a prediction that someone must come to harm.

entries.title: An elephant passes, an ant is stopped
entries.literal_meaning: An elephant passes through, but there is no way for an ant.
entries.explanation: The impossible difference in scale makes the complaint funny: a passage admits an elephant but somehow cannot admit an ant. The dictionary explains this as overlooking large matters while keeping watch over small ones. The target is misplaced scrutiny, not careful attention itself. In an argument, the image can turn the question back on the person enforcing a tiny rule: what larger thing have they allowed to pass?
entries.meaning_odia: ହାତୀ ଗଳିଯାଉଛି, ଅଥଚ ପିମ୍ପୁଡ଼ି ପାଇଁ ବାଟ ନାହିଁ—ଆକାରର ଏହି ଅସମ୍ଭବ ଫରକରେ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ। ଅଭିଧାନ ବଡ଼ ବଡ଼ କଥାରେ ଦୃଷ୍ଟି ନରଖି ଛୋଟ ଛୋଟ ବିଷୟକୁ ଜଗିବା କଥା କହିଛି। ଖୁଟିନାଟି ଦେଖିବା ନିଜେ ଭୁଲ ନୁହେଁ; ବଡ଼ ତ୍ରୁଟି ଛାଡ଼ି କେବଳ ଛୋଟ କଥାରେ ଅଟକିବାକୁ ଏହା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ। କେହି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ନିୟମ ଧରି ବସିଲେ, ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ତାଙ୍କୁ ବଡ଼ ଅବହେଳାଟି ଦେଖାଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: Large lapses pass unnoticed while tiny matters face strict scrutiny.
entries.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ଅବହେଳା ଛାଡ଼ି ଛୋଟ କଥାକୁ କଠୋର ଭାବେ ଜଗିବା।
entries.usage_example: A committee approves a large unexplained expense, then spends half an hour disputing a tiny stationery claim. A member says, “ହାତୀ ଗଳି ଯାଉଛି ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ଗଳିବାକୁ ବାଟ ନାହିଁ,” and asks to examine the larger bill first. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)

entries.title: An ant climbing the lampstand
entries.literal_meaning: Being an ant and climbing onto the lampstand.
entries.explanation: The dictionary applies this small creature and high perch to a “small” person intervening in “big” matters. The wording does more than describe scale: it can dismiss someone’s right to take part by placing them below the subject under discussion. That ranking belongs to the source’s social judgment, not a fact about anyone’s worth or ability. Read critically, the analogy lets us hear how a vivid image can keep a person out of a conversation instead of answering what they said.
entries.meaning_odia: ଛୋଟ ପିମ୍ପୁଡ଼ି ଓ ଉଚ୍ଚ ଦୀପରୁଖାର ଛବିକୁ ଅଭିଧାନ ‘ଛୋଟ ଲୋକ’ ହୋଇ ‘ବଡ଼ କଥା’ରେ ହସ୍ତକ୍ଷେପ କରିବା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ିଛି। ଏହା କେବଳ ଆକାରର ତୁଳନା ନୁହେଁ; କାହାକୁ ତୁଚ୍ଛ କରି ତାଙ୍କ କଥା କହିବାର ଅଧିକାରକୁ ଅସ୍ୱୀକାର କରିବାର ସ୍ୱର ମଧ୍ୟ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି। ସେହି ଉଚ୍ଚନୀଚ ବିଚାର ସ୍ରୋତର ପ୍ରୟୋଗର ଅଂଶ, କାହାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ବା ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ। ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରି ପଢ଼ିଲେ ଦେଖାଯାଏ, ଉତ୍ତର ଦେବା ବଦଳରେ ଏକ ଚିତ୍ର କିପରି ଲୋକଟିକୁ ଆଲୋଚନାରୁ ବାହାରେ ରଖିପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: A historical analogy can dismiss a supposedly insignificant person’s participation in larger matters.
entries.odia_summary: କାହାକୁ ତୁଚ୍ଛ ଭାବି ବଡ଼ କଥାରେ ତାଙ୍କ ଅଂଶଗ୍ରହଣକୁ ଖାରଜ କରିବାର ଏକ ପୁରୁଣା ଉପମା।
entries.usage_example: At a residents’ meeting, a newcomer questions an expense. Someone dismisses the question with “ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ହୋଇ ଦୀପରୁଖାରେ ଚଢ଼ିବା.” Another resident replies that the question should be answered, whoever asked it. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)

entries.literal_meaning: If a mouthful falls from an elephant’s mouth, an ant has food for a hundred years.
entries.explanation: The joke makes the same scrap almost nothing to one creature and an enormous provision to another. The dictionary extends the contrast to an elephant-like person leaving a small amount that can sustain many ant-like lives. The hundred years is the saying’s extravagant measure of scale, not a feeding calculation. The comparison can make an overlooked remainder suddenly look substantial.

entries.english_summary: A tiny remainder to one can be a large provision to another.

entries.literal_meaning: When an elephant urinates, the ants swim.
entries.explanation: The blunt bodily image makes scale impossible to miss: an ordinary discharge for the elephant becomes a flood for the ants. The dictionary’s gloss goes further than the heading’s swimming and says the smaller creatures drown. The contrast can picture how a large actor’s small action overwhelms those with much less room to absorb it; that application is editorial, rather than a separate use supplied by the dictionary.
entries.meaning_odia: ହାତୀ ମୁତିଦେବା ପରି ସାଧାରଣ କାମ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ପାଇଁ ପହଁରିବାର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି କରିଦିଏ। ବଡ଼ ଓ ସାନର ମାପକୁ ଏହି ଖୋଲା ଦେହଜ ଚିତ୍ର ତୀବ୍ର କରେ। ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ବୁଡ଼ିଯିବା କଥା ଅଛି। ବଡ଼ ପକ୍ଷର ଅଳ୍ପ କାମର ପ୍ରଭାବ ସାନ ପକ୍ଷ ପାଇଁ କେତେ ଭାରି ହୋଇପାରେ—ଏପରି ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ଚିତ୍ରଟିର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠ; ଉତ୍ସରେ ଅଲଗା ସାମାଜିକ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: An ordinary act at one scale can overwhelm life at another.

entries.literal_meaning: The analogy of ants eating up the jaggery store.
entries.explanation: The sweet store is something the ants will keep returning to. The dictionary applies the image to work that must always be guarded carefully against an enemy. Its emphasis is continuing exposure, rather than a single finished loss. Unlike putting an ant in charge of the store, this analogy does not appoint the eater as guardian.

entries.english_summary: The source applies the sweet-store image to work needing continuing protection.
entries.odia_summary: ଶତ୍ରୁଠାରୁ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟକୁ ସବୁବେଳେ ସାବଧାନରେ ରକ୍ଷା କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର।

entries.explanation: This is a visual comparison rather than a rebuke. The dictionary describes a place where many people gather and compares their movement to a line of ants. entries.literal_meaning: The analogy of ants being mad for jaggery.
entries.explanation: The ants’ pull towards sweetness supplies a picture of someone’s marked eagerness or greed. The dictionary allows both interest and greed, so the comparison need not carry the same accusation on every occasion. A playful comment about enthusiasm can turn sharp when the attraction is self-serving. The object of desire need not be food.
entries.meaning_odia: ଗୁଡ଼ ପ୍ରତି ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିର ଆକର୍ଷଣକୁ ଧରି ଜଣକର ବିଶେଷ ଆଗ୍ରହ କିମ୍ବା ଲୋଭ ବୁଝାଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଦୁଇଟି ଅର୍ଥର ସୁଯୋଗ ରଖିଛି। ତେଣୁ ପ୍ରତିଥର ଏହାକୁ କଠୋର ଲୋଭର ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିଦେଲେ କଥାର ସ୍ୱର ବଦଳିଯିବ। ଅବସର ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହା ଆଗ୍ରହକୁ ନେଇ ହାଲୁକା ଥଟ୍ଟା ହୋଇପାରେ, କିମ୍ବା ଲାଭ ପାଇଁ ବ୍ୟାକୁଳତାକୁ ବିନ୍ଧିପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: An attraction can be playful eagerness or pointedly described greed.
entries.odia_summary: ବିଶେଷ ଆଗ୍ରହ ବା ଲୋଭକୁ ଗୁଡ଼ ପ୍ରତି ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିର ଆକର୍ଷଣ ସହ ତୁଳନା।
